job_description: Application Closing Date 15th September 2026 Context of Role The International Planned Parenthood Federation (IPPF) is a global sexual and reproductive health (SRH) service provider and one of the leading advocates for universal access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for all. IPPF is a worldwide movement of 120 national organizations, referred to as Member Associations, working with and for communities and individuals. These member associations are the leading civil society providers of contraception in 89 of 120 countries. And in 64 of those 89 countries, IPPF is the only largescale international provider. Collectively, member associations delivered more than 1 billion cumulative services between 2016 and 2022. Headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, the overarching goal of IPPF Africa Region (IPPFAR) is to increase access to SRHR services to the most vulnerable youth, men, and women in sub-Saharan Africa. To reach this goal, IPPFAR works with local civil-society organizations, governments, the African Union (AU), regional economic commissions (RECs), the United Nations, among others, to expand political and financial commitments to SRHR in Africa. IPPFAR tackles the continent’s growing SRH challenges through a network of Member Associations (MAs), strategic partners and volunteers in 42 countries. For more information, please read our 20242 profile (in English and French) here. Project Overview The International Planned Parenthood Federation Africa Region (IPPFAR), in collaboration with AFJCI and CRR lead the delivery of a new project called Justice for Survivors (J4S) . Funded by the Agence Francaise de Développement (AFD), J4S’s overarching goal is to strengthen the capacity of feminist movements to address gender-based violence (GBV) through sub-grants to feminist organizations, with a focus on reaching small, often unregistered, feminist organizations. The project is implemented across 4 countries: Cote d’Ivoire, Guinea, Tanzania and Kenya. Championing an ecological-based model that integrates the use of multi-disciplinary gender transformative approaches and direct sub-granting, J4S will provide longer-term mentorship and support to feminist organizations in their overall development, by designing specific trainings tailored to their needs and helping them identify additional sources of funding. Reinforce the resilience and diversity of feminist civil society organizations (CSOs) through access to sustainable, flexible and adapted financing for small and/or informal and/or structurally excluded groups. About Busara Founded in 2014, Busara is a leading behavioral science and research organization dedicated to improving development outcomes by understanding and influencing human behavior. Busara Uganda partners with governments, development agencies, foundations, research institutions, NGOs, and private sector organizations to design solutions that are evidence-based, contextually grounded, and capable of achieving impact at scale. Over the past decade, Busara has grown into one of the largest behavioral science organizations globally, combining global expertise with deep local knowledge and implementation experience. Busara's mission is to advance and apply behavioral science to help people and organizations make better decisions. The organization's distinctive value lies in its ability to connect rigorous research with practical implementation. Busara combines behavioral science, adult learning principles, human-centered design, systems thinking, and applied research methods to identify the behavioral, social, and institutional factors that influence program outcomes. This enables partners to move beyond understanding what challenges exist to understanding why they exist and how to address them sustainably. Busara supports partners across the full program lifecycle, including assessments, behavioral diagnostics, curriculum development, training and capacity strengthening, program design, monitoring and evaluation, adoption measurement, and knowledge generation. The Mastercard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Strategy aims to enable 7 million young women and men across Kenya to access dignified and fulfilling work. Through partnerships with financial institutions, training providers, enterprise support organizations, and other ecosystem actors, the initiative supports programs designed to expand employment opportunities and strengthen pathways to sustainable livelihoods for youth. Over its implementation, the scale and diversity of supported programs have grown substantially across sectors and geographies. As the strategy has matured, the Foundation’s learning priorities have shifted to place greater emphasis on understanding the nature and durability of the outcomes these programs generate. The central evidence question has shifted from assessing how many young people are reached to examining whether they can access and sustain dignified and fulfilling work as a result of these interventions. In this context, the Foundation wants to understand several interrelated dimensions of program outcomes. These include the sustainability of employment and livelihood outcomes over time, differences in outcomes across youth segments, and the extent to which interventions contribute to broader institutional and ecosystem changes. Busara is partnering with Mastercard Foundation as its Impact Partner Organization (IPO) in Kenya to conduct Program Outcomes Assessments (POA) and Strategic Reviews across Foundation-supported programs under the Young Africa Works Strategy. These assessments and reviews combine quantitative and qualitative inquiry structured around four core POA question areas, including Reach and Access, Progression to Dignified and Fulfilling Work, Improvements in Quality of Life, and Systems and Institutional Contribution, alongside program-specific objectives for each Implementing Partner reviewed. Busara is seeking the services of a Psychosocial Support Officer on a short-term basis to support work across the Young Africa Works Strategy program portfolio, whose programs incorporate gender, inclusion, and safeguarding principles into their interventions for the youth participants. Purpose of the Role The Psychosocial Support Officer will provide specialized professional expertise to safeguard participant well-being throughout the assignment, with a particular focus on identifying, preventing, and responding appropriately to emotional distress or unforeseen crises that may arise during sensitive interviews, surveys, or other field interactions. The role will also support the wider field team in maintaining a safe, ethical, and trauma-informed approach to engagement with participants \n Key Responsibilities Monitor participants for signs of distress, trauma, anxiety, or emotional overwhelm during sessions. Provide immediate emotional support and grounding techniques to help distressed participants regain a sense of safety and stability. Protect participants’ privacy by treating personal stories and mental health information with the highest level of confidentiality. Prepare data collectors to recognize and respond appropriately to emotional stress in themselves and others during the data collection exercise. Facilitate brief daily debriefs to help the team reflect on difficult experiences and support one another after demanding field days. Offer practical guidance and brief supportive counseling to staff members who may feel overwhelmed. Apply established safety protocols and ethical guidelines when engaging on sensitive topics. Escalate any significant safety concerns or incidents to lead researchers immediately. Contribute to adjustments in field plans when new emotional risks emerge during implementation. Prepare an incident report at the end of the data collection exercise, summarizing any incidents identified and the mitigation and referral measures implemented in line with Mastercard Foundation’s Safeguarding policies. Indicative Deliverables A financial proposal/quote itemizing the services to be provided. A brief psychosocial support plan outlining participant safety measures, distress response procedures, and escalation pathways for field activities. Field support notes or debrief summary capturing key wellbeing concerns, actions taken, and any follow-up needs identified during the assignment. An incident and referral log documenting any psychosocial risks, responses provided, and referrals made in line with safeguarding protocols. A concise end-of-assignment report summarizing psychosocial support activities, key observations, mitigation measures, and recommendations for future fieldwork. Required Qualifications and Experience A bachelor’s degree in social sciences, psychology, gender studies, development studies, community development, or a related field from a recognized institution in Kenya; a master’s degree is an added advantage. At least 5–7 years of professional experience in psychosocial support, safeguarding, gender-responsive programming, inclusive fieldwork, or related work in Kenya, preferably in development or humanitarian settings and with vulnerable groups such as refugees, displaced persons, women, youth, or persons with disabilities. Demonstrated experience supporting qualitative fieldwork or participant engagement, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to apply trauma-informed, culturally sensitive, and ethical approaches when working with diverse communities. Working knowledge of safeguarding principles, confidentiality, duty of care, and referral pathways in the Kenya context, including the ability to respond appropriately to sensitive disclosures. Strong communication and facilitation skills in English and Kiswahili; knowledge of additional Kenyan local languages or experience working effectively with interpreters is an advantage. Prior experience contributing to donor-funded evaluations, field research, or program reviews is an added advantage. Position: Growth Lead, Institutional Partnerships (East Africa) Team: Growth Level and grade: L7 Director Position type: Full time; engagement basis set by country of residence Location: East Africa. Nairobi, Kampala, Kigali, Dar es Salaam or Addis Ababa. Reports to: Chief Executive Officer Travel: 40 to 50 percent across the region, occasionally beyond Mandate : The East Africa pipeline from first conversation to signed contract About Us APLYD helps governments, multilateral institutions, development finance institutions and foundations use AI in public systems. Most public-sector AI stops at the pilot. Our work is getting it into everyday service delivery and keeping it running once we leave. Athena Infonomics has done this work for years. In 2026 we set it up as its own company. We cover strategy and readiness, field data and last-mile reach, design and build, evaluation and audit, and scale and production. 440+ engagements 240+ global clients 85+ specialists 7 countries 5 continents The Role You open East Africa for APLYD. The role runs from the first conversation with a ministry, a regional body, a multilateral country office or a development finance institution to a signed contract, and it carries a revenue target. It is a growth role rather than a country profit-and-loss role: delivery is staffed from APLYD's global disciplines, with people in the region when the work requires it. You are the first APLYD hire in the region and you build the team around you, starting with an Associate, Growth (East Africa). You carry a revenue target, and part of your pay is linked to the revenue you originate. Origination credit starts from the first contract you close, the rate increases once you pass target, and there is no cap. In your first year, qualified opportunities you originated that have reached contracting are also credited, because East African institutional cycles often take longer than a financial year. Core Job Responsibilities Represent APLYD in East Africa. For most institutions in the region you will be the first person from the firm they meet, and what you commit to on our behalf, we deliver. Own institutional opportunities from the first conversation to a signed contract: problem definition, scoping, proposal, negotiation, contracting, and a handover that gives the delivery team everything it needs. Decide what we pursue and what we decline. Not every funded opportunity is one we should take. Set the technical expectation before anyone commits to it. Work with senior stakeholders until the problem statement is precise, and hold a credible position on solution architecture, data and AI feasibility, integration constraints, and who owns and operates the system once it is live. Own the proposals: scope, technical approach, timeline, risk, commercial model and budget. At this stage you write the important ones yourself. Read the region for us. Ministries and agencies across several countries, regional bodies, multilaterals, bilateral agencies and philanthropies all decide and budget differently, and the answers change across borders. Keep the pipeline accurate: what is live, what has stalled and what will not happen. Report to the Chief Executive Officer. Hire and lead the Associate, Growth (East Africa), and build the regional team as revenue allows. Qualifications And Competencies Twenty or more years in business development, partnerships or institutional growth across government systems, development organisations or major funders, with most of that time in East Africa. You have taken a new institutional relationship to a signed, funded contract more than once. Current networks across East African governments, regional institutions, multilaterals, bilateral agencies and the philanthropies active in the region. You know how public systems and large development institutions work in the region, and where those answers change across borders. Enough technical depth to hold a credible conversation about AI and data systems, digital public infrastructure, feasibility and architecture. You have been the senior person in the room when an institution decided whether to work with a firm. Based in East Africa, with willingness to travel 40 to 50 percent. Also useful, though we will not screen on it AI, digital transformation, technology-for-development or digital public infrastructure work in Africa. Relationships with county or sub-national governments, and with funders running significant East Africa portfolios. Time in an organisation working at the intersection of evidence, technology and public service delivery on the continent. Additional Requirements This position requires successful completion of a reference check and employment verification. The successful candidate must not be subject to employment restrictions from a former employer, such as a non-compete, that would prevent performance of the responsibilities described. Candidates must declare any current or recent engagement with a government, multilateral or development finance institution that could present a conflict of interest. APLYD’s Work Culture At APLYD, we function in an outcomes-based work environment with flexible hours and a high level of autonomy. Professional development and thought leadership are key elements of our business model: we support our team members’ professional growth through on-the-job training, and we encourage the cultivation of our colleagues’ personal brands through participation in panels, events, publications, and other thought-leadership opportunities. We embrace a transparent, open work environment with meaningful leadership pathways for those with inventive ideas and initiatives. AI Proficiency and Responsible Use Proficiency in the responsible and sophisticated use of AI is a mandatory requirement for all roles, across all levels and functions at APLYD and Athena Infonomics.

job_description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Managing the UN-Women Security and Safety Personnel, the role provides advice and operational oversight, centered on security and safety risk management, industry standards business continuity and crisis management, to ensure organizational programme and mandate delivery. Under the strategic direction of the Director, DFA (D2), the incumbent exercises substantial autonomy in determining professional approaches, developing global frameworks, and directing implementation of security, safety, business continuity and crisis management systems across the organization. The incumbent is accountable for the professional soundness, consistency and effectiveness of these functions organization wide. The incumbent exercises substantial autonomy to: Determine and implement revisions to security, safety, business continuity and crisis management policies, procedures, and standards for UN Women operations worldwide. Make independent determinations on security and safety risk assessments and required measures across all locations. Manage security, safety business continuity and crisis management resources and approve security-related expenditures within approved budget allocations. Direct the work of UN Women Security and Safety personnel to achieve the role objectives. Represent UN Women authoritatively in inter-agency security, safety, business continuity and crisis management forums and with external security stakeholders. The incumbent consults executive leadership on matters with organization wide implications, significant political or reputational sensitivity, major resource implications beyond approved authority levels, or where precedent setting decisions are required, in accordance with UN Women governance arrangements. This vacancy is re-opened to broaden the applicant pool. Candidates who have already applied for this position remain under consideration and are not required to reapply. Key Functions and Accountabilities: Strategic Leadership, Policy Development and Planning: Directs the development, implementation, and continuous refinement UN-Women global security, safety, business continuity, crisis management and occupational health and safety policies, frameworks, standards and guidance, ensuring alignment with UN System requirements and organizational priorities; Provides authoritative interpretation of applicable UN and UN Women policies and ensures their consistent and effective implementation across all organizational locations; Leads preparation of briefing notes, positions papers and strategic inputs for senior management and executive-level decision-making; Monitors and analyzes international developments, emerging threats and evolving risk environments, assessing their implications for UN-Women operations and personnel globally, and determining appropriate professional responses; Ensures effective and timely access by UN-Women managers and Security, Safety, Business Continuity, Crisis Management and Occupational Health and Safety personnel and Policies advisors to prescriptive content such as policy, risk management methodologies, etc. Directs the formulation and oversees execution of the Security and Safety Services annual work plan, ensuring strategic alignment, prioritization and optimal use of resources; Leads security and safety related change management initiatives, promoting innovation, efficiency and strengthened organizational resilience, collaborating strategically with other sections within the Division to drive efficiencies, effectiveness, and automation. job_description: Most finance managers gradually stop doing finance. Their calendars fill with status meetings, task chasing, and people administration while their technical skills go stale. This role takes the opposite path. You will run global finance operations through a team of Senior Accountants while staying close enough to the work to know whether it is actually right. You'll inspect invoices, payments, reconciliations, allocations, and other finance outputs; diagnose the accounting or process failures behind errors; and turn those findings into written coaching that prevents the same mistakes from happening again. When a critical deadline or difficult finance problem demands it, you will still be capable of getting hands-on yourself. Trilogy's Central Finance team operates differently from a traditional accounting organization. We automate routine coordination and continuously look for ways AI and automation can eliminate manual work, leaving finance professionals focused on judgment, quality, and improvement. You'll get exposure to complex global finance operations while retaining the technical edge that many managers lose as they advance. If you want management responsibility without becoming a professional meeting-attendee, this is where your accounting expertise becomes leverage. What You Will Be Doing Here is what your day-to-day work actually looks like in this role: Run day-to-day finance operations through Senior Accountants, continuously prioritizing work based on deadlines, business impact, dependencies, and financial risk. Inspect finance dashboards and completed work to ensure bills, invoices, payments, bank transactions, reconciliations, control accounts, revenue, and spend allocations are accurate and current. Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data) About Mercy Corps Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Program Summary Mercy Corps has been a leader in the drylands of the Horn of Africa for the last decade, supporting households affected by climate change, drought, conflict and other challenges to adapt and thrive in the face of increasing shocks. Our program focuses on strengthening livestock production and markets, enhancing food and water security, addressing gender inequality and youth opportunities, and strengthening devolved governance outcomes to support dryland communities to break from the cycle of humanitarian need and lay the foundations for a more food secure, resilient future. Working across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia, Mercy Corps is implementing the 12-year Regional Livestock Programme (RLP), funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the French Development Agency (AFD). The programme seeks to leverage the significant potential for livestock production and trade within the region by building vibrant regional livestock markets, strengthening livestock production and trade, supporting climate adaptation and enhanced regeneration and governance of rangeland in order to enhance household food security and livelihoods. General Position Summary The Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) Manager for the Regional Livestock Programme will use their in-depth contextual understanding, technical and practical expertise and relationship building skills to lead the collective delivery of a gender transformative program for women’s economic empowerment in the drylands of Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. The WEE manager will lead the design, implementation, and oversight of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy within a Market Systems Development (MSD) framework, ensuring that women, youth, and other marginalized groups benefit equitably from market opportunities. The role will provide technical leadership to integrate gender-transformative and socially inclusive approaches across all program components in targeted corridor, strengthen the quality and effectiveness of WEE interventions, and ensure that program strategies are informed by robust market systems, gender, and social inclusion analyses. Working closely with technical team, partners, and Monitoring and Results Measurement (MRM) teams, the WEE Manager will drive the generation and use of evidence to support adaptive management, learning, and decision-making; oversee the development of gender-responsive Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems; and contribute to knowledge sharing, impact measurement, and external engagement to advance sustainable, inclusive, and scalable program Women Economic Empowerment outcomes. Essential Job Responsibilities VISION AND STRATEGY Set strategic direction and provide leadership for the program’s Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) agenda across target livestock trade corridors, ensuring women and youth are recognized, engaged, and benefit as key economic actors within livestock market systems. Lead the implementation and continuous refinement of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy, ensuring that gender-transformative approaches are effectively embedded across priority interventions and market system activities. Stores In-Charge – Dairy & Beverage Industry Job Title - Stores In-Charge Department - Supply Chain / Stores & Warehouse Industry - Dairy & Beverage Manufacturing Location - Salgaa, Kenya Reporting To- Plant Finance Manager Job Purpose The Stores In-Charge will be responsible for managing the receipt, storage, preservation, issuance, transfer, and reconciliation of inventory , including raw materials, packaging materials, engineering spares, consumables, and other stock. The role will ensure accurate inventory records, strong warehouse controls, food safety, FEFO/FIFO compliance, and timely availability of materials to production and other authorized users. The position is responsible for maintaining high levels of inventory accountability, minimizing stock losses, expiry, damage and obsolescence, and ensuring all physical stock movements are accurately recorded in SAP/ERP on a timely basis. Key Responsibilities 1. Stores & Warehouse Operations Manage day-to-day stores and warehouse operations. Ensure proper receipt, storage, handling, picking and issuance of materials. Maintain proper storage locations, bin discipline and warehouse space utilization. Ensure appropriate segregation of raw materials, packaging materials, spares, consumables, chemicals, quarantine/rejected stock and obsolete materials. Maintain housekeeping and 5S standards . Ensure warehouse access is restricted to authorized personnel. 2. Material Receiving Receive materials against approved Purchase Orders and delivery documentation. Verify quantities against Purchase Orders, Delivery Notes, invoices and packing lists. Check packaging condition and visible damage. Record batch/lot numbers and expiry dates. Coordinate with Quality Assurance for inspection and release of food-grade materials. Ensure damaged or non-conforming materials are properly segregated. Accurately record Goods Receipt/GRN in SAP/ERP. Report shortages, discrepancies, damages and quality issues promptly. 3. Inventory Storage & Preservation Ensure materials are stored according to approved storage conditions. Maintain appropriate temperature, humidity and hygiene requirements where applicable. Protect food-grade materials from contamination. Ensure appropriate segregation of chemicals and hazardous materials. Maintain clean and safe pallets, racks and storage areas. Monitor shelf life and expiry dates. Maintain complete batch traceability. 4. FEFO / FIFO Management Implement FEFO (First Expiry, First Out) for materials with shelf-life restrictions. Apply FIFO where FEFO is not applicable. Monitor ageing and near-expiry inventory. Prepare regular near-expiry reports. Escalate approaching-expiry materials to Supply Chain, Production, QA and Finance. Ensure expired materials are not issued to production. Segregate and system-block expired/obsolete materials. Develop action plans for slow-moving and near-expiry stock. 5. Material Issue to Production Issue materials only against approved Material Requisitions, Production Orders or SAP transactions. Verify material code, description, quantity and batch before issuance. Follow FEFO/FIFO during picking. Ensure all issues are accurately and timely posted in SAP/ERP. Maintain proper acknowledgement from receiving departments. Investigate discrepancies between requested and issued quantities. Ensure production returns are properly documented and recorded. 6. SAP / ERP Inventory Management Ensure all physical stock movements are accurately reflected in SAP/ERP. Manage transactions including: Goods Receipt Goods Issue Stock Transfers Material Returns Stock Adjustments Batch Transfers Location Transfers Blocked/Unrestricted Stock Movements Production Material Consumption Ensure no physical movement occurs without system documentation. Ensure system stock movements are supported by physical movements or approved adjustments. Ensure transactions are posted on the same day wherever practicable. Maintain continuous reconciliation between physical and system stock. 7. Inventory Control & Stock Accuracy Maintain accurate stock records across all inventory categories. Monitor critical and high-value materials. Conduct regular cycle counts and monthly physical stock counts. Reconcile physical stock with SAP/ERP balances. Investigate stock variances and perform root-cause analysis. Ensure stock adjustments are made only with appropriate approval. Implement corrective actions for recurring variances. Target: Inventory accuracy of 98–99% or higher . 8. Inventory Ageing & Obsolescence Prepare regular inventory ageing reports. Identify non-moving, slow-moving, excess, near-expiry, expired and obsolete stock. Coordinate with Supply Chain and Procurement to avoid unnecessary replenishment. Work with Production and QA on approved alternative usage of near-expiry materials. Ensure obsolete and expired stock is properly segregated. Support disposal/write-off processes. Minimize inventory losses caused by expiry, damage and poor storage. 9. Stock Reconciliation & Reporting Prepare daily and periodic inventory reports, including: Stock Movement Reports Critical Stock Reports Stock Availability Reports Monthly Inventory Reports Stock Ageing Reports Variance Reports Maintain accurate documentation and records. Provide inventory information and analysis to Finance, Supply Chain and Plant Management. Key Requirements Minimum 5 years of experience , preferably within the Dairy/FMCG manufacturing industry . Experience within East Africa is preferred. Strong hands-on experience in SAP/ERP inventory management . Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel . Strong understanding of warehouse operations, inventory control and stock reconciliation. Experience with FEFO/FIFO, batch tracking and inventory ageing . Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy. Disciplined, meticulous and highly focused on enforcing controls. Strong analytical, problem-solving and reporting skills. Ability to work effectively with Production, Finance, Procurement, QA and Supply Chain teams. Core Skills SAP / ERP | Advanced Excel | Inventory Management | Warehouse Operations | Stock Reconciliation | FEFO/FIFO | Inventory Control | Reporting | FMCG/Dairy Manufacturing | Process & Controls

Our program focuses on strengthening livestock production and markets, enhancing food and water security, addressing gender inequality and youth opportunities, and strengthening devolved governance outcomes to support dryland communities to break from the cycle of humanitarian need and lay the foundations for a more food secure, resilient future. Working across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia, Mercy Corps is implementing the 12-year Regional Livestock Programme (RLP), funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the French Development Agency (AFD). The programme seeks to leverage the significant potential for livestock production and trade within the region by building vibrant regional livestock markets, strengthening livestock production and trade, supporting climate adaptation and enhanced regeneration and governance of rangeland in order to enhance household food security and livelihoods. General Position Summary The Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) Manager for the Regional Livestock Programme will use their in-depth contextual understanding, technical and practical expertise and relationship building skills to lead the collective delivery of a gender transformative program for women’s economic empowerment in the drylands of Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. The WEE manager will lead the design, implementation, and oversight of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy within a Market Systems Development (MSD) framework, ensuring that women, youth, and other marginalized groups benefit equitably from market opportunities. The role will provide technical leadership to integrate gender-transformative and socially inclusive approaches across all program components in targeted corridor, strengthen the quality and effectiveness of WEE interventions, and ensure that program strategies are informed by robust market systems, gender, and social inclusion analyses. Lead the implementation and continuous refinement of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy, ensuring that gender-transformative approaches are effectively embedded across priority interventions and market system activities. Contracting unit: - Office of the Chief Scientist, CGIAR System Organisation Budget Ceiling: - USD 30,000 (all-inclusive; competitive open call) Duration: - 6-8 weeks 2027 milestone: - Blueprint endorsed; build procurement decision made Delivery lead: - Portfolio Performance and Results Team (PPT) Oversight: - Steering Group (Office of the Chief Scientist, DTA, Digital) Deadline for Applications: - 8 September 2026, 23:59hrs (Paris time GMT+2) Background The Performance & Results Management System (PRMS) is CGIAR's core infrastructure for portfolio planning, results reporting, quality assurance, adaptive management, risk management and accountability. It was identified in the CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework as a common system housing planning, theory of change management, stage-gate decision points, and annual reporting — with linked datasets, an integrated dashboard for funders and management, and access aligned to international standards. A February 2021 Accenture fit-for-purpose assessment translated this into implementation requirements: integrated business applications, standardized data definitions across CGIAR systems, and comprehensive onboarding of end users. CGIAR invested approximately USD 800k per year to build and run that system during the period 2022-25, with joint Independent Advisory and Internal Audit review during rollout to ensure delivery against specification. The PRMS was built for a context of relatively stable institutional requirements: a defined set of manual inputs, largely from Window 1/2 funding, processed sequentially — each stage waiting for the previous — to produce a predetermined set of outputs on a predictable cycle. Bespoke requests that fell outside those predetermined outputs required specialists to extract value case by case. That design was rational for the conditions in which it was built. Five shifts prompt a redesign. The first is the nature of demand. The portfolio now requires dynamic, on-demand, user-defined outputs — some anticipated, many not. New business requirements arrive at unpredictable intervals: a GST decision requiring real-time performance data for resource allocation, a donor wanting a bespoke cut across Programs, an AI tool needing to interrogate the data layer directly. A system with predetermined outputs cannot serve this. The second is the scope of what the system must hold. Window 3/bilateral funding — around 1000 non-pooled projects — is heterogeneous in structure, language, and reporting logic. W3/bilateral data cannot be pre-programmed into the system; it is a different problem type, and the current architecture has no way to accommodate it. The third is the ability to orchestrate. CGIAR now deploys operational AI tools — for example SNAP, the zero-draft generator, the QA helper, the Progress Tracking Solution — that need to query, submit to, and coordinate across the system. The current PRMS is not orchestrable: its components are not designed to be called, sequenced, or managed by an AI agent. A system that AI can understand and act on any layer is a key requirement. The fourth is the multiplicity of data sources the system must draw on. Portfolio evidence already sits across many instruments and repositories — among them legacy CRP and Initiative results, current Program and Accelerator results, Plans of Results and Budget (PoRB), Projected Benefits, the Impact Compendium, CGSpace, AnaPlan and others — each with its own structure and logic, with limited interconnections. The fifth is the technological revolution in data management. The maturing of AI and large language models has changed what is possible: data no longer has to be captured through fixed forms and rigid fields to be usable, and outputs no longer have to be predetermined and assembled by hand. This reframes the redesign itself — not a faster version of the old model, but a shift to more flexible, AI-native handling of data that cuts duplication, lowers effort, and can generate higher-quality outputs on demand while maintaining core security safeguards. The new PRMS must be modular, reconfigurable, and interoperable by design — not simply cheaper to build, but cheaper to run and extend, with a clear view of the trade-off between reduced human effort and the real costs of AI-driven processing at scale. Two developments in 2026 show what this looks like in practice. The CGIAR Progress Tracking Solution — launched in July 2026 — demonstrates a possible target architecture: AI-assisted, modular, with a human validation layer, open enough for users to connect their own systems via API. The June 2026 GST-endorsed Guidance Note on Program/Accelerator-level prioritization establishes that actual performance against theories of change will directly inform W1/W2 fund allocation from 2026 onward: PRMS data must be queryable in real time to feed consequential resource allocation decisions, not compiled into static reports after the fact. Together, they define what fit for purpose now requires. Purpose This commission produces an architectural blueprint for a rebuilt PRMS — the design basis for a subsequent build investment. It is not a developer-ready technical specification. It is the front end of a two-stage process: design now, procure and build against it. Steering Group endorsement of this blueprint will be the decision gate for the larger investment. The starting point is not the technology but the people the system serves — funders, senior leadership and governing bodies, Program and Accelerator directors, Centers, and external partners — and the outputs they need, from stabilized reports and dashboards to on-demand answers tailored to a specific question. The design works back from those needs to the data the system already holds, and it must make the system materially lighter to feed — less manual entry, less duplication, less double reporting — not only cheaper to run. The design target is a system that is orchestrable: modular, reconfigurable, and interoperable, built so that AI agents can understand and operate across any layer — or so that any process can run without AI, depending on the risk appetite and the requirement. A result linked to a causal pathway is the atomic unit; everything else is an expression of it. Report once, use many times. The system must function as a data layer that CGIAR tools and authorised external actors can query, contribute to, and act on — not a system that only produces predetermined outputs for predetermined audiences. The blueprint must address constraints: that replacing human effort with AI-driven processing shifts cost rather than eliminates it, and that AI operating costs at scale must be designed for; and that Center and Program adoption has been suboptimal, and the design must address why. Both are in scope. The blueprint must be specific enough to brief the Performance and Results Management Steering Group, scope a build procurement, and hold a development team accountable. Objectives Map the demand the system must serve. Identify the priority users and uses — internal and external — and the outputs each needs, from those already mandated by CGIAR governance to the on-demand, tailored outputs that AI now makes possible. Distinguish what the system already delivers well from what users cannot currently obtain Take stock of the foundational building blocks the portfolio already runs on — for example the Theory of Change, the Projected Benefits model, the Results Framework and its 3 indicator tiers, PoRB/PoD planning instruments — and assess their fitness as the base for a redesigned system rather than starting from a blank slate Characterize the data supply and its fragmentation — what is entered by hand versus captured automatically, and what lives across CGIAR, donor, and Center systems — and consider the growing overlap between monitoring data and science or project data under FAIR. Set out what this implies for a system that draws on existing sources rather than re-collecting data during each reporting cycle Define the connecting layer between demand and supply — the core of this commission. At the level of principle and direction, set out how a result linked to a causal pathway becomes the atomic unit that is reported once and reused many times; how the layer is made FAIR, API-first, and orchestrable so that CGIAR tools and authorised external actors — including AI agents — can query and contribute to it; and how heterogeneous W3/bilateral data is accommodated without being forced into a W1/W2 mold Show how the redesign lightens the load — and where it does not. Explain how it may reduce fields, duplication, and double reporting and shift effort from manual data entry toward data interoperability, while being honest about the trade-offs, including AI operating costs at scale and the points where human judgment must remain Set out the direction of travel and a phased path — what is foundational and should be settled now versus what can be resolved at the build stage, including a costed view of the interim 2027 release and the fuller rebuild. As part of this, diagnose at a strategic level why Centers and Programs have historically, to different extents, routed around PRMS, and what the new system must do differently to earn adoption Scope and Constraints This is a conceptual design commission. The consultant produces the architectural blueprint and roadmap, with the Performance and Results Management Steering Group providing oversight and independent challenge. While security, access controls, audit trails and availability are core aspects of the future system, detailed technical specification — schema definitions, API contracts, and migration mechanics — is deliberately out of scope at this stage: the blueprint establishes direction and principle, and the build phase resolves the detail. Ready by 2027 means: blueprint endorsed by the Steering Group and a build procurement decision made — not full system deployment. Specific PRMS capabilities needed for the 2027 reporting cycle will be identified in the roadmap and may be delivered as an interim release against the existing system while the rebuild proceeds. The costed build roadmap must give PPT and Centers a concrete transition path for modules currently under active management — including the Planning Module and POD — specifying which planned enhancements should continue during the review period and where enhancement work should pause pending the interim 2027 release, so teams are not left to decide this unilaterally while the review is underway. W3/bilateral data integration — where permitted by Centers — is within scope. It is a distinct architectural problem that the blueprint must address — not a future phase or an edge case. The heterogeneity of non-pooled project data, the challenge of connecting it to the CGIAR results hierarchy, and the implications for Center-level data ownership and access are design questions the consultant must answer. Center and Program adoption is a governance and change management challenge, not an architectural one. The blueprint will diagnose it and specify design requirements that reduce friction, but the Steering Group — not the consultant — must own the adoption strategy. Given that PPT leads both delivery and the Steering Group secretariat, the blueprint will be subject to independent technical review by at least two Steering Group members with relevant technical expertise before endorsement. This is a process requirement, not optional. Deliverables Architectural blueprint Costed build roadmap Performance and Results Management Steering Group briefing deck Methodology Review of PRMS technical documentation, AI tool dependency evidence, MELIAF Interoperability Framework, March 2026 operational incident record, enhancement request history, and existing API documentation and agent integration work produced by the PRMS infrastructure team Interviews with PRMS infrastructure team, PPT AI tool developers, MELIAF workstream leads, Center MEL leads, and Center representatives who have actively worked around PRMS. The interview set must include demand-side users, not only the supply side Co-design sessions with PPT to validate architecture decisions Independent technical review of draft blueprint before finalisation — reviewers nominated by the Performance and Results Management Steering Group Timeline Duration: 6-8 weeks Weeks 1-2: Document review, interviews, co-design sessions Weeks 3-5: Blueprint drafting Week 6: PPT review and iteration Weeks 7-8: Independent technical review, revisions, Steering Group briefing Requirements Required Expertise Senior-level expertise in data architecture and API design for complex, federated data environments — including experience designing for AI orchestration and agentic access patterns Advanced understanding of AI/ML pipeline requirements — practical understanding of what LLM-based and agentic tools require from upstream data infrastructure, including cost modelling at scale Deep experience in MEL and risk-informed systems in international development — results frameworks, theory of change, indicator management, and bilateral reporting structures Proven ability to advise on organizational change and adoption in federated, multi-stakeholder settings Track record producing architectural blueprints that non-technical leadership can act on and developers can build against Strong capacity to translate user, governance, and reporting needs into system and data requirements — a service-design sensibility that starts from what users must be able to answer Experience with CGIAR, multilateral research organisations, or comparable federated institutional environments is an advantage Required Application Documents A technical proposal, including: Updated CVs and a cover letter explaining how the consultant's qualifications and experience meet the requirements of the assignment; A short approach to the work, maximum 2-4 pages, outlining how the consultant proposes to address the objectives and deliverables in these TORs, with reference to comparable assignments that demonstrate the required expertise A financial proposal in USD, quoted as a lump sum and supported by a cost breakdown by level of effort per deliverable. Combine both technical and financial proposal in one document Evaluation and communication CGIAR places strong emphasis on ensuring that the objectives of the PRMS Architectural Redesign Blueprint are met. Proposals will be assessed on technical merit and value for money. Only pre-selected candidates will be contacted. Annex 1: CGIAR Performance and Results Management Framework's definition of the Performance and Results Management System (December 2020) Building on investments made in the current phase of CGIAR research programming, a comprehensive, mature and accessible Performance & Results Management System (PRMS) that encompasses planning, monitoring, and reporting will provide robust information upon which to take informed decisions. It will provide: Practical services aligned to meet learning, accountability and resource mobilization objectives, Dashboards open to Funders and partners, with access to the full set of underlying quality-checked data, including communications-focused products capturing collated evidence of CGIAR contribution to change (e.g. outcome/impact case reports) Alignment with international standards such as IATI (International Aid Transparency Initiative) Key PRMS features The CGIAR PRMS will feature: A common system housing plan of work and budget, theory of change management, stage-gate decision points, and annual reporting processes. Job Description Regional oversight: Southeast Africa – Kenya, Uganda, Malawi, Zambia – and China The Supply Chain Manager is responsible for leading the organization’s end-to-end supply chain operations, including demand and supply planning, international shipping, import clearance, warehousing, inventory management, distribution, and supplier performance. The position ensures that products and materials are available at the right place, time, cost, and quality while maintaining compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, customs regulations, and applicable laws. This role will report to the Global Director of Supply Chain. ABOUT YOU We are seeking a dynamic, mission-driven supply chain leader who thrives in complex, multi-country environments and embodies VisionSpring’s values. The ideal candidate will bring: Proven leadership experience with at least 10–12 years in supply chain, procurement, logistics, or operations, including 3+ years in a managerial role. Strong analytical skills with confidence in SAP, Excel, Power BI, and dashboards to interpret operational data and guide decisions. Operational excellence across demand planning, replenishment, inventory management, and international logistics. Stakeholder management expertise, with the ability to negotiate, influence, and build trusted relationships across internal teams, suppliers, and external partners. Governance and compliance discipline, ensuring audit readiness, ethical procurement practices, and adherence to organizational policies. People leadership capability, including coaching, delegation, succession planning, and cross-country coordination. A resilient, detail-oriented, and mission-driven mindset, comfortable working in a lean, fast-moving, multi-country environment. ABOUT US VisionSpring increases lifelong earning, learning, safety, and well-being through eyeglasses for people vulnerable to poverty. We believe in the wonder of clear vision for everybody. Our vision is to ensure that everyone who needs eyeglasses will have them by 2050. We sell and deliver radically affordable optical products and services and develop markets for eyeglasses. This 700-year-old technology has failed to reach 1 billion people in need of vision correction, most of whom live on less than $4 a day. We serve low-income consumers, not as beneficiaries but as customers. Our customers expect high-quality, affordable products and eyecare services, and are willing to spend their limited discretionary income on the immediate and tangible benefits of vision correction. As a social enterprise, we are purpose first. We blend philanthropic and earned revenue, drawing on nonprofit and business practices, and utilize sales and efficiency metrics, as well as social impact measures, to bring vision correction to an ever-growing number of people. We catalyze collaborative action in an expansive, multisector partner network and use our evidence and experience to influence systems change and close the global clear vision gap. We believe in scaling our impact, not our organization. We are a lean team of doers, which means you'll have the opportunity to take on significant responsibilities and make a direct impact on our mission. Our big goal: Everyone who needs eyeglasses will have them by 2050. Job Requirements Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business, Logistics, Procurement, Engineering, or Finance. Strong knowledge of trade terms, letters of credit, customs clearance, and cargo insurance. Advanced analytical skills with SAP, Excel, Power BI, and dashboards. Strong stakeholder management, negotiation, and communication skills. Experience in governance, audit readiness, and SOP development. Proven leadership capability, including coaching, delegation, and succession planning. Lead annual planning, budgeting, risk assessment, and capacity planning. Serve as the main link between country teams, Finance, Global Supply Chain, and leadership. Drive governance through SOPs, RACI matrices, documented processes, and structured escalation. Review warehouse and 3PL Performance and manage persistent 3PL underperformance and support transition planning. job_description: BRAC is an award-winning international non-governmental development organization, with the vision of a world free from all forms of exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. BRAC is a leader in developing and implementing cost-effective, evidence-based programmes to assist poor and disadvantaged communities in low-income countries, including in conflict-prone and post-disaster settings. It is an organisation of and for the people of the Global South, pioneering new development and social enterprise approaches to equip communities to achieve prosperity. As well as being the world's biggest NGO by the number of staff and people directly reached, BRAC has regularly been ranked the number one NGO in the world by the Geneva-based NGO Advisor, an independent organisation committed to highlighting innovation, impact, and governance in the non-profit sector. BRAC retained the top spot in 2020 among the top 500 NGOs for the fifth consecutive year. BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 by Sir Fazle Hasan Abed. It started its first programme outside of Bangladesh in Afghanistan in 2002 and today has activities in 14 countries across Africa and Asia. BRAC has a holistic approach to development that uses a wide array of programmes that include microfinance, education, health, agriculture, gender, and human rights. BRAC invests in communities’ own human and material resources, catalysing lasting change and creating an ecosystem in which people in poverty have the chance to seize control of their own lives. About The Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative The Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative (“UPGI”) is a global unit within BRAC that was founded in 2016 to build off the success of BRAC’s Ultra-Poor Graduation programme in Bangladesh. BRAC UPGI aims to position the evidence-backed Graduation approach as a key driver to eradicate extreme poverty worldwide. It does this by: Advocating for uptake of the Graduation approach by policymakers, national governments, multilateral institutions, and non-governmental organisations; and Effective adaptation and implementation of the Graduation approach in countries around the world, supported through technical assistance and capacity strengthening for external stakeholders. In 2002, BRAC pioneered the Ultra-Poor Graduation (“Graduation”) approach in Bangladesh — a sequenced, two-year investment that enables people to create lasting pathways out of extreme poverty — after recognising that existing programmes were not reaching the poorest people. Through the provision of a productive asset, basic needs support, and ongoing coaching, the Graduation approach tackles multiple constraints at once and achieves lasting impact. Graduation has been adapted and implemented across a wide variety of contexts and countries, with dozens of rigorous evaluations documenting its effectiveness at achieving broad and lasting impact, as well as returns that greatly outweigh the costs. So far, a total of 6.7 million households have been reached by Graduation programs, more than 2 million of which BRAC reached through its flagship Graduation programme in Bangladesh. To help eradicate extreme poverty, BRAC UPGI is working with governments across Africa and Asia to scale Graduation by integrating it into existing government programmes. Alongside governments, BRAC aims to equip 21 million more people to lift themselves from extreme poverty by 2030. About The Position The BRAC Ultra-Poor Graduation Initiative (UPGI) in Africa is seeking to hire a Head of Partnership. This mid-to-senior-level role is intended for candidates with strong grants management and donor management skills who are eager to contribute to the management and implementation of government-led Graduation programmes. We are looking for candidates with prior experience working with large multi-country and complex grants to support in managing grants Reporting to the relevant BRAC UPGI Executive Leadership Team (ELT) member, and working closely with the Director of Strategic Partnerships & Fundraising, the Head of Partnerships will be based at a BRAC office location, with Nairobi, Kenya as the preferred duty station. The BRAC UPGI team works with governments to integrate and scale the Graduation approach into national and subnational systems. In Africa, this involves engaging with staff in countries and central teams as well as donors. The Head of Partnerships will: Drive and oversee or coordinate Grant Management and Reporting Lead in the coordination and development of Programme Investments Proposals Support Donor Relationship in coordination with Director of Strategic Partnerships & Fundraising This role requires comfort working in ambiguous, evolving environments, where solutions must be iteratively developed. The Head of Partnership provides strategic leadership and oversight of BRAC International UPGI's grants portfolio, ensuring effective grant acquisition support, donor compliance, financial stewardship, high-quality reporting, and portfolio performance. The role serves as the central coordination point for complex multi-country donor-funded programmes, working closely with country teams, Finance, Program Design & Impact, Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning, and Strategic Partnerships to ensure successful implementation of grants from award through close-out while strengthening organizational grant management systems and donor relationships. The role requires collaboration across BRAC UPGI and global teams, as well as national partners, necessitating strong interpersonal skills, a willingness to travel, and the ability to work flexibly. The ideal candidate will enjoy a challenge, think innovatively, and be passionate about contributing to sustainable solutions to eradicate extreme poverty. Responsibilities Grant Management and Reporting Serve as the primary point of contact and coordination lead for the SGGA grant, holding the aggregate picture of grant status, timelines, and obligations across all countries and components. Work across teams to Implement BI's SGGA program Establish grant management policies, SOPs and tools Lead and coordinate the preparation of high-quality progress and financial reports to the donor, working closely with country teams, MEL and Program Design & Impact, and Finance and Operations teams to compile accurate, quarterly submissions. Maintain a thorough understanding of SGGA grant requirements, donor rules and regulations, and ensure compliance is embedded across the programme lifecycle. Coordinate closely with Finance to monitor budget vs. actuals across the grant; identify variances, flag risks, and work with budget holders to develop and implement remedial plans. Manage award amendments, budget realignments, no-cost extensions, and other grant modifications, coordinating approvals across UPGI and the Partnerships function as required. Ensure all award documentation is accurately maintained, including in any awards management systems used by BRAC International. Programme Investment Coordination Coordinate the end-to-end process management for SGGA Programme Investments (PIs), working with country teams and PDI on proposal development timelines, review processes, and submission logistics. Support country teams in the development of PI proposals, including contributing to writing, editing, and ensuring alignment with SGGA grant requirements and donor expectations. Track the PI pipeline across the portfolio, maintaining a clear overview of upcoming proposals, approvals, and implementation status. Liaise with donor on PI-related queries and ensure required approvals are secured in a timely manner. Donor Relationship Management Maintain strong working relationships with donor counterparts, serving as an organised, reliable, and well-informed point of contact on grant management matters. Facilitate information flows between UPGI country and central teams and BI Partnerships, ensuring BRAC members of Joint Steering Committee have what they need to support key touchpoints and decisions. Integration With UPGI Programme And Finance Functions Work closely and collaboratively with Finance and Operations to integrate program planning with budgeting and ensure financial reporting is accurate and aligned with technical reporting including supporting effective partner financial management Support new country start-up processes within SGGA relating to award kick-off coordination, ensuring country teams understand grant requirements and timelines from the outset. Maintain knowledge of BRAC International grant management frameworks and ensure SGGA practices are aligned with BRAC International’s wider grant management policies and systems. Team Leadership Manage and develop 1-2 junior staff, building a high-performing, well-organised team with clear roles and strong internal coordination. Foster a team culture that is detail-oriented, proactive, and committed to enabling the wider BRAC International programme to succeed. Qualifications A Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, or another relevant discipline is required.A Master’s degree in a relevant field will be an added advantage. Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in grants management within international development with significant experience managing large, complex donor grants. Minimum 5 years in a middle level management role. Experience managing multi-million-dollar donor portfolios. Demonstrated experience managing the full grant lifecycle, from start-up through reporting and closeout. Experience working with major institutional donors; familiarity with foundation or bilateral funding mechanisms an advantage. Experience working in or managing grants across sub-Saharan Africa strongly preferred. How To Apply BRAC International offers a competitive salary and benefits package. Ziara is a product of AfexAI Innovations Ltd. ABOUT ZIARA Ziara turns a 360° virtual tour into a guided tour led by a voice AI. The visitor asks out loud — the size, the service charge, the neighbourhood, the payment plan — and the tour answers. When a visitor is genuinely interested, their contact details are captured during the conversation. The guide speaks nine languages, and the visitor can switch language mid-tour. For any of that to exist, someone has to be on the ground to scan the property. That is the Ziara Ambassador. THE ROLE You travel to the property, shoot the 360° captures, and build the guided tour. Three packages — you choose which ones you offer: - Scan only - Scan + guided tour setup - Setup only, when the client already has their own photos This is not a remote position. Every assignment happens on site, in your own town and region. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR - A 360° camera — Insta360, Ricoh Theta or equivalent - Discipline on light, framing and vantage point - Your own means of getting to properties - Fluent English; Swahili is a real advantage on site, and any additional language helps with diaspora buyers - Experience in real estate, hospitality or commercial photography is an asset No coding required. You upload the panoramas, name the rooms, add the property details. About fifteen minutes of setup once the photos are taken. HOW IT WORKS - Step one — you create your Ambassador profile. It is free. - Step two — you appear in the directory for your city. - Step three — a client who needs a scan finds you and assigns the job. - Step four — you complete the shoot, delivered straight into their account. - Step five — payment is made through Ziara. Rates are confirmed to you before you accept any assignment. Ambassadors in Nairobi are onboarded in person by our team. WHY THIS IS NOT A ONE-OFF SHOOT A guided tour is not a single job. A developer with several unit types needs one tour per typology, per phase, per launch. An agency with moving stock needs a new one every time a mandate comes in. And the strongest case in Kenya: the diaspora buyer. Someone in the US, the UK, Canada or the Gulf, buying an apartment in Nairobi or a holiday home on the coast, who cannot fly in to view before deciding. A photo gallery answers none of their questions. A guided tour does. Hospitality is the second: lodges, camps and coastal resorts selling rooms to guests who book months ahead and want to know exactly what they are getting. PRIORITY CITIES Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru, Eldoret, Naivasha, Diani, Malindi, Thika, Nanyuki. Tourist areas and neighbourhoods with strong diaspora demand matter most. The directory works everywhere — better to be the first listed in your area. HOW TO APPLY Apply here, or create your profile directly at ziara.app. You can also write to us with your city and coverage area, your 360° equipment, and two or three examples of your work.

job_title: Medical Doctor- Antimicrobial Stewardship Focal Point
job_description: Main Purpose Lead an antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) program in a medical and surgical humanitarian hospital. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) / Doctors Without Borders has increased its focus on the problem of antibiotic resistance. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is growing rapidly in low and middle-income countries and MSF faces ongoing challenges managing antibiotic resistant infections in hospitalized patients particularly in patients with burns, trauma, hospital infections and in pediatric and neonatal care. AMR threatens patient outcomes, makes hospitals less safe and increases costs. MSF is committed to responding and one part of this response is to increase efforts to conserve the effectiveness of antibiotics through antibiotic stewardship. A ccountabilities Medical doctors tasks In addition to Antimicrobial Stewardship Focal Point tasks Leading, promoting and supporting antimicrobial stewardship efforts in the healthcare facility(s) across the spectrum of healthcare. Establish and participate in a multidisciplinary Antimicrobial Stewardship( AS )committee (that meets regularly with Terms of Reference). Identify antimicrobial stewardship priorities together with the AS committee and the mission. Monitor, collect and analyze the antimicrobial data reported to the multidisciplinary AS committee. Conduct regular audits relevant to stewardship priorities. This might include audits of antibiotic use, treatment of select conditions, indications for microbiology testing, and communication of results. Provide feedback to the project and the mission regarding results of audits and plan improvements Co-ordinate and deliver education to other medical, nursing and pharmacy staff around stewardship Support other clinical staff regarding antibiotic choices and regularly participate in clinical rounds. Liaise with the laboratory for timely communication of results (where relevant), interpretation of results and feedback to clinicians. Collaborate with lab + IPC to prospectively monitor pathogens of concern and respond to hospital outbreaks including outbreaks of multidrug resistant organisms/bacteria (MDRO). Identify opportunities to improve stewardship in the project (e.g., therapeutic drug monitoring, OPAT) Participate in relevant project level committees (e.g., IPC, Quality improvement, Morbidity + Mortality reviews). In collaboration with IPC and the clinical team, participate in detection, management and prevention of healthcare associated infections. Requirements Requirements Education: Essential: Medical Doctor degree registered with the Kenya Medical Practitioners and Dentists Council (KMPDC) with a valid practicing licence. Desirable : Completed on-line training in Antimicrobial stewardship [e.g. BSAC (British Society of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy) and/or WHO (World Health Organisation)] Experience: Essential: Essential: at least 5 years’ experience in working as a medical doctor in inpatient settings. Desirable : experience in reviewing medical records/reviewing appropriateness of antimicrobials Languages : English Essential & Swahili Desirable Knowledge : Essential – Have a working understanding of key pathogens, their usual antibiotic susceptibilities, typical clinical presentations, and empiric or targeted treatment. • Have a working understanding of the modes of action of antimicrobials including their spectrum of activity. • Have a working understanding of the key principles of infection prevention and control (IPC) and the relationship between IPC and AMR Antimicrobial Resistance). • Have a working understanding of the appropriate use of antimicrobials to prevent the emergence of resistance and avoidance of adverse effects. • Have a working understanding of the use of diagnostic tests in the investigation and management of infectious diseases. How to use data for feedback and reporting. Desirable: Understanding of behaviour change principles. • Able to provide face to face feedback to prescribers about antibiotic prescriptions Competencies: People management • Commitment • Flexibility • Results • Analytical thinking • Planning and organization • Teamwork

Support development of baseline assessments and connectivity mapping. Review technical sections of donor proposals and communications materials for scientific accuracy. 4. Governance framework development - drafting the transboundary coordination architecture, including options for formal agreements and joint protocols. Government engagement - supporting and, where appropriate, facilitating engagement with relevant national and regional authorities. Who We Are At Trees for the Future (TREES), we believe farmers have the power to transform the world. For over 30 years, we’ve been a global leader in agroforestry, partnering with smallholder farming families to build vibrant economies, sustainable food systems, and thriving ecosystems. Through our proven nature-based solution, farmers restore their land, plant thousands of trees, sequester carbon, and diversify their farming enterprises, breaking cycles of climate change and generational poverty. By reclaiming their agency and expanding their skills and market connections, farmers are creating new possibilities for their families, communities, and the environment. We’ve worked all around the world and are currently active in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda. TREES has planted over 420 million trees to date, restored more than 40,000 hectares of land and partnered with more than 60,000 farmers and their families. Joining our passionate, collaborative team means empowering farmers to lead lasting change for people and the planet. Learn more at trees.org. THE ROLE TREES is seeking a dynamic, entrepreneurial leader to build and deploy our market integration strategy. This role bridges the gap between farm-level programming and viable market access, ensuring smallholder farmers have the information and resources needed to meet market demands (product / variety, quality, timing, and volume) for high-margin agricultural products while advancing long-term land restoration outcomes. The Director will help identify and navigate tradeoffs between commercial opportunity and environmental objectives, ensuring both farmer prosperity and landscape regeneration remain central to program design. Beyond setting strategy, the Director will guide the design, implementation, and evaluation of market integration partnerships across all of our programs. We partner with over 30,000 smallholder farmers in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, delivering extension services, inputs, and financing through our network of last mile project officers. As we expand our impact, we are integrating market mechanisms to ensure farmers not only grow sustainably but thrive economically. The ideal candidate brings private sector experience aligning commercial agricultural opportunities with the needs and perspectives of smallholder farming communities, a track record of developing market access partnerships in multiple value chains, financial acumen, and an existing network within East African agricultural markets. Frequent regional travel is required, and existing permanent work authorization in one of Kenya, Tanzania, or Uganda is required. Evaluate the implications of market integration opportunities on both farmer profitability and restoration outcomes, and recommend approaches that optimize long-term value across both objectives. Design and lead TREES’ market integration roadmap across East Africa, in coordination with country program teams and technical advisors, to ensure integration with country-level programmatic approach, on-the-ground reality, and farmer and market readiness. Identify and prioritize market intervention entry points (i.e. financing, inputs access, offtake aggregation, transport, cold chain, branding), and develop and execute rapid pilots to get to proof of concept (or disprove concepts). Support the design of bundled financial products (e.g. input financing, insurance, forward contracts) to facilitate end market access. Analyze deal structures, leverage regular farmer input and feedback, and negotiate contracts with buyers, processors, and service providers as a trusted partner to farmers. Partnerships & Ecosystem Engagement Build strategic partnerships with cooperatives, exporters, agri-tech firms, and buyers. Engage with private sector actors to co-create structural market access approaches. Represent TREES in value chain forums, trade associations, and other relevant industry networks. Integrate market and restoration performance data to inform recommendations on crops, production systems, and market opportunities. job_description: About TechnoServe: At TechnoServe, we believe that everyone deserves the opportunity to build a better life. We hold ourselves and each other to the highest standards of integrity and transparency. And we focus on delivering lasting impact for our mission. Job Summary: We are seeking a dynamic and motivated Program Director to lead the anticipated five-year AgEMERGE (Agricultural Enterprise-led Market Ecosystems for Resilience, Growth and Equity) program in Kenya, based in Nairobi. AgEMERGE is a market-led program that deploys a delivery model that combines direct technical assistance and Dutch commercial partnerships with a Local Investment Facility. The Program Director will manage this milestone-based grants facility and co-investment portfolio, including awards to local businesses. The PD will also lead the consortium, liaising with the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN), coordinating with sub-national regional leadership and in-country partners, supervising the project teams, and overseeing implementation and resource management in project offices. This role includes financial and administrative oversight and accountability, reporting, risk management and monitoring and evaluation of the project. Program Overview: AgEMERGE is a five-year, €15 million Food and Nutrition Security program funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (EKN) in Kenya. Implemented by a consortium led by TechnoServe, AgEMERGE takes a catalytic, market-led approach centered on the middle of the value chain, strengthening the midstream businesses (aggregators, processors, traders, and logistics providers) that connect farms to markets. A Market Systems Development approach will be adopted to maximise localisation and sustainability. A strong emphasis on inclusive value chains, women’s empowerment and creating economic opportunities for youth will be a cross-cutting priority. Working across three market corridors and 14 predominantly Arid and Semi-Arid Land (ASAL) counties, the program will reach approximately 85,000 farmers, pastoralists, and MSMEs (at least 50% women and youth). AgEMERGE will crowd in commercial investment and Dutch partnership to build a market-driven, climate-resilient, and inclusive agri-food system. Primary Functions & Responsibilities: Lead overall implementation and management of the program, from inception to close-out, ensuring that the program achieves established goals, objectives and targets. Provide strategic guidance, leadership, management and general technical oversight of the program. Drive the program’s catalytic, market-led strategy across the three corridors (Commercial Growth, Adaptive Crops, and Coastal-Northern) and five activity pathways, adjusting intensity and sequencing to market maturity. Oversee the Local Investment Facility and its grant windows (Local Systems & Delivery; Local Trade & Investment; and Local Research, Innovation & Learning), ensuring milestone-based disbursement, cost-share, due diligence, and compliance. Cultivate and activate Dutch commercial partnerships and the investment pipeline — working with European development finance and government credit agencies such as EKN, RVO, FMO, and Dutch firms to connect Kenyan market actors to Dutch knowledge, technology, and capital. Ensure integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), climate resilience, and nutrition as market-system priorities across all activity pathways and grantee engagements.
