job_description: INTRODUCTION World University Service of Canada (WUSC) is a leading Canadian international development organization focusing on three programmatic areas: Economic Opportunities, Education, and Empowerment. Our vision is a better world for all young people. It is a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable world in which all young people, especially women, persons with disabilities (PWD) and marginalized youth from refugees and host communities, are empowered to secure a good quality life for themselves, their families, and their communities. WUSC currently works in 25 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America, with an annual budget of approximately CAD $50 million. Globally, we partner with a network of higher education institutions, civil society organizations, private sector partners, professionals, students, volunteers, faculty, and community leaders who help us achieve our mission. Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems And Pathways (step) Project Description The Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems & Pathways in Kenya (STEP) project is a seven-year initiative implemented by the World University Service of Canada (WUSC). The project aims to improve the economic well-being of displaced and host community youth in Kenya, with a focus on refugee and host populations in Kakuma, Kalobeyei (Turkana County), and Dadaab (Garissa County). STEP seeks to strengthen pathways to employment, entrepreneurship, and digital livelihoods by supporting market-responsive Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), enhancing inclusive entrepreneurship ecosystems, expanding access to digital work opportunities, and addressing systemic barriers affecting youth economic inclusion. The project aims to contribute to positive change for over 10,000 youth, with at least 60% being young women and approximately 70% being refugees or displaced persons. It will do so by strengthening the capacities of ecosystem actors including Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs), Women’s Rights Organizations (WROs), Organization of Persons with Disabilities (OPD), Entrepreneurship Support Organizations (ESOs), TVET institutions, employers, and government agencies. The project is grounded in a Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Safeguarding and Human Rights-Based Approach, recognizing intersecting vulnerabilities faced by young women, persons with disabilities, persons with diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC), and other marginalized groups. Purpose of the Baseline The purpose of the STEP project's baseline study is to support key stakeholders in defining, measuring and documenting the project's achievements in terms of a set of expected outcomes. Further, it aims to empower stakeholders to collaboratively measure progress towards them, review achievements, and adapt strategies as needed and appropriate. Specific Objectives Aligned with this purpose, the baseline study will achieve the following specific objectives: Validate Theory of Change (TOC)Assumptions: Assess pre-implementation contexts and integrate the perspectives and experiences of diverse community members, including women, young youth, PWD, marginalized groups, refugees and host communities to validate the ToC assumptions, gaining insight into community members' perspectives and experiences to inform and refine the overall program implementation strategy. Gather quantitative and qualitative insights from community members to validate the assumptions within the project’s ToC, allowing for the revision and refinement of the program design where appropriate. Establish PMF Baselines & Targets: Determine baseline values and define end-of-project targets for all outcome and output indicators within the Performance Measurement Framework (PMF), including appropriate disaggregation and equity dimensions, Recommend refinements and adjustments to indicator formulations and measurement methodologies based on baseline findings. Baseline Youth Economic & Livelihood Status: Establish baseline data on the economic wellbeing, employability, skills readiness, and entrepreneurial capacity, agency and decision-making of young people in the areas of operation, Map and assess existing local opportunities for employment, entrepreneurship, and digital work to understand the demand side of the youth livelihood ecosystem. Analyze GESI, Power Dynamics and Safeguarding: Benchmark the capability of key ecosystem actors—including TVETs, ESOs, RLOs, OPD WROs and other relevant actors—to deliver inclusive, market-relevant, gender-responsive services, disability-inclusion and safeguarding-sensitive services (utilizing the Institutional Performance Assessment System). Inform the Project MERL Plan: Provide strategic, evidence-based recommendations for finalizing and operationalizing the results-based Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) framework, including equity-sensitive indicators, safeguarding measures, accountability and feedback mechanisms, ethical data-collection protocols, and future data-collection requirements . Design, contextualize, and implement the Household/individual Resilience Measurement Survey (RMS) across project locations to establish baseline resilience scores and track metrics to be re-measured at Midline and Endline, including consideration of differential exposure to shocks, coping strategies, access to support, agency and safety across population groups. Develop, contextualize, pilot and baseline key instruments within the project's MERL system, specifically ensuring that all instruments are inclusive, accessible, culturally appropriate and safeguarding-sensitive: Institutional Performance Assessment System: Establish baseline capability scores for ecosystem actors (TVETs, ESOs, RLOs, WROs, OPD) to deliver inclusive, market-relevant , gender-responsive, disability-inclusive and safeguarding-sensitive services; MSD Partner Adapt-Expand Survey: Baseline early systemic adoption, operational changes, scaling behaviors and institutional practices among direct Market Systems Development (MSD) partners including actions that strengthen GESI, safeguarding and accountability . Crowding-In Survey: Design baseline tools to measure indirect, market-wide replication and systemic crowding-in by non-partner market actors over time, including the extent to which inclusive, safe and equitable practices are adopted. About BRAC International BRAC is an award-winning international non-governmental development organisation, with the vision of a world free from all forms of exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. BRAC is a leader in developing and implementing cost-effective, evidence-based programs to assist poor and disadvantaged communities in low-income countries, including in conflict-prone and post-disaster settings. It is an organisation of and for the people of the Global South, pioneering new development and social enterprise approaches to equip communities to achieve prosperity. As well as being the world’s biggest NGO by number of staff and people directly reached, BRAC has regularly been ranked the number one NGO in the world by the Geneva-based NGO Advisor, an independent organisation committed to highlighting innovation, impact and governance in the non-profit sector. BRAC retained the top spot in 2020 among the top 500 NGOs for the fifth consecutive year. BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 by Sir Fazle Hasan Abed. It started its first program outside of Bangladesh in Afghanistan in 2002, and has since reached millions of people in 11 countries in Asia and Africa. BRAC has a holistic approach to development that uses a wide array of programs and social enterprises, including in microfinance, education, health, agriculture, gender and human rights. BRAC believes that every person has inherent potential, and when an enabling environment is created and that potential is unleashed, even the poorest can become agents of positive change in their own lives, for their families and their communities. About the AIM Program The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway. About the AIM Education Pathway The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students. This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems. job_description: About BRAC International BRAC is an award-winning international non-governmental development organisation, with the vision of a world free from all forms of exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. BRAC is a leader in developing and implementing cost-effective, evidence-based programs to assist poor and disadvantaged communities in low-income countries, including in conflict-prone and post-disaster settings. It is an organisation of and for the people of the Global South, pioneering new development and social enterprise approaches to equip communities to achieve prosperity. As well as being the world’s biggest NGO by number of staff and people directly reached, BRAC has regularly been ranked the number one NGO in the world by the Geneva-based NGO Advisor, an independent organisation committed to highlighting innovation, impact and governance in the non-profit sector. BRAC retained the top spot in 2020 among the top 500 NGOs for the fifth consecutive year. BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 by Sir Fazle Hasan Abed. BRAC has a holistic approach to development that uses a wide array of programs and social enterprises, including in microfinance, education, health, agriculture, gender and human rights. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students. This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems. Opening Date: 4th September 2026 About Resource Mobilization As our ambition and impact have grown, Namati’s budget has increased from $5M to more than $15M in ten years. Namati’s Resource Mobilization team does not take a transactional approach to fundraising; instead, we form relationships with funding partners committed not only to our organization, but to the entire legal empowerment movement. We strive to build and steward expansive, long-term, and high-level funding partnerships that match the ambitious scale of our vision. This kind of fundraising requires a team of aligned, courageous, and strategic connectors who understand where Namati is uniquely placed to make a difference, who can learn continually from our work - and the work of our network and collaborators - to identify promising opportunities, and to create new ones. As we deepen our impact across the globe, we seek a strategic and relationship-driven Partnerships Manager to secure funding for Namati’s work in Africa. As Namati’s fundraising strategy evolves, we’re shifting much of our global Resource Mobilization (RM) team to prioritize multi-program and thematic awards spanning several countries or global initiatives. The Manager will drive the full lifecycle of program-specific fundraising, from prospect identification and cultivation to securing awards to stewarding relationships for longevity and growth. This role will report to the Senior Advisor for the time being. This is a unique opportunity for a skilled fundraiser to embed in the work of locally-rooted country teams, working side-by-side to resource their essential work during a time of global instability, while benefiting from close collaboration with a professional, global fundraising team. Key Responsibilities include: Pipeline development & strategy Build and maintain a robust pipeline of funding opportunities for Namati’s programs in Africa, with particular attention to embassies, local foundations, global foundations with country-specific grantmaking strategy, and in-country offices of bilateral and multilateral agencies. Track donor trends and identify opportunities that align closely with near-term program priorities as well as supporting longer-term country strategies. Collaborate with U.S.-based colleagues to ensure program-specific fundraising complements and aligns with broader thematic and multi-country strategies. Proposal development & reporting Lead the drafting, coordination, and submission of concept notes, proposals and reports for program-specific opportunities in tight collaboration with program and finance teams. Ensure compliance with donor requirements and internal processes, meeting all commitments to funders on time and at the highest quality. Donor cultivation & stewardship Develop strong relationships across diverse stakeholders ranging from embassy staff to local donor representatives to foundation program officers, positioning Namati as a trusted partner. Represent Namati at external meetings, events, and donor convenings in Nairobi and (occasionally) Freetown or elsewhere, including regional or continental convenings such as the Africa Philanthropy Forum. Cultivate opportunities to build multi-country relationships with donor agencies whose embassies fund across more than one Namati country. Internal collaboration Work hand in hand with our Sierra Leone and Kenya program leads to understand their strategies, priorities, and funding needs, and to provide funding outlook insights to inform country strategy. Monitor key pipeline and renewal metrics, ensuring that day-to-day fundraising efforts lead to measurable progress toward strategic fundraising goals. Contribute to team-wide learning about effective program fundraising approaches, sharing insights about country programs and in-country donor landscapes with the global RM team. Coordinated with U.S.-based RM team to ensure your chosen messaging for a Sierra Leone-specific proposal aligns with broader organizational communications and global funding strategies. Relationship-builder: Demonstrated success cultivating relationships with embassies, foundations, or donor agencies with professionalism, warmth, and credibility. Program fluency: Capacity to quickly learn and speak compellingly about Namati’s varying strategies across our African country programs. Communication skills: Excellent writer and communicator, able to produce persuasive proposals and reports, and to adapt messaging to different audiences. Collaborative spirit: A team player who thrives on close collaboration with program and fundraising colleagues across countries and time zones. Public speaking skills, including experience representing organizations at philanthropic or global policy events. Location and Travel This role will be based in Nairobi, Kenya, with occasional travel to Sierra Leone, other parts of Africa, and other global locations as required (approximately 10–15% of the time). Candidates must already be legally eligible to work in Kenya; Namati is unable to sponsor a work permit for this role. The successful candidate will also be expected to occasionally work outside standard working hours to accommodate colleagues across different time zones, particularly as most of the members of the RM team are based in the United States. Compensation and Benefits The offer range for this position is an annual compensation of 5,800,000- 7,100,000 KES/year. Final compensation will be commensurate with the depth of experience that the selected candidate brings. Namati also offers excellent benefits, which include health coverage, generous paid time off, retirement or old-age plan contributions, sick leave, and parental leave. All staff also have access to funds for professional development opportunities. How to Apply Please apply by completing our online application form. Applications will be accepted on a rolling basis, and the position will be open until filled. Initial application review will begin 18th September 2026. No phone calls, please. Namati is an Equal Opportunity Employer. About Namati Since 2012, Namati has worked to build a movement of grassroots justice advocates worldwide. We’ve grown from a small founding group of change-makers to a global staff of 170+ people across 12 time zones in Asia, Africa, and the Americas. The Grassroots Justice Network, which we co-founded and convene to this day, has grown from 30 people in one room to the world’s largest community of justice advocates, with membership from 4,200 organizations across 190 countries. We’ve received the Skoll Award for Social Entrepreneurship , the Global Pluralism Award , and the 2030 Racial Equity Prize , among other honors. Documentaries about our work have been screened at film festivals, government offices, museums, in communities, and beyond.

Resolution & Retention Agent Position Overview As a Resolution & Retention Agent , you will help customers who are considering canceling an order or subscription or returning a product. Your primary goal is to understand why the customer wants to cancel or return and apply our Save-a-Sale strategy to identify an appropriate solution that may allow us to retain the customer, subscription, or order. This is a combination of customer service, problem-solving, and sales/retention . Rather than simply processing a cancellation or return request, you will listen carefully to the customer's concern, identify the underlying reason for the request, and match that reason with the most appropriate save option. You will work with customers through a combination of inbound and outbound contacts . Some customers will reach the Resolution Team directly through our inbound channels, while others will be assigned to you for follow-up after initially interacting with our AI Customer Happiness Agent. This is a commissioned position . In addition to hourly pay, Resolution & Retention Agents are eligible to earn incentives for successfully saved orders and subscriptions. Key Responsibilities Customer Resolution & Save-a-Sale Handle customer requests involving subscription cancellations, order cancellations, and product returns. Identify the customer's primary reason for wanting to cancel or return before determining the appropriate resolution. Apply the company's established Save-a-Sale strategy based on the customer's specific concern and circumstances. Present relevant save options that may include adjusting shipment timing or frequency, modifying product quantity, offering an approved discount, providing product education or troubleshooting, or other approved retention solutions. Clearly explain the value and benefits of available options without pressuring the customer or creating unnecessary friction. When a save is not appropriate or the customer declines the available options, complete the cancellation or return process according to company policy. Inbound & Outbound Customer Contact Manage customer conversations across assigned inbound channels, including phone, email, chat, and other supported communication channels. Complete assigned outbound follow-up with customers whose cancellation or return request began through our AI Customer Happiness Agent or another customer service channel. Be equally comfortable responding to incoming customer requests and proactively reaching out to customers to complete unresolved requests and retention opportunities. Follow through on assigned customer cases until the appropriate resolution has been reached. Customer Needs Assessment & Problem-Solving Ask thoughtful questions and actively listen to understand the customer's reason for canceling or returning. Recognize common concerns such as cost, excess product, shipment frequency, product usage, expectations, subscription confusion, or other barriers to continued use. Use good judgment to determine which approved save strategy best addresses the customer's actual concern, rather than making the same offer to every customer. Provide accurate product education and guidance when additional information may help resolve the customer's concern. Recognize situations where a retention attempt is not appropriate and follow company procedures for cancellations, returns, escalations, adverse reactions, or other special circumstances. Retention Performance Work toward individual and team goals for orders saved, subscriptions retained, save rate, and revenue retained. Make appropriate save attempts on eligible cancellation and return requests according to company guidelines. Accurately record whether a save was attempted, the offer made, whether it was accepted or declined, and the final customer outcome. Participate in coaching and performance reviews designed to improve save effectiveness, customer experience, and overall retention results. Earn commission or incentives on eligible successfully saved orders and subscriptions according to the company's current incentive program. Documentation & Follow-Through Accurately document customer concerns, save offers, outcomes, cancellations, returns, and follow-up activity in company systems. Maintain clear records so that another team member can easily understand what occurred and what actions have already been taken. Identify recurring cancellation or return trends and share useful customer feedback with leadership. Take ownership of assigned customer requests and ensure they are fully resolved rather than leaving unnecessary open issues for another team member. Team Collaboration & Continuous Improvement Participate in team discussions, coaching, and training to strengthen retention strategies and customer communication. Share successful approaches and customer insights that may help improve team save performance. Stay current on company policies, Save-a-Sale strategies, products, promotions, subscription options, return procedures, and approved customer offers. Collaborate with Product Protocol Specialists and other Customer Happiness teams when additional expertise or support is needed. Skills & Qualifications Preferred: 1+ year of customer service, retention, outbound sales, collections, or other customer-facing experience. Strong verbal and written communication skills. Comfortable handling both inbound and outbound customer interactions. Strong active-listening skills with the ability to uncover the reason behind a customer's request. Ability to confidently recommend solutions and explain their value while remaining empathetic and professional. Strong judgment and problem-solving skills, with the ability to match customer concerns to appropriate solutions. Comfortable working in a performance-driven, commissioned environment with measurable retention goals. Ability to manage objections and difficult customer conversations without becoming defensive or overly aggressive. Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately document customer interactions and outcomes. Experience using CRM, customer service, or contact-center software is preferred. Key Attributes The Ideal Resolution & Retention Agent Is Curious: Seeks to understand why the customer wants to leave before offering a solution. Solution-Oriented: Looks for an appropriate way to solve the customer's concern rather than simply processing the request. Persuasive: Confidently communicates the value of relevant solutions without creating pressure. Empathetic: Understands the customer's perspective while still working toward a successful retention outcome. Results-Driven: Motivated by goals, performance metrics, and the opportunity to earn incentives through successful saves. Resilient: Comfortable hearing "no," handling objections, and moving confidently to the next opportunity. Accountable: Takes ownership of assigned customers and follows through to resolution. Adaptable: Comfortable moving between inbound requests, outbound follow-up, phone conversations, and written channels. Pay Structure Hourly Pay + Commission/Incentives Resolution & Retention Agents are eligible to earn additional compensation for qualifying successfully saved orders and subscriptions. This structure rewards agents for creating positive customer outcomes while retaining revenue for the company. Why Join Us? Join The Hero Company and become part of a Customer Happiness team focused on finding solutions, creating great customer experiences, and building lasting relationships. This role allows you to directly influence both customer satisfaction and company growth , while earning additional compensation for successful retention results. You'll receive comprehensive training on our products, systems, Save-a-Sale strategies, and customer experience standards, along with ongoing coaching and opportunities for professional growth. job_title: RFP-Development of AI Powered Entrepreneur Training Support Platform
job_description: About Inkomoko Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive. In 2026, Inkomoko was listed by the Financial Times as the 5th fastest-growing company in Africa, supporting entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa to grow thriving businesses and build inclusive, resilient economies. Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 100,000 entrepreneurs, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest investor to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa. Inkomoko has 900+ staff in 50 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko's 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives. INKOMOKO VALUES All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values: Purpose: be solutions-oriented and produce high-quality work and be a global leader Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you think is possible. Improvement: be humble and committed to continuous learning and growing through giving and receiving open and accurate feedback Bravery: willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, inclusive Turikumwe / Tuko Pamoja / Abren Nen / Kulana Sawa / We Are Together: appreciate your colleagues, celebrate success, and support each other in hard times Assignment / Service Design, Development, Commissioning and Maintenance of an AI-Powered Entrepreneur Training & Support Platform Objective of the Assignment Inkomoko is transitioning from a human-mediated service delivery model to a digitally scaled service model, to improve the client experience, enhance the quality and consistency of entrepreneur training, and reduce the operational burden currently placed on frontline Business Advisors, trainers, and support staff Clients and staff currently rely heavily on Relationship Managers, trainers, and support staff for: Basic product and policy questions Loan balance and repayment enquiries Training in products and systems Routine support issues This dependency leads to delays, inconsistent messaging, and a high manual workload on Inkomoko's field and support teams — constraining the organisation's ability to scale its entrepreneur programs across new regions and cohorts. Inkomoko is seeking proposals from qualified vendors to design, develop, commission, and provide ongoing maintenance and support for an AI-powered platform (the "Platform") that will: Deliver structured, interactive AI-driven training that guides entrepreneurs progressively through the four stages of the Inkomoko entrepreneur journey: Ideation, Investment Readiness, Business Planning and Market Entry; Provide 24/7 automated customer support and FAQ handling; Respond securely to loan and financial product enquiries; Integrate with Inkomoko's core systems (including the Core Banking System (CBS), Inkobook, and the PBI reporting dashboard); Enforce role-based access, data privacy, and full audit control Scope of Work The Platform being procured through this RFP must digitise and scale Inkomoko's existing, field-tested Program Design. This design guides an entrepreneur through a structured, sequential journey of training modules paired with in-person or remote consulting visits. Each module builds on the previous one, combining skills training with structured advisory data collection that informs the client's next stage of readiness. 3.1 Idea-Stage Track (Primary Focus Of This Platform) The Idea-stage track takes an entrepreneur from a business idea to market entry across four sequential modules; each paired with a consulting visit: Module 1 - Business Ideation Module 2 - Investment Readiness Module 3 - Business Planning Module 4 - Market Entry 3.2 Existing Business (Growth) Track — Future Scalability Context Inkomoko also runs a parallel Existing Business (EB) track across five (5) consulting visits namely: Investment Readiness Bookkeeping Business Model Canvas Sales Marketing While the primary scope of this RFP is the Idea-Stage journey, the Platform's information architecture, content model, and workflow engine must be designed so that the EB track and any future cohort tracks can be configured and onboarded without requiring a re-architecture of the Platform. Vendors should describe in their proposal how their solution supports this configurability (see Section 6.5). 3.3 Supporting Tools in the Current Program Inkomoko's current program relies on the following tools, which the Platform must be capable of integrating or interoperating with: Inkobook - training attendance and consulting record system PBI Dashboard - reporting and analytics Digital Bookkeeping tools Analog Bookkeeping (booklet-based) records, for clients without digital access Deliverables / Outputs The selected vendor will be responsible for the end-to-end design, development, testing, commissioning (deployment into production), and ongoing maintenance of the Platform, covering the following functional areas: 4.1 AI-Driven Training Delivery Deliver AI-driven training modules mapped to the four Idea-Stage modules (Business Ideation, Investment Readiness, Business Planning, Market Entry), sequenced to mirror the existing consulting-visit journey; Enable interactive learning through chat-based conversation and/or guided, step-by-step workflows (e.g., dynamic Lean Canvas builder, investment-readiness checklist); Track individual user progress, module completion, time spent, and drop-off points; Allow Inkomoko training staff to upload, version, and manage training content without vendor intervention 4.2 Automated Customer Support Provide 24/7 automated customer support across supported channels; Handle common queries and service requests without human involvement wherever possible; Escalate complex or sensitive issues to human agents with full conversation context preserved; Create and track support tickets end-to-end, including status updates back to the client 4.3 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and General Enquiries / Knowledge Management Maintain a dynamic, centrally managed knowledge base covering products, policies, and training content; Respond accurately to frequently asked questions using natural-language understanding; Continuously learn and improve response quality using feedback and usage data; Provide an administrative interface for non-technical Inkomoko staff to manage, approve, and publish content updates 4.4 Loan Product and Financial Enquiries Provide guidance on Inkomoko loan products and partner financial-institutions relevant to the client's investment-readiness stage; Avail a cashflow and profitability analysis tool 4.5 Other Cross-Cutting Requirements Multi-channel support, including WhatsApp with consistent experience across channels; Role-based access control differentiating internal staff (Business Advisors, trainers, administrators) from external users (clients/entrepreneurs); Configurable workflows that Inkomoko can adapt as the program design evolves year-to-year; Real-time analytics and reporting on training engagement, support resolution, and enquiry volumes, feeding into (or complementing) the existing PBI Dashboard; Well-documented APIs for connecting to Inkomoko's existing systems; Comprehensive audit logging of all interactions, including AI-generated responses and escalations; Compliance with applicable data privacy and protection regulations in each country of operation; Multilingual support (at minimum, English, French, Kinyarwanda, and Kiswahili — vendors should confirm supported languages and propose an approach for additional languages); High availability and horizontal scalability to support expansion across multiple countries and growing client cohorts Duration / Timeline Vendors should propose a detailed project plan; the phasing below is indicative and subject to negotiation. Discovery, Requirements Validation, and Solution Design Indicative Duration: 3-4 weeks Core Platform Development (Architecture Layers and Integrations) Indicative Duration: 8-12 weeks Training Module Build-Out (All 4 Idea-Stage Modules) Indicative Duration: 6-8 weeks (may run in parallel with the core platform development) Testing (Functional, Security, Performance, and UAT) Indicative Duration: 3-4 weeks Pilot Deployment (Limited Cohort / Region) Indicative Duration: 4-6 weeks Full Commissioning and Roll-Out Indicative Duration: 2-4 weeks Post-Launch Hypercare and Transition to Steady-State Maintenance Indicative Duration: 8 weeks post go-live Reporting / Supervision The vendor will report directly to Inkomoko's Digital Transformation Product Lead for the AI Platform. Reporting frequency and communication expectations are as follows: Weekly progress meetings during the design and development phases Bi-weekly status reports summarizing progress, risks, and upcoming milestones Ad-hoc communication via established project channels (e.g., Slack/Email) for urgent issues or clarifications Monthly review meetings with the project steering committee to align on strategic direction and budget tracking The vendor will be responsible for ongoing maintenance and support of the Platform following commissioning, under a Service Level Agreement (SLA) to be finalised at contracting. Vendors should propose SLA terms addressing, at minimum: Critical Definition: Platform down / core function unavailable to all users Target Response Time: ≤ 1 hour Target Resolution Time: ≤ 4 hours High Definition: Major function degraded / affecting a subset of users Target Response Time: ≤ 4 hours Target Resolution Time: ≤ 1 business day Medium Definition: Non-critical defect with workaround available Target Response Time: ≤ 1 business day Target Resolution Time: ≤ 5 business days Low Definition: Cosmetic issue / enhancement request Target Response Time: ≤ 3 business days Target Resolution Time: Next scheduled release Requirements Required Qualifications and Experience Prospective vendors must demonstrate the following minimum qualifications: Proven experience designing and deploying AI-powered conversational platforms (chatbots/virtual assistants) at production scale, ideally in financial services, EdTech, or international development contexts; Demonstrated experience with multi-channel deployment, including WhatsApp Business API, web chat, and mobile applications; Experience integrating with core banking systems (CBS) or similarly sensitive financial/transactional systems; Demonstrated capability in natural language processing for multiple languages, including African languages such as Amharic, Arabic, English, French, Kinyarwanda, Kiswahili and Somali (or a credible plan to develop this capability); Strong data privacy, security, and compliance track record, including relevant certifications where applicable (e.g., ISO 27001); Experience delivering projects in emerging markets and/or with low-connectivity user bases; At least three (3) verifiable references from comparable engagements completed in the last five years; Demonstrated financial stability and capacity to support a multi-year maintenance engagement Benefits Submission Requirements Vendors must submit a Technical Proposal and a Financial Proposal as two separate documents/sections, in accordance with the structure below. 8.1 Technical Proposal Company profile, relevant experience, and team composition (including CVs of key personnel); Copies of relevant business registration and statutory documents; Understanding of Inkomoko's requirements and proposed solution approach; Proposed solution architecture, mapped to the model; Detailed response to the scope of work; Proposed technology stack, including AI/NLP models or platforms to be used, and rationale; Data privacy, security, and compliance approach; Proposed project plan and timeline; Proposed maintenance and support model; Risk register and mitigation approach; At least three (3) client references with contact details; Any other documents relevant to the assignment. Evaluation Criteria Proposals will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Technical Proposal: Detailed methodology, understanding of the assignment, implementation approach, and proposed work plan Technical Solution: Description of the proposed solution, system, methodology, or approach applicable to the assignment Integration/Implementation Approach (where applicable): Proposed implementation methodology, integration capabilities, project management approach, and technical architecture Financial Proposal: Detailed and itemized pricing, including implementation, licensing, professional service, travel, and any recurring costs Experience and Qualifications: Demonstrated experience in similar assignments, client references, qualifications of key personnel, and organizational capacity Compliance Requirements: Evidence of compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, statutory, and industry requirements relevant to the assignment Submission Instructions Submission Deadline: 18th September 2026 Deadline for Clarification Questions: 11th September 2026 Clarification and Submission Email: procurement.regional@inkomoko.com Mandatory Email Subject: Proposal Submission - [AI-Powered Entrepreneur Training & Support Platform] - [Vendor Name] Terms & Conditions Confidentiality: All information shared as part of this RFP process is confidential and must not be disclosed to third parties without Inkomoko's written consent Intellectual Property: All custom-developed source code, content, and documentation produced under this engagement shall become the property of Inkomoko upon payment, except for pre-existing vendor IP or third-party/open-source components, which must be clearly disclosed and licensed appropriately Right to Reject: Inkomoko reserves the right to accept or reject any or all proposals, and to cancel this RFP process, without incurring any liability to affected vendors No Commitment: Issuance of this RFP does not commit Inkomoko to award a contract or to reimburse any costs incurred by vendors in preparing their proposals Proposal Validity: Proposals must remain valid and open for acceptance for a minimum of 90 days from the submission deadline Data Ownership: All clients' information, training, and interaction data generated through the Platform remains the sole property of Inkomoko Compliance: The selected vendor must comply with all applicable laws and regulations in each country where the Platform is deployed, including data protection law Communications: All official communications regarding this RFP must be directed to the contact named in Section 10.

We strive to build and steward expansive, long-term, and high-level funding partnerships that match the ambitious scale of our vision. This kind of fundraising requires a team of aligned, courageous, and strategic connectors who understand where Namati is uniquely placed to make a difference, who can learn continually from our work - and the work of our network and collaborators - to identify promising opportunities, and to create new ones. Start Date: September 2026 End Date: December 2026 Contract Type: Consultancy Deadline for Applications: 16 September 2026 by 11:59 pm CEST Background and context Across eleven genebanks, CGIAR Centers are custodians of the world's most diverse publicly available crop collections, comprising more than 700,000 accessions of more than 3,000 plant species. Under the terms of the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA, hereafter ‘the Plant Treaty'), the genetic material housed in these CGIAR genebanks is freely available to researchers, breeders, local communities, and farmers; contributing to science and innovations for more resilient and sustainable food systems. From 2025, CGIAR's work on genebanks has been organized under the Genebanks Accelerator. The Accelerator brings together CGIAR Centers and partners to strengthen the use of crop diversity through rigorous conservation, enabling policies, and world-class phytosanitary controls. By leveraging frontier technologies in genomics, artificial intelligence (AI), and cryopreservation; the Accelerator aims to enhance the availability and impact of genetic resources worldwide. For more than two decades, CGIAR has worked closely with the Global Crop Diversity Trust (‘Crop Trust') alongside other funders to ensure the sufficient, sustainable, and predictable financing of genebanks consistent with Centers' obligations under the Plant Treaty. In practice, in addition to the funding from the Crop Trust to CGIAR Centers and any earmarked contributions through CGIAR Trust Fund Window 2 (W2) to the Genebanks Accelerator and its predecessors, CGIAR has used unearmarked CGIAR Trust Fund Window 1 (W1) contributions - allocated to the Genebanks Accelerator and its predecessors - to ensure that essential genebanks operations are funded at a ringfenced, minimum level. Underpinning this approach is a series of careful costing reviews, aiming to ensure that funding towards CGIAR genebanks keeps up with the cost of sustaining their essential operations. The last comprehensive CGIAR genebanks costing study was completed in 2020 as a joint undertaking between CGIAR and the Crop Trust, after which a lighter-touch review was carried out in 2024. In April 2026, CGIAR's Global Science Team (GST) agreed to launch, in 2026, an external, independent review of the costs of essential CGIAR genebank operations, associated chargeback practices, and potential efficiencies and cost savings, following CGIAR Cost Principles and Indirect Cost Guidelines. In support of a first phase of this exercise, CGIAR seeks an experienced individual or firm (hereafter "Consultant") to carry out an external and independent assessment of the costs of and funding towards CGIAR genebanks operations, and recommended next steps. Objectives Through this assignment, CGIAR aims to ensure that: CGIAR Centers' obligations under the Plant Treaty over the 2028—2030 time frame are fully financed; financing is grounded in clear, transparent, consistent, and agreed costing across Centers, genebanks, and Germplasm Health Units (GHUs); and near- and medium term efficiencies and cost savings are identified and realized Key Responsibilities Working under the oversight and guidance of a Steering Group that brings together the Genebanks Accelerator, representation from the Crop Trust, as well CGIAR finance and funding experts, the Consultant will: engage with key stakeholders to understand their level of confidence in and support for the current approach to costing and financing essential CGIAR genebanks operations; carry out a desk review of current CGIAR genebanks costs - including future-proofing activities, GHUs, and policy work - and associated financing arrangements; and building on the above, compile a report with conclusions and recommended next steps addressing, inter alia, the adequacy of the current costing and financing arrangements as well as any key data and information gaps that could require revisiting the comprehensive 2020 costing study High-level timeline The assessment will be carried out from September to December 2026 with a view to informing next steps from January 2027. Requirements Key competencies The Consultant is expected to demonstrate strong experience and expertise in the following areas: genebanks and their core functions in the context of science and innovations to transform food, land, and water systems; genebanks operations - including future-proofing activities, GHUs, and policy work - and financial management; CGIAR's stakeholder landscape and work on science and innovations to transform food, land, and water systems in a climate crisis; and multi-stakeholder engagement in a global research for development context To safeguard the independence of the assessment, the Consultant cannot be formally affiliated with any current CGIAR Center or funder, or the Crop Trust. How To Submit a Proposal The Candidate will submit: a short profile demonstrating relevant experience and qualifications; a concise technical proposal outlining the intended approach and delivery steps within the proposed timeframe; and a simple budget proposal outlining the proposed number of working days and daily rate, with costs broken down by deliverable The technical and budget proposals can be combined as one document. Training Admissions and Engagement Coordinator CONTRACT: Full-time, with an initial one-year contract (renewable) based on performance and funding availability. REPORTS TO: Head of the Centre for the Nature Economy DIRECT REPORTS: None LOCATION: The post will initially be based at NATURAL STATE’s office in Nanyuki, with plans to relocate to the Centre for the Nature Economy once operational. On-site residence may be required. ABOUT NATURAL STATE Natural State is a pioneering environmental non-profit organisation working to catalyse large-scale nature restoration and conservation by revolutionising impact monitoring, creating innovative financial mechanisms, and building capacity at the local level. With operations in Kenya, the United States, and South Africa, we bring together science, technology, and community partnerships to restore ecosystems and secure a more resilient and biodiverse future. Natural State and its partners are establishing the Centre for Nature Economy in Kenya, a centre devoted to global excellence in developing the leaders, knowledge and enterprises needed to accelerate the nature economy. We deliver core programmes in vocational training and leadership, Indigenous knowledge and learning, and community finance and resilience. For more information, visit www.naturalstate.org. ROLE SUMMARY The Training Admissions and Engagement Coordinator is an enabling role within the Leadership and Learning Department, responsible for the systems, administration and coordination that support the Centre’s programmes and participant journey. This includes admissions and enrolment, participant engagement, university and learning partner outreach, bursary administration, and learning and participant management systems.The role supports the Head of Centre and the Department’s Training, Learning Design, Indigenous Knowledge and Innovation, MEL, and Operations units, and liaises with Fundraising, Communications and Partnerships and other Natural State departments as required. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following: 1. Admissions and Participant Engagement · Manage applications, admissions, enrolment and participant onboarding across Leadership and Learning programmes. · Act as a key contact for prospective and enrolled participants, providing timely information on programme requirements, fees, bursaries, schedules and next steps. · Maintain accurate applicant and participant records and coordinate selection administration, confirmations, waiting lists and completion documentation. · Manage participant communications before, during and after programmes, including engagement between modules, post-programme follow-up, and ongoing communities of practice. · Work with FCP and programme colleagues to support programme promotion and participant recruitment. 2. University and Learning Partner Engagement · Support outreach and relationship management with universities, colleges, training institutions and other relevant learning partners. · Research and maintain a pipeline of priority institutions and contacts and coordinate meetings, visits, information sessions and follow-up. · Support institutional relationships that contribute participants, expertise, research connections, placements or other learning opportunities. · Work with the Head of Centre, relevant Leadership and Learning colleagues and Fundraising, Communications and Partnership to coordinate partner engagement and track agreed actions. 3. Training Bursary Fund Administration · Administer the centre’s training bursary fund in line with approved criteria, budgets and procedures. · Coordinate applications, eligibility checks, assessment administration and communication of approved decisions. · Maintain accurate records of awards, beneficiaries, commitments and available balances, working with Finance on related financial administration. · Track bursary utilisation and prepare routine summaries and information for internal and donor reporting. · Final bursary and financial approvals remain with the appropriate authorised decision-makers. 4. Learning Systems and Training Administration · Support day-to-day administration of the LMS and other admissions, participant and engagement platforms, including learner accounts, enrolment, access and records. · Maintain the training calendar, participant databases, attendance, completion records, programme files and standard administrative tools. · Provide first-line support for basic learner platform issues and escalate technical matters to the appropriate system owner. · Support online and blended programme administration and maintain accurate, secure and consistent information across systems. · Support adoption and improvement of learning and participant management systems as the Centre grows. 5. Programme Coordination and Operations Interface · Provide the Centre’s Operations/Facilities unit with timely participant numbers, schedules, arrival and departure details, accommodation, dietary and other programme requirements. · Support participant registration, orientation and programme readiness for residential, in-person and field activities. · Coordinate participant-facing travel and logistical information and communicate changes promptly to relevant teams. · Support the CNE Operations/Facilities unit with accommodation, catering, transport, facilities and site operations. 6. MEL and Reporting Support · Work with the MEL Manager to administer agreed participant surveys, feedback tools and programme data collection. · Maintain accurate admissions, demographic, attendance, completion, bursary and engagement data and provide agreed information for MEL and departmental reporting. · Support participant and alumni follow-up and data-quality checks as required. 7. Departmental and Head of Centre Administrative Support · Provide administrative and coordination support to the Head of Centre, including meeting bookings, calendars, agendas, briefing materials, action tracking and follow-up. · Provide administrative support to the Training, Learning Design, and Indigenous Knowledge and Innovation units and other departmental workstreams as required. · Maintain departmental files, correspondence, contact lists, calendars and shared information resources. · Support departmental meetings, events, partner visits, travel, routine budget tracking, invoices and other administrative requirements, coordinating with relevant Natural State functions. 8. Professional Relationships and Communication • Maintain clear, open, and timely communication with the line manager, raising any concerns or risks promptly. • Collaborate effectively with colleagues across the Leadership and Learning department and the wider organisation, including HR, communications, and operations teams. • Act as a role model in upholding the organisation's core values, contributing to a positive, professional, and inclusive working culture Person Specification Must Have Experience At least five years’ relevant experience in training or programme administration, admissions, participant engagement, education administration or a comparable coordination role. Demonstrated experience managing applications, admissions, enrolment and participant records. Experience coordinating multiple programmes, schedules, meetings, deadlines and administrative processes. Experience communicating with participants and engaging with external organisations or institutional partners. Experience using digital systems to manage records, applications, communications or programme administration. Knowledge & Skills Excellent organisational and administrative skills, with strong attention to detail and follow-through. Strong written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills. Strong digital capability, including Microsoft Office and confidence using databases, online forms, shared platforms and digital systems. Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently and coordinate effectively across teams. Sound judgement and discretion when handling confidential participant, bursary and organisational information. A proactive, flexible and service-oriented approach, with a commitment to a high-quality participant experience. Education Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant qualification in business administration, education, programme management, communications, community development or a related field. Candidates with an appropriate diploma or professional qualification combined with substantial relevant experience will also be considered. Nice to Have Experience working within a university, training institution, professional education provider or similar learning environment. Experience engaging with universities, training institutions or other learning partners. Experience administering bursaries, scholarships or participant financial support. Experience using an LMS, CRM, admissions or participant management system. Experience supporting residential, blended, vocational or community-based learning programmes. Experience supporting participant or alumni engagement, including communities of practice. Experience administering participant feedback, surveys or MEL data collection. Experience working in conservation, restoration, sustainable development or the nature economy. Knowledge of Laikipia and/or relevant Kenyan language skills. job_description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. Job Purpose/Objective The Emergency Officer will support the implementation, monitoring, and reporting of emergency response and disaster risk reduction (DRR) activities within the country program. The position will assist the Emergency Manager in conducting assessments, implementing response interventions, engaging communities and partners, monitoring crisis triggers, and ensuring timely delivery of emergency response activities in accordance with IRC policies, donor requirements, humanitarian standards, and government regulations. Main Responsibilities She/he will ensure that an engagement approach to working with communities and the local authorities, other partners is employed and all activities are carried out in a way that is sensitive to community needs and promotes the full and equal participation of women, men, children and youth. Primary responsibilities include: Project Planning and Assessments Support rapid needs assessments, baseline surveys, and emergency field assessments. Collect and analyze information to support identification of humanitarian needs and priorities. Assist in the development of project implementation plans, work plans, budgets, and response strategies. Support the development and review of technical specifications, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and operational guidelines for emergency response activities. Participate in contingency planning and emergency preparedness initiatives Project Implementation Coordinate and implement emergency response activities in assigned locations. Monitor daily project activities to ensure quality implementation and adherence to approved plans. Support effective delivery of emergency interventions within approved budgets and timelines. Ensure beneficiary participation, inclusion, accountability, and protection principles are integrated into all project activities. Support procurement processes through preparation of technical inputs, field verification, and monitoring of supplies and services. Promote compliance with IRC policies, humanitarian principles, and donor requirements during implementation. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Assist in collecting, compiling, and validating project data and indicators. Support implementation of monitoring and evaluation frameworks and tracking systems. Conduct routine field monitoring visits and prepare monitoring reports. Track project progress against work plans and targets and promptly report challenges. Maintain accurate project records, beneficiary databases, and activity documentation. Support accountability mechanisms, including community feedback and complaint response systems. Contribute to documentation of lessons learned, success stories, and best practices. Reporting Prepare weekly, monthly, quarterly, and other routine activity reports. Compile field updates, assessment findings, and response progress reports. Ensure timely submission of project documentation and supporting evidence. Provide regular updates on implementation progress, risks, and emerging humanitarian concerns. Community Engagement and Coordination Facilitate community mobilization and awareness activities. Strengthening engagement with local authorities, community structures, and humanitarian partners. Support coordination meetings at community and field levels. Encourage participation of women, men, youth, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups in project activities. Actively participate in inter-sectoral activities and coordination initiatives. Emergency Preparedness and Response Monitor humanitarian situations and report emerging risks and crisis triggers. Support rapid deployment and scale-up of emergency interventions during crises. Participate in emergency preparedness exercises, simulations, and contingency planning. Assist in outbreak response, displacement response, and other emergency operations as required. Compliance and Safeguarding Ensure adherence to IRC Code of Conduct, safeguarding, and protection policies. Comply with donor regulations, government requirements, and humanitarian standards. Promote safe, accountable, and inclusive programming. Immediately report safeguarding concerns, security incidents, and operational risks through appropriate channels. Required Qualifications Degree/Diploma in public health, nursing, community development, clinical medicine or related field. A minimum of Three years’ experience on programming in emergencies, relief or development including implementing a large-scale community-based humanitarian project with evidence of successful implementation of similar projects. Required Experience & Competencies Minimum of 3 years relevant work experience in ASAL Strong skills in project management Demonstrated skills in technical design and roll out of humanitarian response and disease outbreaks.
