job_description: Description Location: Hargeisa , Mogadishu, Kismayo, Nairobi, Addis Ababa or Jigjiga Position Status: Full -time, Regular Salary Level TBD (Based on country salary scale) Current Team Member New Position Risk Level: ☐ Level 3 ☐ Level 2 ☐ Level 1 (Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability. Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children. Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data) About Mercy Corps Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future. Program Summary Mercy Corps has been a leader in the drylands of the Horn of Africa for the last decade, supporting households affected by climate change, drought, conflict and other challenges to adapt and thrive in the face of increasing shocks. Our program focuses on strengthening livestock production and markets, enhancing food and water security, addressing gender inequality and youth opportunities, and strengthening devolved governance outcomes to support dryland communities to break from the cycle of humanitarian need and lay the foundations for a more food secure, resilient future. Working across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia, Mercy Corps is implementing the 12-year Regional Livestock Programme (RLP), funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the French Development Agency (AFD). The programme seeks to leverage the significant potential for livestock production and trade within the region by building vibrant regional livestock markets, strengthening livestock production and trade, supporting climate adaptation and enhanced regeneration and governance of rangeland in order to enhance household food security and livelihoods. General Position Summary The Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) Manager for the Regional Livestock Programme will use their in-depth contextual understanding, technical and practical expertise and relationship building skills to lead the collective delivery of a gender transformative program for women’s economic empowerment in the drylands of Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya. The WEE manager will lead the design, implementation, and oversight of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy within a Market Systems Development (MSD) framework, ensuring that women, youth, and other marginalized groups benefit equitably from market opportunities. The role will provide technical leadership to integrate gender-transformative and socially inclusive approaches across all program components in targeted corridor, strengthen the quality and effectiveness of WEE interventions, and ensure that program strategies are informed by robust market systems, gender, and social inclusion analyses. Working closely with technical team, partners, and Monitoring and Results Measurement (MRM) teams, the WEE Manager will drive the generation and use of evidence to support adaptive management, learning, and decision-making; oversee the development of gender-responsive Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) systems; and contribute to knowledge sharing, impact measurement, and external engagement to advance sustainable, inclusive, and scalable program Women Economic Empowerment outcomes. Essential Job Responsibilities VISION AND STRATEGY Set strategic direction and provide leadership for the program’s Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) agenda across target livestock trade corridors, ensuring women and youth are recognized, engaged, and benefit as key economic actors within livestock market systems. The role will strengthen the capacity of program teams and partners to integrate gender-transformative approaches across livestock value chains and supporting sectors, including animal health, feed and forage, livestock trade, business development services (BDS), and financial inclusion (FI). Lead the implementation and continuous refinement of the program’s Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) strategy, ensuring that gender-transformative approaches are effectively embedded across priority interventions and market system activities. Working closely with Corridor Managers, the Deputy Director/Technical Lead, the Investment Manager, and the NRM Lead, the role will provide technical oversight and strategic guidance to address systemic gender constraints, strengthen inclusive market outcomes, and enhance women’s participation, leadership, agency, and economic benefits within livestock market systems. Support the Program Leadership Team in engaging and influencing key stakeholders, including government institutions, private sector actors, development partners, donors, and civil society organizations, to advance the program’s WEE objectives. She/he will support strengthen multi-stakeholder partnerships, donor engagement and resource mobilization efforts directed to WEE, contribute to policy dialogue and advocacy initiatives, and promote collaborative actions that expand sustainable, inclusive, and market-driven economic opportunities for women. Lead the development and implementation of the GESI/WEE learning, evidence, and knowledge management agenda to support adaptive management, advocacy, and thought leadership. This includes refining annual learning priorities and questions based on emerging evidence and program needs; leading qualitative and quantitative analysis to inform decision-making, donor reporting, stakeholder engagement, and capacity strengthening; and overseeing the development of internal and external communication products that highlight WEE achievements, lessons, and impact. Promote innovation, learning, and adaptive management by identifying emerging opportunities, encouraging innovative approaches to overcome barriers to women’s economic participation, and fostering an environment where diverse perspectives are valued. The role will champion a culture of continuous learning, reflection, and evidence-based adaptation to strengthen program effectiveness and WEE outcomes TECHNICAL Leadership FOR IMPLEMENTATION Matrix accountability with program director for overall performance, quality, and results of RLP’s WEE and GESI portfolio across all countries and trade corridors Lead the implementation of Mercy Corps’ Global Minimum Standards for Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) across the RLP, ensuring consistent integration of GESI principles throughout program design, implementation, monitoring, and learning processes. Provide strategic and technical leadership for the design and implementation of GESI and Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) interventions, investments, and activities across all program components. Ensure interventions are informed by robust gender and social inclusion analyses, technically sound, market-driven, and aligned with donor requirements and recognized good practices. Set annual WEE strategic priorities with program director Guide and support program teams and partners to effectively integrate GESI considerations across interventions, ensuring women, men, youth, and other marginalized groups are meaningfully included, participate equitably, and benefit from program outcomes within livestock market systems. Strengthen the capacity of program teams, partners, and stakeholders through training, coaching, mentorship, and technical support to foster ownership of GESI and WEE approaches and promote the application of gender-transformative and inclusive development practices. Provide technical oversight for field monitoring, learning, and adaptive management related to GESI and WEE, including leading periodic qualitative reviews to assess progress, identify emerging opportunities and challenges, and inform strategic adjustments to interventions. Lead the analysis, interpretation, and use of sex-, age-, and diversity-disaggregated data to generate evidence, strengthen program learning, and inform WEE strategies, intervention design, partnership development, and adaptive management decisions. Contribute to high-quality donor and program reporting, ensuring that progress, lessons learned, and evidence of gender-transformative change, social inclusion, and inclusive market development outcomes are effectively documented and communicated. Champion the integration of GESI across program operations, systems, and organizational practices, ensuring that internal policies, procedures, and ways of working reflect inclusive and gender-responsive principles. Serve as the RLP Safeguarding Focal Point, promoting safeguarding awareness, strengthening compliance with Mercy Corps policies, supporting prevention and risk mitigation efforts, and ensuring safeguarding concerns are appropriately managed and addressed MANAGEMENT & COORDINATION Provide matrix management through technical supervision and mentorship of RLP’s GESI Focal Points and wider program team. Lead and coordinate cross-country GESI community of practice to share learning and best practices across corridors. Lead planning and coordination of WEE investments, in collaboration with budget holders to ensure GESI interventions are fully resourced. . Provide technical sign-off on WEE grants, investments and partnerships as appropriate Monitor value for money and effectiveness of WEE investments Ensure that program and country staff understand, are familiar with, and have the skills to contribute to the integration of Mercy Corps’ GESI Minimum Standards. Liaise with key external stakeholders to include their input on GESI, youth, and WEE perspectives in all aspects of program activities. Engage with the global GESI team and relevant internal communities of practice to share and benefit from lessons and best practices across the organization. EXTERNAL REPRESENTATION Identify strategic influence opportunities to represent RLP’s learning on GESI and MSD with donors, peers, policy makers, and private sector actors. Design compelling, evidence-based presentations and learning products to share externally Represent Mercy Corps and the program with donors and government and community leaders, as well as peer-oriented meetings and events, including in MSD and GESI-related networks and coordination bodies. Lead publication of regional learning products on GESI and MSD in close collaboration with the Director Evidence & Learning Resilient Dryland Production Systems Prepare and deliver presentations to stakeholders about program approaches, best practices, and learnings related to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion. Security Work closely with the country team’s security focal point to promote and maintain systems that promote the safety and security of all team members. Ensure that gender specific needs and interests of program staff in relation to safety and security are identified and responded to appropriately. SAFEGUARDING Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options. Supervisory Responsibility Provides matrix leadership, technical supervision, performance input, and work-planning oversight to GESI focal points and relevant technical staff across Kenya, Ethiopia, and Somalia. Accountability Reports Directly To: Program Director Works Directly with RLP Staff including: Within the RLP : Deputy Director/Technical Lead, Monitoring and Results Measurement Manager, Director of Evidence & Learning RDPS, Trade Corridor managers, Inclusive Finance and Investment Manager, and the Communication and Knowledge Management Manager and wider RLP program team. National, Regional and Global : S/He will collaborate with the National Gender advisor(s) within the 3 countries if that role exists, the Regional Gender Advisor, and Global GESI and MSD technical advisors and MEL team members for strategic support to the RLP, her/his own professional growth, and to share insights and progress to others in Mercy Corps and beyond. To Beneficiaries Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our beneficiaries and to international standards guiding international relief and development work, while actively engaging beneficiary communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs and MC's policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues. Minimum Qualifications & Transferable Skills Master’s degree in Gender Studies, Social Sciences, Development Studies, Economics, Rural Development, Agricultural Economics, Livestock sector or a related field, with at least 10 years of relevant professional experience, including 5 years in a senior GESI/Women’s Economic Empowerment (WEE) leadership role. Experience in Market Systems Development (MSD), livestock value chains, and/or private sector development is highly preferred. Proven experience leading the design and implementation of GESI and WEE strategies within large development programs, with demonstrated success in integrating gender and youth into livestock market systems, and economic development programming. Strong experience working with the private sector to identify, test, and scale innovative business models, technologies, and market-based solutions that address barriers to women’s and youth’s economic participation and empowerment. Demonstrated experience working on matrix teams and managing staff and budgets. Demonstrated ability to build the capacity and commitment of program teams, partners, government institutions, and other stakeholders to apply gender-transformative approaches and promote women’s economic empowerment. Proven technical leadership in the design, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, and learning of GESI/WEE interventions, including mentoring multidisciplinary teams and supporting adaptive management processes, preferably within an international NGO or donor-funded program. Experience implementing women’s economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, youth employment, and livelihoods programs, preferably in pastoralist and agro-pastoralist contexts. Experience in the Horn of Africa is highly desirable. Strong analytical and learning skills, including the ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and utilize qualitative and quantitative data to inform strategy, learning, advocacy, and decision-making. Experience working with major donors such as SDC, Sida, AFD, the World Bank, and similar development partners, including donor compliance, reporting, and stakeholder engagement. Excellent facilitation, communication, networking, and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence diverse audiences and foster collaboration across sectors. Strong organizational, problem-solving, and adaptive management skills, with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver results in complex and evolving environments. Demonstrated cultural sensitivity, diplomacy, and ability to work effectively within multicultural and multidisciplinary teams. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. Willingness and ability to travel regularly to field locations (30-50%) as required Success Factors The successful Women Economic Empowerment Manager will have strong technical skills combined with strategic visioning and leadership. She/He must operate with diplomatic tenacity to advocate for the prioritization of women’s economic empowerment programming across all RLP intervention areas and with public/private partners. She/He will have an outstanding ability to inspire teams to deeply understand gender and youth dynamics and integrate this understanding into activities that enhance program impact and take the program to new levels. She/He will also have proven experience with cross-cultural teams and capacity building, individual staff development, and strong mentoring skills. She/He will have demonstrated ability to follow procedures and meet deadlines with flexibility and creativity in planning and problem solving. The Manager will have proven ability to learn quickly, multi-task, prioritize, take initiative and be accountable for results. The most successful Mercy Corps staff members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments, and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations. Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions The position will be based either in Nairobi, Addis Ababa, Jijiga, Mogadishu, Hargeisa, or Kismayo. The position requires a minimum of 30% travel to support implementation teams and stakeholder engagement. Travel will include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited. This role does not include expatriate benefits or work authorization. Ongoing Learning In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development. Team Engagement and Effectiveness Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work. We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to the Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme . As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. job_description: About the Company We're a plaintiff's catastrophic contingency fee law firm with specialized units in mass tort and medical malpractice. Our mission, echoing our founder's guiding principle: " to win the case that can't be won, for the family who can't afford to lose. " Unlike traditional personal injury firms, we exclusively handle catastrophic injury and wrongful death cases. We prepare every case for trial, recognizing that clients with devastating injuries have fundamentally different needs than those with moderate injuries. Our Trial Lawyers fully litigate each matter with unwavering dedication. Our clients are individuals across the United States fighting David vs. Goliath battles against powerful corporations. We level the playing field in these underdog contests, representing people, never companies. Rather than focusing on personal injury, we deliver personal victory: helping clients reclaim their lives when justice is finally served. Our landmark victories include $60 million against General Motors, $82 million against Celsius Holdings, and $27 million for a pressure cooker explosion. Named " Personal Injury Law Firm of the Year " three consecutive years, we're featured on CNN, CBS News, and recognized by Best Lawyers, Super Lawyers, and U.S. News & World Report. OUR COMPANY VALUES guide our team and shape our culture: 🤝All Hands on Deck: We win as a team, stepping up for colleagues regardless of formal role boundaries. ⚡Walk Fast: The work matters, so we stay organized and advance cases daily without delay. 🚘Drive All Night: We do whatever it takes — our commitment is our competitive edge. ✨Stand Out: We create exceptional client experiences through meticulous, memorable work. 🔍Don't Forget the Basics: We master the details, because a single oversight can change someone's life. We're a fully remote organization with 50-60 professionals working in nimble, high-performing teams of 3-8 people. Headquartered in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, our talent spans across the United States—with Attorneys in California and Chicago—plus international team members in the Philippines, Pakistan, Nigeria. Kenya, Mexico, Colombia and Brazil. Our environment isn't about making money; it's about saving lives. We handle catastrophic cases where the stakes couldn't be higher, creating an intensity and purpose we embrace. Every detail matters profoundly; even a single typo can affect a client's outcome. This creates a workplace where your contribution directly changes lives, offering a sense of purpose rarely found elsewhere. About the Role We're looking for a remote Legal Project/Program Manager to build and run the operational backbone of our litigation division, a team managing a few hundred active cases across five American cities. In this role, you'll audit our current systems, rebuild workflows, and manage the day-to-day production machine so our Lawyers can focus on winning cases. This isn't about tweaking a well-oiled system; you're building one from messy foundations, with the full support of firm leadership and Trial Lawyers . This role is internally facing; you won't be client-facing yourself, though the people you manage are. Right now, the firm's ability to take on more cases and reach more families is held back by operational capacity rather than by demand or will. This position exists to close that gap. Our IDEAL CANDIDATE brings 6+ years of relevant project or program management experience, whether that's a legal-specific background in plaintiff's contingency fee law or mass tort (with or without legal PM certifications), or project management experience built more broadly in professional services. Experience managing a group of Paralegals across that kind of caseload counts too, even without an exact title match, and you don't need to be a lawyer to succeed here, just a clear read on complexity and how to move work through people. You're the kind of presence that makes a team feel instantly more "pro": you walk into a meeting, quickly diagnose what's broken, and lay out a fix people trust. You lead like a head coach, not just executing the work yourself but running the team around you so everyone's playing their position well, and you understand the stakes go beyond this team: get this right, and it opens the door for the firm to expand into new cities and help more people. Performance Metrics: Your performance will be measured by how smoothly operations run, how quickly incidents get resolved with lasting fixes, how well the firm can scale capacity while maintaining quality, and the accuracy of your forecasting in preventing problems before they surface. Reporting Structure: You'll be in the Litigation division, working closely with Paralegals , Legal Assistants , Intake Specialists , Associate Attorneys , and other members of the firm leadership team. This position reports directly to the Attorney . You'll be doing things like: System Audit & Process Redesign: evaluating current workflows; identifying bottlenecks; restructuring roles and processes to support scalability; documenting new processes as standard operating procedures Tooling & Technology: upgrading the firm's project management stack, including new platforms; using the case management system to track case progress; leveraging AI tools for documentation and workflow efficiency Project-Level Coordination & Troubleshooting (per case) : coordinating the full team behind each case from intake through trial; keeping cases on schedule; troubleshooting delays; refining workflows to prevent recurring issues Program-Level Management (across the full caseload) : tracking case statuses across active programs; surfacing status data and dashboards for leadership; monitoring team capacity and staffing needs to keep pace with caseload; forecasting bottlenecks before they surface Team Communication & Cadence: running regular huddles and meeting cadences with project leads; keeping attorneys and leadership updated on progress Financial Tracking & Reporting: tracking and reporting cost per project Hiring & Resourcing Strategy: collaborating on expansion planning into new cities; defining new roles needed to support that growth; participating in vetting candidates to confirm fit Skills & Qualifications 6+ years of experience in a legal-specific project/program management role (e.g., Legal Project Manager , Mass Tort Manager ), or in a Program Manager , Project Manager , or Operations Manager role within high-volume professional services more broadly — legal or plaintiff's-side experience is a plus, not a requirement Project or program management experience with demonstrated success in building or overhauling systems Strong analytical skills: forecasting, capacity planning, resource optimization Experience managing high-volume, lifecycle-driven projects in deadline-driven, high-stakes environments Tech-savvy, comfortable learning and implementing new platforms quickly Extremely organized with sharp attention to process and detail Problem-solver who spots issues early and implements fixes Excellent written and verbal communication in English Diplomatic with strong EQ Skilled at driving process change while operations stay fully up and running Skilled at building buy-in across teams without formal authority over them Comfortable operating in ambiguous, still-forming environments without a playbook already in place Bonus if you also have: Legal project management certification (PMP, Legal Lean Sigma Green Belt or higher, IILPM LPP or higher, AIPM CPPM or higher, LPM Institute Advanced Certification) Experience in plaintiff's contingency fee law or mass tort settings Background managing paralegal or legal operations teams American-based law firm or legal organization experience Bilingual capabilities (English/Spanish or English/Creole) A law degree (even without practicing law) Experience with AI and automation tools for documentation and workflows Familiarity with our tools: LeadDocket, Zoom, MS Office suite, MS Outlook, OneDrive, Dropbox, ChatGPT Position Details Working Hours: 8:30 AM–5:00 PM ET (Eastern Time), with a 1-hour break. Our Vision We believe in a world where everyone, regardless of their country’s wealth or frontiers, enjoys access to medicines and healthcare when they need it. Our Mission We work tirelessly to remove access barriers faced by patients and caregivers across Low and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs) when seeking quality medicines and quality healthcare. Who We Are: Accelerating access to medicines for all Imagine a world where critical medicines are within reach, affordable, and synonymous with quality, no matter where you are. That is the world we're building with our unique, demand-aggregation model that unites healthcare providers across LMICs. At the heart of our identity is a single, resolute commitment: to build a future where geography and income never stand between any individual and life-saving medicines. Our platform isn't merely a space for transactions, we unlock affordable access to medicines by aggregating demand across healthcare providers. We also help manufacturers build a sustainable and reliable global access strategy. Our business focuses on low- and middle-income countries and strengthens the purchasing power of these markets to ensure the supply of cost-effective, high-quality medicines. We partner exclusively with authorized, high-quality pharmaceutical companies and certified caregivers to accelerate sustainable access to medicines. About the Position: Axmed is building a B2B marketplace that changes how quality medicines are procured across low and middle income countries (LMICs), alongside logistics SaaS and trade financing that connect healthcare providers, governments, NGOs and pharmaceutical manufacturers through one data-driven platform. Quality is the promise that makes the marketplace work: buyers need to trust every product and every supplier on it. As Quality Lead you are the hands-on owner of day-to-day quality assurance and quality control operations. You will run external audits and quality checks in the system to prevent issues, maintain and improve the Quality Management System (QMS), write and update SOPs, manage CAPAs, qualify suppliers and products, and keep Axmed ready for regulatory and customer audits. You will work closely with Commercial, Operations, Tech, Legal and Regulatory colleagues to make quality practical for a lean, remote-first team, and you will report to the Head of Quality once that role is filled. What you'll own Run quality assurance day to day: supplier and product quality checks, documentation review, consignment release and non-conformance handling in line with GDP and GMP principles. Support internal and external audits and inspections: prepare documentation, assess current processes against requirements, advise on readiness plans, and recommend and track corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) through to closure. Develop and maintain SOPs so they reflect WHO MQAS and Good Distribution Practice (GDP) standards and how Axmed works. Monitor and improve the QMS: evaluate the existing system, recommend improvements aligned to industry standards, and work with stakeholders to implement them. Qualify and monitor suppliers and logistics partners: collect and review quality documentation, run risk assessments and support supplier audits. Design and deliver training on GDP and quality systems at axmed for internal teams, and maintain the records that demonstrate compliance. Provide ongoing, practical regulatory and quality guidance to Commercial, Tech, Legal and Regulatory colleagues, and stay current with evolving guidance so processes keep pace. Skills: Hands-on application of GDP and GMP in a pharmaceutical, medical device or health supply chain setting. Particular focus to WHO MQAS framework. Working knowledge of stringent regulatory authority quality requirements (FDA, EMA or Swissmedic) and WHO guidance, and how they apply to distribution and procurement. SOP writing, document control, deviation and CAPA management, and QMS maintenance (ISO 9001, ISO 13485 or equivalent). Strong and consistent digital and AI exposure Audit preparation and execution: internal audits, supplier audits and supporting regulatory or customer inspections. Clear written and verbal communication; able to simplify complex regulatory topics into accessible guidance and training. Experience 4 to 7 years in quality assurance or quality control, ideally within pharma, medical devices or health supply chain. Demonstrated hands-on execution: audits, quality checks, documentation, GDP or GMP application, rather than oversight only. Experience operating with limited internal infrastructure, for example in a lean team, a startup or a field-based supply chain role. Experience preparing for regulatory audits and inspections. Exposure to humanitarian or global health supply chain organisations, or to a Swiss or European pharma distributor, is a strong plus. Experience designing and delivering compliance training is also valued. Traits Self-starting and organised: comfortable owning a quality workload end to end without a large team around them. Pragmatic and risk-based, with high attention to detail where it matters. Collaborative and approachable; makes quality feel like support rather than policing. Adaptable to remote, asynchronous working across time zones. Digital first Right to Work: As an early-stage company, we are not currently able to offer visa sponsorship or relocation support. For this reason, candidates must already have the legal right to work in the country where they are based. What is in it for you? At Axmed, we believe in creating a supportive and rewarding environment where our team can thrive. Here’s what we offer: Unlimited PTO : Take the time you need to recharge and maintain work-life balance. Monthly wellness allowance : Prioritize your health and well-being with extra support. Paid parental leave : Time off to bond with your new family member without any added stress. Flexible working hours : Enjoy the freedom to structure your workday in a way that suits your lifestyle. Annual off-site retreats : Connect with the team and build lasting relationships during our company retreats. Fully remote work : Work from anywhere in the world and join our distributed team. The opportunity to make a difference : Be part of a mission-driven company working to improve healthcare equity. Competitive salaries : We offer a compensation package that reflects your skills and experience. Plenty of room for growth : We believe in nurturing talent and offering opportunities for professional development and advancement.

job_title: Terms of Reference – Baseline, Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems & Pathways (STEP) in Kenya
job_description: Kenya Terms of Reference – Baseline, Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems & Pathways (STEP) in Kenya Organization World University Service of Canada Posted 4 Sep 2026 Closing date 13 Sep 2026 Introduction World University Service of Canada (WUSC) is a leading Canadian international development organization focusing on three programmatic areas: Economic Opportunities, Education, and Empowerment. Our vision is a better world for all young people. It is a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable world in which all young people, especially women, persons with disabilities (PWD) and marginalized youth from refugees and host communities, are empowered to secure a good quality life for themselves, their families, and their communities. WUSC currently works in 25 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America, with an annual budget of approximately CAD $50 million. Globally, we partner with a network of higher education institutions, civil society organizations, private sector partners, professionals, students, volunteers, faculty, and community leaders who help us achieve our mission. Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems And Pathways (step) Project Description The Strengthen Skills Training Ecosystems & Pathways in Kenya (STEP) project is a seven-year initiative implemented by the World University Service of Canada (WUSC). The project aims to improve the economic well-being of displaced and host community youth in Kenya, with a focus on refugee and host populations in Kakuma, Kalobeyei (Turkana County), and Dadaab (Garissa County). STEP seeks to strengthen pathways to employment, entrepreneurship, and digital livelihoods by supporting market-responsive Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), enhancing inclusive entrepreneurship ecosystems, expanding access to digital work opportunities, and addressing systemic barriers affecting youth economic inclusion. The project aims to contribute to positive change for over 10,000 youth, with at least 60% being young women and approximately 70% being refugees or displaced persons. It will do so by strengthening the capacities of ecosystem actors including Refugee-Led Organizations (RLOs), Women’s Rights Organizations (WROs), Organization of Persons with Disabilities (OPD), Entrepreneurship Support Organizations (ESOs), TVET institutions, employers, and government agencies. The project is grounded in a Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), Safeguarding and Human Rights-Based Approach, recognizing intersecting vulnerabilities faced by young women, persons with disabilities, persons with diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC), and other marginalized groups. Purpose of the Baseline The purpose of the STEP project's baseline study is to support key stakeholders in defining, measuring and documenting the project's achievements in terms of a set of expected outcomes. Further, it aims to empower stakeholders to collaboratively measure progress towards them, review achievements, and adapt strategies as needed and appropriate. Specific Objectives Aligned with this purpose, the baseline study will achieve the following specific objectives: Validate Theory of Change (TOC)Assumptions: Assess pre-implementation contexts and integrate the perspectives and experiences of diverse community members, including women, young youth, PWD, marginalized groups, refugees and host communities to validate the ToC assumptions, gaining insight into community members' perspectives and experiences to inform and refine the overall program implementation strategy. Gather quantitative and qualitative insights from community members to validate the assumptions within the project’s ToC, allowing for the revision and refinement of the program design where appropriate. job_title: PropTech & SaaS Sales and Business Development
job_description: About the Role We are a fast-growing technology company scaling innovative software solutions across East Africa. We are looking for a hungry, adaptable, and tech-savvy Sales Executive to drive our market penetration. In this role, you will wear two hats: driving adoption of our cutting-edge PropTech solutions among real estate developers and property managers, and selling our high-value AI CRM SaaS to medical clinics, healthcare providers, and other targeted sectors in Nairobi. If you understand complex software sales, love closing deals, and can speak the language of both property magnates and medical professionals, we want you on our team. Key Responsibilities Market Expansion: Identify, pitch, and close B2B software contracts with real estate firms, property management agencies, medical clinics, and allied businesses in Nairobi. PropTech Portfolio Sales: Sell our proprietary property technology ecosystem (tenant portals, automated leasing, property accounting, and smart-building integrations) to real estate stakeholders. AI CRM SaaS Sales: Demonstrate and sell our workflow-automating AI CRM to medical clinics and service providers, emphasizing patient management, automated booking, and retention analytics. Tech-Savvy: Deep understanding of CRM tools (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce), SaaS pricing models, and a high comfort level explaining AI/automation features to non-tech buyers. Communication Skills: Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills in English and Swahili. Exceptional negotiation and objection-handling prowess. Drive & Attitude: Self-starter mentality, resilient under pressure, target-driven, and capable of working with minimal supervision in a fast-paced startup environment. What We Offer Competitive Compensation: Base salary plus an aggressive, uncapped commission structure tied to closed MRR (Monthly Recurring Revenue). Growth Opportunity: Be part of an early-stage expansion team with clear pathways to heading up vertical sales units. job_title: Agile Scrum Master Senior Analyst- Cigna Healthcare
job_description: Job Role: Scrum Master/Agile Team Coach About Cigna Cigna is a global health insurance company, dedicated to its mission of helping improve the health, well-being, and peace of mind of those we serve by making health care simple, affordable, and predictable. Together with colleagues located across Europe, Asia Pacific, the Middle East, Africa, and India, you will support Cigna's International Health business. As part of Cigna Healthcare, International Health provides global and local health insurance solutions for internationally mobile individuals, multinational organizations, government entities, IGOs, NGOs, and local customers worldwide. We are going through a global Agile transformation. As a result, we are expanding our teams and are looking for experienced Scrum Masters / Agile Team Coaches to join our team. Purpose of the Role The purpose of the Scrum Master / Agile Team Coach role is to maximize value delivery through collaboration, impediment removal, visibility, learning, and evidence-based improvement. This role supports high-performing team dynamics, sustainable delivery, continuous flow, and self-managed teams that are shaping and maturing Agile ways of working across International Health. About The Role The Scrum Master / Agile Team Coach is a team coach and servant leader who facilitates change through the adoption and application of Agile principles, practices, and frameworks. The role enables teams to self-organize, improve flow, embrace effective ways of working, and consistently deliver value outcomes to stakeholders. The role partners closely with Product Owners, team members, Release Train Engineers, Agile Product Managers, and other stakeholders to support predictable delivery and continuous improvement. This is a Band 3 Contributor Career Track Role. Key Responsibilities Team Coaching and Agile Enablement Provide coaching and guidance to Agile Teams and support the adoption and application of Agile values, principles, and practices. Act as a servant leader, facilitator, mentor, and coach for individuals and teams. Enable teams to improve collaboration, transparency, psychological safety, accountability, and self-management. Use effective communication and listening skills to teach, coach, mentor, and support healthy team interactions. Foster a healthy working culture, build strong relationships, and strengthen key interactions across teams and stakeholders. Delivery Flow and Continuous Improvement Support teams in improving flow, reducing bottlenecks, managing impediments, and operating at a sustainable pace. Help teams establish realistic and achievable delivery commitments based on capacity, clarity, dependencies, and delivery risks. Maintain metrics and data necessary to provide visibility into maturity, progress, quality, flow, predictability, and value delivery. Facilitate evidence-based improvement through retrospectives, improvement actions, and follow-through on agreed outcomes. Encourage Built-In Quality, continuous learning, and relentless improvement as part of day-to-day team working practices. Facilitation and Cadence Events Support and facilitate team ceremonies and cadence events that drive progress toward value delivery and business outcomes. Facilitate team events such as planning, team syncs, backlog refinement, reviews, retrospectives, and improvement workshops, as applicable to the team context. Participate in Sync events, Scrum Master / Team Coach forums, and internal Agile communities of practice. Support ART-level alignment events, including PI Planning, ART Sync, Coach Sync, System Demo, and Inspect & Adapt, as applicable. ART Alignment, Dependencies, and Impediments Provide support that helps Agile Teams improve overall ART performance through collaboration and alignment between team objectives, vision, and strategic themes. Facilitate and support dependency management to ensure alignment of delivery across teams. Support removal of impediments that hinder achievement of team goals and objectives. Protect the team from unnecessary disruptions and external distractions while escalating systemic impediments in a timely manner. Collaborate with Product Owners, RTEs, Agile Product Managers, business stakeholders, and technology partners to maintain transparency and alignment. Success in this Role Teams demonstrate stronger self-management, collaboration, and ownership of delivery outcomes. Impediments, blockers, dependencies, and delivery risks are made visible and addressed promptly. Team ceremonies and cadence events are purposeful, outcome-focused, and continuously improved. Metrics and qualitative insights are used to improve flow, predictability, quality, and stakeholder transparency. Teams operate at a sustainable pace while maintaining alignment with ART priorities and International Health business outcomes. Continuous improvement becomes embedded in the team culture. Required Qualifications / Skills / Experience Certified Scrum Master (CSM), SAFe Scrum Master, SAFe Advanced Scrum Master, Professional Scrum Master, or equivalent Agile certification. At least 4 years of proven experience as a Scrum Master/Agile Team Coach role. Experience facilitating team development and continuous improvement initiatives. Strong knowledge of Lean-Agile principles, Scrum practices, Kanban practices, and team-level Agile delivery. Experience with Scaled Agile Framework (SAFe) and understanding of its principles and practices. Excellent communication, facilitation, coaching, mentoring, and conflict resolution skills. Ability to work effectively with cross-functional and geographically distributed teams. Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and organizational skills. Ability to manage priorities in a changing environment and support teams working under delivery deadlines. Ability to interact with Subject matter experts, Product Owners, Agile Product Managers, and stakeholders in a matrix structure. Knowledge of IT concepts, software delivery lifecycle, delivery methodologies, architecture considerations, and technical standards. Desired Qualifications / Skills / Experience Working knowledge of Jira, Confluence, Mural, or similar collaboration tools. Experience supporting product, platform, operational, or service-based delivery teams. Experience facilitating organizational change and Agile transformation initiatives. Experience in software development lifecycle, IT delivery, product delivery, or project management. About Cigna Healthcare Cigna Healthcare, a division of The Cigna Group, is an advocate for better health through every stage of life. Our tagline, “We Keep Our Word,” reflects our unwavering commitment to integrity, transparency, and delivering on our promises to our clients, partners, and communities. CIC Group is passionate about innovation, digital transformation, and inclusive insurance solutions that meet the evolving needs of cooperatives, SMEs, corporates, and individuals. About the Role Reporting to the Underwriting Manager, the role will support the acquisition and onboarding of Group Life business by preparing accurate quotations in line with approved pricing requirements, completing KYC/AML checks, setting up scheme records and ensuring complete handover to the Underwriting Manager. Key Responsibilities Receive and review quotation requests to confirm that the required member data, benefits and supporting information have been provided. Prepare Group Life quotations accurately and within the agreed turnaround times. Ensure quotations comply with approved products, rates, pricing tools, underwriting guidelines and authority limits. Verify quotation calculations, benefits, commissions, taxes and other applicable charges before release. Escalate non-standard benefits, pricing exceptions and complex risks to the relevant underwriter or manager. Register and track quotation requests, revisions, outcomes and conversion status. Review onboarding documents, including accepted quotations, proposal forms, member schedules, premium evidence and intermediary documents. Perform KYC, AML and sanctions screening and escalate incomplete or adverse findings. Follow up on outstanding onboarding requirements before the scheme is handed over for underwriting. Create the scheme folder in SharePoint and upload all required documents using the approved naming and filing standards. Prepare a complete onboarding pack and hand over the scheme to the Underwriting Manager for allocation. Prepare reports on quotations, turnaround times, conversion rates, production, acquisition pipeline, onboarding status and KYC/AML compliance. Maintain accurate records of pending quotations, incomplete onboarding requirements and ageing items. Support process improvement, quotation automation and enhancement of acquisition and onboarding controls. Ensure confidentiality of member, salary, pricing and other sensitive information. Who We’re Looking For Essential Knowledge/Skills and Experience Required: Degree in actuarial Science, BCOM Insurance, Statistics or a business related degree Progress in Diploma in Insurance 4 years’ relevant work experience in Group Life Underwriting or similar role Good knowledge of group underwriting Analytical skills Attention to detail Technology oriented with interest in emerging technologies like AI and ML Exceptional Interpersonal skills Why Join Us? Joining CIC Insurance Group as a Business Acquisition Specialist offers an exciting opportunity to play a pivotal role in converting business opportunities into sustainable growth within the Group Life business. You will be at the heart of the acquisition journey, managing quotation preparation, client onboarding, KYC/AML compliance, and seamless handover to underwriting while ensuring accuracy, speed, and a strong customer experience. The role provides valuable exposure to Group Life products, pricing, underwriting processes, intermediary relationships, and acquisition analytics, while also offering opportunities to contribute to automation and continuous process improvement. Reporting to: Senior Programme Manager, Professional Pathways Pillar Closing Date: 21 September 2026, midday (EAT) Start Date: 19 October 2026 (desired) but flexible About The Refugee-Led Research Hub The Refugee-Led Research Hub (RLRH) supports individuals with lived experience of displacement to become leaders in fields related to human rights, forced migration, humanitarian response and development, politics, and law, among other areas. We do so by delivering academic and professional development programming to a global cohort of students who have been affected by displacement—as refugees, asylum seekers, IDPs, stateless, and beyond—supporting access to graduate degrees and advanced career opportunities. RLRH also creates opportunities for researchers with displacement backgrounds to lead primary and secondary research studies, from start to finish. RLRH’s team is comprised of colleagues who are deeply committed to advancing refugee leadership, the majority of whom have lived experience of displacement. Our network of staff, researchers, students, and other affiliates is made up of 1,400+ individuals across 80+ countries. RLRH has six active offices: our first was established in Nairobi in 2020, we have had an office at the University of Oxford since 2021, and we have since developed physical hubs in Kakuma refugee camp (Kenya), Kuala Lumpur (Malaysia), Kampala (Uganda), and in the Oxfordshire community (UK). From October 2025 RLRH is funded to serve as a technical partner for the Mastercard Foundations Scholars Program network, advancing an ambitious global agenda to support displacement-affected learners to access 1,000+ graduate-level scholarships at partner universities around the world. RLRH provides expert guidance and implements specialised programmes to help these learners enter university, thrive on course, and pursue meaningful and enduring careers on completion of their degrees. A complementary, refugee-led research agenda designed by RLRH colleagues produces insights to help Scholars Program partner universities and other stakeholders accelerate positive, long-lasting systems change. The Role Overview Of The Professional Pathways Pillar The Professional Pathways Pillar (PPP) supports individuals with displacement backgrounds to access career opportunities. We work most closely with RLRH affiliates who have completed our academic and research programmes and other students who have completed or are pursuing postgraduate degrees at partner universities. We also collaborate closely with allied organisations and universities to systematically strengthen the inclusion of refugees in the workforce. RLRH’s people-centred career advancement programming brings to life our vision of creating transformative refugee leadership in impactful professional settings throughout the world. We deliver three main interventions: Foundationally, we provide individualised career counselling to RLRH affiliates at any stage in their journey, helping them to identify career pathways that are well suited to their personal and professional skills, experiences, and aspirations. To build out core professional skills, we run a stipended six-month, in-person advanced traineeship for degree completers, which combines foundational professional training with deep mentorship. This is currently run in three of RLRH’s offices – in Kampala, Kakuma, and Nairobi, with plans for future expansion – in collaboration with our Research Pillar. To develop meaningful and sustained pathways, we facilitate paid external professional placements with values-aligned partnered employers who are active and influential across various sectors of interest to RLRH affiliates. Placements provide a supportive environment for affiliates to establish themselves in the workforce, building skills and profiles that will serve them for years to come. On top of our existing global footprint, the PPP will grow in the coming years in collaboration with the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, with the aim of supporting African graduates across 20+ universities worldwide to transition to meaningful employment soon after completion of their degrees. By 2028, the programme expects to have enrolled 110 African displacement-affected graduates in the traineeship across RLRH’s physical hubs and facilitate 130 professional placements with employer partners. Overview Of Position The Transitions Manager is responsible for the design and delivery of the PPP’s professional development and employability support services for graduates affected by forced displacement. The postholder will develop and implement a portfolio of career readiness activities that prepare affiliates to successfully transition into placements, fellowships, employment opportunities, and other career pathways. Combining strategic programme development with direct affiliate support, this is a dynamic role involving the delivery of high-quality online and in-person career coaching, group workshops, and application support. Through these activities, the postholder will equip affiliates with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to navigate the barriers frequently faced by refugee and displaced professionals pursuing meaningful career opportunities. The postholder will draw on their expertise, alongside insights from RLRH affiliates and university and employer partners to inform the expansion and strengthening of the PPP’s professional development services. As this area of work grows, the Transitions Manager will play a vital role in supporting the development and management of a broader careers function, contributing to staff supervision and the professional development of junior colleagues. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced careers or employability professional to build and lead a growing area of RLRH's transition to employment work. Working closely with Professional Pathways team members, they will help create innovative and impactful services that support refugee and displaced graduates to pursue and achieve their long-term career goals. Responsibilities Professional development services design and improvement (35%) Lead the design of professional development services for RLRH affiliates, piloting workshops, practical resources and application support sessions. Produce and maintain clear documentation outlining programme design and implementation. Use participant engagement, feedback, and emerging needs to inform the continuous improvement of professional development services. Keep abreast of labour market trends and placement opportunities to inform programme content and participant guidance. Participant support and delivery (35%) Deliver 1:1 career coaching to programme participants. Facilitate group-based workshops and employability sessions. Lead the onboarding and induction of participants into placements and other Professional Pathways Pillar programmes. Match affiliates to relevant opportunities and provide career readiness support. Collaborate with PPP colleagues and Research Facilitators to support Graduate Trainees and placement participants. Technical expertise and external guidance (15%) Work closely with the PPP’s Partnerships Manager to provide technical support to professional transitions leads at Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program universities and other allied institutions. Deliver transitions-related workshops with university partners to master’s graduates who have been affected by displacement. Supervise and support incoming RLRH Careers Advisors as the portfolio of professional development services expands. Operations and administration (10%) Maintain case management systems and participant records to track professional development progress and outcomes. Other duties as assigned (5%) Attend PPP team meetings and contribute to planning and coordination activities. Undertake additional responsibilities aligned with the role’s purpose and organisational priorities, as directed by the PPP’s Senior Programme Manager. Selection criteria Essential A bachelor’s degree in education, human resources, social sciences, international development or a related field, or equivalent professional experience in career development. Significant experience in careers guidance, employability, professional development, career coaching, talent development, or workforce transitions. Demonstrated experience designing and delivering employability, professional development or career readiness programmes. Demonstrated experience delivering workshops, group learning programmes and 1:1 career coaching. Experience working with refugees, displaced populations, or other individuals facing barriers to employment, education, or professional progression. Experience maintaining participant records and using CRM, database, or case management systems to support programme delivery Demonstrated knowledge of labour market trends, recruitment processes, and career pathways, particularly within the African context. Excellent interpersonal and relationship management skills, with experience working across diverse teams. Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently. Commitment to inclusion, equity, and affiliate-centred practice and programming. Excellent cultural competency and cultural humility. Excellent written and verbal English. Desirable A master’s degree in a relevant field of studies. Experience working within nonprofit, higher education, and/or international development environments. Experience working across multiple regions, particularly in LMIC contexts. Fluency in additional languages spoken by RLRH learners and affiliates, such as French, Swahili, Arabic, Amharic, Somali, and/or Oromo. Demonstrated experience supervising, mentoring, or supporting the professional development of colleagues. Professional qualification in career guidance, coaching, counselling, learning and development or related fields. Applicants are expected to have or obtain the right to work in Kenya. job_title: Strategic Content and Storytelling Manager - Africa Region
job_description: What We Can Achieve Together The Content Strategy & Storytelling Manager is responsible for shaping and driving TNC Africa Region's content vision, editorial strategy, and storytelling agenda. This role serves as the primary architect of compelling narratives that showcase conservation impact, elevate partner and community voices, strengthen donor engagement, expand influence, and deepen audience connection with the organization's mission across Africa. This is a highly specialized content leadership position requiring exceptional editorial judgment, narrative development expertise, and demonstrated experience translating complex conservation, scientific, and community-based work into compelling stories that inspire action and support. Through exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and production, this role will help TNC Africa demonstrate conservation impact and deepen connections with strategic stakeholders and audiences. The position leads the development of strategic content plans and manages the end-to-end storytelling process, from story identification and field reporting to writing, editing, multimedia production, publishing, and performance analysis. The role collaborates closely with conservation, policy, philanthropy, and Marketing and Communications experts, both regionally and globally, to ensure content aligns with organizational priorities and engages audiences through powerful, authentic, and evidence-based storytelling. In partnership with creative agencies, photographers, and videographers, the incumbent will identify, develop, produce, and publish high-quality storytelling assets. Nature.org will be the primary delivery platform, complemented by video productions, blogs, podcasts, photo stories, and other creative multimedia formats. The role reports to the Director Marketing & Communications - Africa and shall be based in any country where TNC has offices, in Kenya, Tanzania, Gabon, Zambia, South Africa, Angola. No employment visas or assistance is being offered with this position except for the local labour employment requirements. We’re Looking For You Are you a strong writer, editor, producer, and creative storyteller who can transform complex conservation science into clear and memorable content? Are you excited by the opportunity to report from some of Africa’s irreplaceable landscapes, work with partners, communities, and conservation teams, create donor-focused stories, and help expand influence in written, visual, video, and audio formats? We are looking for someone with excellent editorial judgment, a strong portfolio, and the ability to manage content from initial idea through publication. By joining the Africa Marketing and Communications team, you will help bring our Big 5 Irreplaceable Landscapes story to life and connect donors with the people, places, and conservation outcomes their support makes possible. Role Scope & Key responsibilities Content Strategy & Editorial Leadership Develop and own the Africa content and storytelling strategy aligned with regional priorities, conservation objectives, philanthropic engagement goals, and organizational brand standards. Establish an editorial vision and annual storytelling roadmap that identifies priority themes, narratives, audiences, and content opportunities across Africa. Lead content planning processes to ensure a consistent pipeline of high-impact stories throughout the year. Define storytelling frameworks, editorial standards, voice, tone, and content governance practices. Advise leadership and program teams on strategic storytelling approaches that strengthen audience engagement and showcase impact. Identify emerging stories, trends, and content opportunities that support regional priorities and strategic objectives. Story Development & Narrative Creation Serve as the lead storyteller, writer, and editor for the Africa region. Identify, source, research, and develop compelling stories from landscapes, communities, Indigenous Peoples, conservation practitioners, scientists, donors, partners, and staff. Transform complex scientific, technical, and conservation information into clear, engaging, audience-centered narratives. Produce feature stories, long-form articles, case studies, donor stories, scripts, blogs, and impact reports. Conduct interviews and gather firsthand information to build authentic, evidence-based narratives. Ensure all content reflects diverse voices, local perspectives, and ethical storytelling practices. Multimedia Storytelling & Content Production Lead the conception and development of multimedia storytelling projects, including video, photography, audio, and digital content. Travel to field sites to conduct reporting, interviews, story gathering, and content production activities. Develop creative briefs and storytelling concepts for visual and multimedia projects. Collaborate with photographers, videographers, designers, editors, and production partners to produce high-quality storytelling assets. Oversee content production workflows and ensure consistency with editorial and storytelling objectives. Maintain a library of approved stories, photographs, video assets, and supporting content resources. Audience Engagement & Content Performance Monitor content effectiveness using audience insights, analytics, and engagement metrics. Evaluate storytelling performance across channels and recommend improvements based on data and audience behavior. Apply audience research and engagement data to strengthen narrative approaches and content decisions. Measure the effectiveness of storytelling initiatives in supporting donor engagement, partnership development, and organizational visibility. Content Collaboration & Internal Consulting Partner with philanthropy, conservation, science, policy, country, and digital teams to identify strategic storytelling opportunities. Provide editorial guidance and storytelling support to colleagues across the Africa region. Review, edit, and strengthen content created by internal contributors and external partners. Serve as a subject matter expert on storytelling best practices and content development. Building the network and collaborations to ensure Africa stories are elevated for global showcases. Desired Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in in Journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English related field and a minimum 7 years related experience or equivalent combination of education and experience. Exceptional writing, editing, interviewing, and narrative development skills. Demonstrated experience developing content strategies and managing editorial pipelines. Experience producing content across multiple formats, including written, digital, visual, and multimedia platforms. DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, Media Studies, English, or related field. 8+ years of professional experience in content strategy, editorial leadership, journalism, storytelling, publishing, or multimedia content development. Experience working in conservation, environmental, development, sustainability, or nonprofit sectors. Background in journalism, documentary storytelling, or editorial publishing. Experience producing stories for donor, philanthropic, and partnership audiences. Knowledge of digital content performance metrics and audience engagement strategies. Experience working across multiple African countries and cultures. Strong understanding of ethical storytelling, representation, and inclusive narrative practices. Strong portfolio demonstrating impactful storytelling and editorial leadership. Experience gathering stories through direct field reporting and stakeholder interviews. Excellent project management skills with experience managing multiple content initiatives simultaneously. Excellent relationship-building and collaboration skills, with experience working across cultures, functions, locations, and time zones. Fluency in written and spoken English. Employees may not drive Conservancy-owned/leased vehicles, rental cars, or personal vehicles on behalf of the Conservancy if considered "high risk drivers." To learn more about the Auto Safety Program, visit the Auto Safety information page. Duty Station(s) Home based Posting End Date: 22-Sep-2026 Role Purpose The Technical Specialist supports ICAT in strengthening the accessibility, usability and practical application of its Toolbox for developing countries. The role focuses on reviewing and mapping ICAT tools and guides, assessing their relevance against country needs, and identifying linkages, gaps and opportunities for further methodological development. Working under the supervision of ICAT’s Technical Advisor, the Technical Specialist will provide evidence-based recommendations to help countries more effectively use ICAT resources to build transparency frameworks for the implementation of the Paris Agreement. Functions / Key Results Expected Background The ICAT Toolbox consists of a range of over 40 tools and guides. In particular, it includes a series of guides and accompanying tools to support countries in assessing the impacts of policies and actions, covering greenhouse gas impacts in a variety of different sectors, as well as sustainable development and transformational impacts. Other important topics that are covered in the toolbox include the transparency of climate finance, monitoring of just transitions, M&E of adaptation, mainstreaming gender, and links between Articles 6 and 13. The development of the toolbox thus far has been driven by the needs of countries and the toolbox has been applied widely and received positively. However, feedback highlights the need to enhance its accessibility, usability, visibility and direct application to climate policies and actions, including their design, implementation and monitoring. To support this objective, a review and mapping exercise of the ICAT toolbox is needed. The aim is to clarify how the ICAT Toolbox supports developing countries to build robust transparency frameworks to implement the Paris Agreement. Specifically, the mapping will provide a concise overview of how each guide and tool can support countries to: develop evidence-based climate policies, develop and implement ambitious NDCs, mobilize finance, and facilitate international reporting (e.g. reporting of NDC progress in BTRs). The mapping will thus highlight how ICAT’s Toolbox aligns with ICAT’s strategy . The mapping will clarify the relevance and applicability of the tools and guides for different purposes, and position the toolbox within the broader landscape of tools and guides that are available from other organizations and entities. The results of this work will also be used to bring clarity to the benefits and functions of the toolbox, so that users can more easily navigate, understand and choose the tool or guide that suits their needs, and will also include identification of areas for further methodological development. Role Purpose: To manage the company's receivables and collections while driving accuracy, speed and insight in the company's financial data. The role combines day-to-day credit control with data capture, reporting automation and the continuous improvement of Excel and Sage processes, so that the finance team spends less time compiling numbers and more time acting on them. Maintain complete and correct customer records, including duly signed credit facility agreements, bank guarantees and updated contracts. Authorise and approve loadings to the sales team based on approved outstanding debt status. Design and enforce simple data entry standards and templates so that data is captured once, correctly, and can be reused. Act as custodian of the integrity of the receivables data used for management reporting. Efficiency & Process Improvement: Identify manual, repetitive finance processes and redesign them using better Excel structure, formulas and automation. Build and maintain reusable Excel tools: linked workbooks, dynamic formulas, pivot-based reporting, Power Query data refreshes and dashboards. job_description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF), established in 1979, provides National Societies with start-up funds for large-scale disaster response operations and as grants to cover the costs of small-scale disasters. Through close collaboration with its major partners, the International Federation is seeking to promote the quality of DREF operations, timely and quality reporting and transparency in the use of the funds and to further enhance the confidence of partners in the performance of the National Societies in implementing operations. Over the years, Africa Region remains one of the highest users of the DREF. The region plays a central role in the global use of the Disaster Response Emergency Fund (DREF). Within the Africa Region, DREF operations represent the biggest portion of the overall emergency operations portfolio. The region’s complex humanitarian landscape and the cyclical nature of crises continue to amplify operational demands and workload. Job Purpose As a member of the Global DREF Team and in alignment with DREF Procedures, the Regional DREF Delegate will support all DREF-related processes and support in the Africa Region. The role will support timely, compliant, and well-coordinated processing, documentation, and reporting of DREF requests, while providing expert technical and compliance analysis and guidance throughout the DREF cycle. Acting as a technical focal point on DREF to African National Societies, IFRC delegations, and regional staff, the role supports criteria-compliant submissions, contributes to the eligibility review of requests, and provides technical support on the appropriate and strategic use of DREF funds—ensuring operational relevance and alignment with procedures. In addition to compliance, the DREF Delegate support the technical review and quality assurance of DREF operations in the region, ensuring performance is aligned with IFRC KPIs, risk thresholds, and strategic frameworks. From that oversight position, the DREF Delegate provides ongoing analysis and technical support to inform operational decision-making in Delegations, the Regional Office, and National Societies across the full DREF cycle, including proactive monitoring and escalation of compliance or performance issues as needed. The DREF Delegate supports the Africa DCC team in operations coordination, contributing to the oversight of operational quality beyond the compliance role. job_description: UNDP works in 170 countries and territories to eradicate poverty, reduce inequality and support sustainable development. In Kenya, UNDP works with national partners to strengthen institutions, advance innovation and accelerate progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals. The programme brings together national AI compute infrastructure, public-sector capabilities and use cases, responsible AI and data governance, and Kenya's innovation ecosystem. The role will lead the data, modelling and evaluation layer of priority AI-enabled solutions, ensuring that solutions are built on appropriate data and demonstrate measurable improvement against credible baselines. Key Responsibilities Assess data readiness, quality, coverage, representativeness, labelling, provenance and licensing or consent for selected AI use cases. Define training, validation and testing strategies and determine appropriate modelling approaches across machine learning, NLP, computer vision, generative AI, large language models and retrieval-augmented approaches. Develop, adapt and fine-tune models for five selected priority AI use cases . Build and maintain data preparation, feature engineering, prompt engineering and retrieval pipelines. Lead structured experimentation, including hyperparameter searches, ablation studies and prompt or retrieval configuration testing. Optimise model accuracy, size, latency and inference costs for the available on-premise NVIDIA GPU-based compute environment. Develop evaluation protocols and benchmark model performance against agreed baselines. Conduct failure-mode and error analysis, including testing for overfitting, data leakage, spurious correlations and performance on under-represented groups. Work with the Responsible AI Specialist to assess model-level bias, fairness, robustness and privacy. Mentor junior AI developers and internal technical staff and support knowledge transfer through modelling sessions, code reviews and technical clinics. Develop model cards, dataset documentation, retraining playbooks and final technical handover documentation Profile Required Experience: Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in: Machine learning Applied AI Data science AI solution development Candidates must have hands-on experience developing, adapting, fine-tuning, evaluating and improving machine learning or AI models that have been taken into production or operational use . Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics , or a closely related field.
