job_title: Senior Research Officer for Sudan, based in Nairobi (Link For External Applicants)
job_description: BACKGROUND ON IMPACT Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. IMPACT aims to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilization, and development settings. Through our team of assessment, data, geospatial, and thematic specialists, IMPACT promotes the design of people-centred research and set standards for collecting and analysing rigorous, high quality data in complex environments. Over the past 15 years, IMPACT has been growing in size and geographic reach to become one of the largest humanitarian research agencies in the humanitarian sector. IMPACT's teams implement assessment, monitoring, evaluation, and organisational capacity-building programmes in direct partnership with aid actors. IMPACT's team is composed of over 200 full-time international experts as well as a roster of consultants, who are currently implementing over 50 programmes in over 30 countries across Africa, Middle East and North Africa, Central and South-east Asia, and Eastern Europe. We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our Sudan country team, currently based in Nairobi, Kenya Position: Senior Research Officer Cash and Markets Contract duration : 6 months Starting Date : ASAP Location : Nairobi, Kenya COUNTRY PROFILE Clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in Khartoum on 15 April 2023 and spread quickly across the country. Civilians have fled areas affected by fighting in large numbers, including to Chad, Egypt and South Sudan. Prices of food, fuel and other basic goods have skyrocketed skyrocketing, making critical goods unaffordable for many people. Half of Sudan’s population are in need of humanitarian assistance, and the country is on the verge of a catastrophic hunger crisis. Humanitarian organizations are racing to respond to the most pressing needs wherever and whenever feasible, with access issues complicating the ability of actors to respond. In this fast-evolving context, IMPACT Initiatives is working to inform the emergency response to enable effective prioritization with scarce resources. POSITION PROFILE Under the line management of the Research Manager for the Inter-Cluster Unit, the Senior Research Officer will take responsibility for all Cash workstreams, including overall responsibility for the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI) research cycle which records prices and stock levels across Sudan on a monthly basis, as well as associated analytical pieces based on JMMI data. This involves overseeing two Research Officers responsible for managing the JMMI, representing IMPACT in critical cash coordination fora like the Cash Working Group and Transfer Value Task Force, and independently developing and implementing new analysis based on JMMI data. This position requires strong research skills, a willingness to work in a team, an analytical mind, creativity, and strong independence. Knowledge of the national or regional context in Sudan, as well as fluency in Arabic are considered a strong asset. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings. The position will regularly require looking at data, pulling out relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research. BACKGROUND ON CASH AND MARKET ASSESSMENTS In recent decades, humanitarian action has moved towards giving aid in the form of cash or voucher assistance (CVA) issued directly to beneficiaries. This gives beneficiaries a choice in how to spend aid money, and it also supports livelihoods, markets, and supply chains within impacted localities. Effective CVA must be backed by informed research on price levels, the availability of goods, and the resilience of supply chains across different localities. Responsibilities The Senior Research Officer’s responsibilities include: RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT Take overall accountability for the robust and timely implementation of the JMMI research cycle Manage additional research cycles based on JMMI data end-to-end, including development of objectives, research design and analysis. Manage timelines and deliverables aligning outputs with partners programmatic objectives Research And Technical Skills Independently develop analysis based on JMMI and additional secondary data sources relevant to the context and supporting humanitarian programming Oversee the development of the JMMI and provide technical guidance on needed adjustments Produce high quality research outputs in English. EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT Represent IMPACT on all cash-related platforms, including the Cash Working Group, Collective Sudan (CCS), Markets in Crisis Group and others, as well as regular engagement with senior stakeholders involved in cash programming, including WFP, IFPRI, CHC, Rift Valley Institute and others Provide technical advice to external partners such as the Transfer Value Working Group based on JMMI data Develop an understanding of key information gaps based on feedback from partners to develop new analysis products accordingly CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING Develop an understanding of price and market dynamics across different regions in Sudan Keep up to date with conflict dynamics STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING Manage two Research Officers who are responsible for liaising with partner organisations who carry out data collection, supporting data cleaning, analysing findings, and crafting outputs such as factsheets and written reports Promote capacity building across the IMPACT Sudan mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience). INTERNAL COORDINATION Interact autonomously with HQ departments and possibly serving as a mission focal point for particular themes or technical areas; Coordinate with research units and teams to move forward or improve aspects of the research cycle; Supporting senior management with designing, planning, and implementing strategies, and objectives. The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during their assignment with IMPACT. Requirements Academic qualifications Excellent academic qualifications are required. A master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.) is an asset. Years of work experience At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting or equivalent, which could include assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis. Research skills Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience is required. Thematic experience in cash and markets in emergencies Proven track record of engaging in cash and markets work in contexts of crises with a deep understanding of concepts such as the MEB, Transfer Values, regional price fluctuations and impacts on the response Communication/reporting skills Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills in English for effective reporting are required. Software skills Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software is an asset Familiarity with aid system Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums is an asset. Thematic experience Prior experience with Cash and Markets, particularly with the JMMI is an asset. Experience in geographical region Past experience in the region is desirable; knowledge of the national context in Sudan would be a significant asset. Language skills Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is a significant asset. Compensation & Benefits For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere. Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse. Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance. Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered). Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance) Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable. Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training; IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees.

Senior Manager, Communications — M-KOPA Your pitches land. Your crisis plans hold up. But can you make both work across five markets — while keeping a business, its leaders and its reputation moving in the same direction? There are communications roles where the brief is clear, the markets are familiar, and there is a team for every specialist need. This isn't one of them. At M-KOPA, communications sits much closer to the business. You'll shape the narrative, advise senior leaders, manage reputation, navigate complex stakeholders and know what to do when the story changes faster than the plan. You'll need to be equally comfortable building the story before it becomes news and protecting it when the stakes suddenly rise. We're building financial access at a scale few companies attempt. M-KOPA now serves 7 million customers across Sub-Saharan Africa, having unlocked over $2 billion in credit . Independent research tells us 86% of our customers report improved quality of life , 70% use our products to generate income , and 55% are accessing formal financial services for the first time . Behind that: 2,300+ employees, 35,000+ agents, $45 million contributed in taxes, 2 million smartphones assembled in Kenya, and a growing e-mobility business already saving riders $5.62 a day in fuel costs. Why this timing matters If you've noticed M-KOPA advertising several senior roles at once, that's not a coincidence — it's deliberate. We're scaling from 7 million customers toward 10 million, and that means building the infrastructure, leadership bench, and narrative capability to match. Communications sits right at the centre of that. As we grow, more markets, more media, more employees, more regulators and more public stakeholders need a coherent, credible story about who we are and the impact we're creating. And that story needs to work at two levels: locally, where context matters, and across the Group, where consistency matters just as much. This role exists because we're at the point where communications can't simply respond to what is happening. It needs to help shape what happens next. What makes this different Most Senior Manager, Communications roles at this level sit above the work — reviewing, approving, delegating. This one doesn't. You'll draft the media pitch yourself. You'll sit with a Country MD and work through group positioning. You'll counsel senior stakeholders on how to navigate a sensitive issue. You'll work alongside marketing to make sure campaigns, brand and corporate reputation are telling the same story. You'll partner directly with People/HR on a sensitive change narrative. You'll also build relationships with the people who matter beyond the organisation — from media and partners to government stakeholders and regulators across the markets in which we operate. And when something goes wrong, you'll be one of the people in the room figuring out what happens next. Because reputation doesn't stop at the press release. It lives in the decisions a business makes, the way leaders communicate, the relationships it builds and how it responds when circumstances get complicated. And in the same week, you might chase a purchase order and reconcile a budget line, because there's no one else to hand that to. It's a rare mix of strategic counsel, integrated communications, reputation management and genuine hands-on ownership — and because M-KOPA doesn't have dedicated in-market communications teams, you'll be the connective tissue holding Group positioning and market execution together across the region. What you'll need to bring A communications career, not just communications exposure. You've built your expertise in corporate communications, integrated communications or a similarly broad communications environment, and understand how media, reputation, brand, internal communications and stakeholder engagement connect. Strong strategic instincts. You can take a business objective, understand what matters to different audiences and turn it into a communications strategy that leaders can actually use. You're as comfortable giving counsel as you are executing the work yourself. Deep experience in reputation and issues management. You've operated in situations where the stakes are high and judgement matters. You understand that protecting reputation isn't simply about controlling a message — it's about understanding the business, anticipating risk and knowing how to communicate when there isn't an obvious answer. Crisis communications experience that goes beyond a playbook. You've had to think clearly under pressure, advise leaders, coordinate stakeholders and communicate externally when the circumstances weren't neatly packaged. You know that a crisis rarely arrives in the format you prepared for. Multi-market experience, ideally across Africa. You've managed reputation and communications across different geographies, cultures, regulatory environments and stakeholder landscapes. You understand that what works in one market may not work in another — and can balance local relevance with a consistent Group narrative. Stakeholder confidence. You'll work with Country MDs, senior executives, government stakeholders, regulators, media and other external partners. You need to be able to build trust quickly, navigate different agendas and provide clear counsel — particularly when the answer isn't straightforward. Strength across external and internal communications. External communications will be a significant part of the role, but you'll also need to understand employee communications, leadership messaging, organisational change and culture — and how the two worlds influence each other. Excellent writing. You can turn complexity into clarity. You know when a message needs precision, when it needs personality and when it needs both. Whether you're writing a press statement, executive briefing, leadership speech, crisis response or employee communication, the quality of your thinking should come through in the quality of your writing. Experience in complex, fast-moving environments. You may have worked in a fintech, technology business, high-growth company, agency or another matrixed organisation. What matters is that you've learned to operate across functions, influence without always having direct authority and get up to speed quickly when the context changes. Comfort operating lean. You don't need a large team around you to get things done. You know when to bring in an agency or specialist, when to solve the problem yourself and how to keep momentum without unnecessary layers. Operational ownership. Agencies, suppliers and budgets aren't someone else's problem. You're comfortable taking work from strategy through to execution — including procurement, POs, spend tracking and the finance administration that keeps the function moving. What the work actually looks like One day you're drafting a press statement under time pressure. The next, you're on a call with a Country MD, working through why local execution has drifted from Group messaging — and helping them fix it, not just flagging it. You're preparing a senior leader for a difficult conversation with an external stakeholder. You're working with marketing on an integrated campaign and asking the questions that make sure the communications strategy supports the wider business objective. A regulatory issue emerges in one market. You need to understand it quickly, bring the right people together, assess the reputational implications and help determine what M-KOPA should say — and what it should do. You're building the weekly media report that actually tells the Director something useful about sentiment and share of voice, not just a list of clippings. You're in a planning session with People/HR, shaping how a sensitive organisational change gets communicated to employees across several countries. And somewhere in the same week, you're raising a PO, chasing an invoice, or reconciling the department's budget — because keeping the function's engine running is as much your job as the storytelling is. The honest version This role is genuinely demanding. You're doing strategic, high-visibility work and operational detail in the same breath, often across multiple markets and without the buffer of a dedicated in-market communications team. It asks for someone who can move between the boardroom and the detail. Someone who can challenge a senior leader with confidence, build trust with a regulator, navigate a developing issue, write a statement at speed and still care about whether the budget reconciles at the end of the month. You'll need to be curious about Africa. Comfortable with ambiguity. Commercial enough to understand the business behind the story. Calm when things move quickly. And experienced enough to know when communications needs to lead, when it needs to listen and when it needs to get out of the way. If you're looking for a role where communications is neatly separated into internal, external, brand and PR lanes, this probably isn't it. If you're looking for the opportunity to shape reputation, influence leaders, work across markets and be close enough to the business to actually change the outcome , it might be. Let's talk If you're the kind of communications professional who wants to do more than manage the message — someone who wants to understand the business, shape the narrative, counsel the people making the decisions and know what to do when the unexpected happens — we'd like to hear from you. Maybe you've built that experience inside a high-growth fintech. Maybe you've done it in a global agency. Maybe you've worked across multiple markets in a complex, matrixed organisation and know how to make things happen without waiting for perfect conditions. Wherever you've built it, if Africa, reputation, complexity and meaningful scale sound like the kind of communications challenge you'd want to get your hands on, let's talk. Why M-KOPA? At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. job_description: What NuruFi does? NuruFi is the credit engine for clean energy trade in emerging markets. We operate an asset-light risk verification and assessment engine that enables clean energy equipment distributors to safely extend credit terms to local EPCs, unlocking stalled pipelines and getting productive-use solar assets into the market faster. The trajectory is phased: v1 asset-light underwriting and servicing (earn fees, build the dataset); v2 tooling to make assessment faster and cheaper; v3 financing purchase orders directly, funded by a separate debt vehicle raised once the performance record justifies it. The core capability is underwriting productive-use payers that carry no credit rating and that international funds cannot assess cost-effectively NuruFi is currently part of the Carbon13 venture-building programme. The current team: Founder / CEO — energy systems engineer; owns the technical underwriting (system design, sizing, performance risk) and overall direction. Operations & Credit Lead (Uganda) — origination, on-the-ground verification, and collections. The role: You would own credit as a function and build it into a system. Specifically: Underwriting. Own and develop the credit methodology — the scorecard, risk framework, and decisioning — for unrated business payers. Personally assess deals in the early phase; the manual work is the point, and it is how the model gets built. Structuring. Set deal terms (limits, tenor, deposits, milestones), design the collection waterfall, and work with local counsel on assignment of receivables and its perfection. Portfolio & risk. Build servicing, monitoring, early-warning, and workout/recovery practice. Own the performance dataset that the underwriting model will be trained and re-weighted against. Capital (as the company matures). Lead the eventual raise of a debt facility and the relationships with debt funds, DFIs, and guarantors that finance the receivables in the next phase. Co-Founder Governance: Participate directly in company strategy, investor fundraising pitches, board dynamics, and institutional scaling. Who you are? Direct experience underwriting SME, trade, receivables, or working-capital credit in an African or emerging market — you have made real credit decisions and lived with the outcomes. Hands-on. You are willing to assess deals yourself, chase payments, and work out a default in the early stage, not only design frameworks for others to run. Comfortable building structure from little: a scorecard in a spreadsheet before it is a system; a method before it is software. Working knowledge of structured trade finance and debt-raising — receivables facilities, security and collateral, and what debt funds and DFIs require — or a credible path to owning it. Grounded and analytical in how you communicate risk. Numbers and structure over narrative. Useful: Exposure to clean-energy, asset, or equipment finance. Familiarity with East African legal and payments infrastructure (movable-collateral registration, mobile money, bank rails, assignment of receivables). A network among debt funds, DFIs, or guarantee providers active in Sub-Saharan Africa. Terms: Co-founder equity, commensurate with a founding role and the stage. Cash compensation is limited until the first raise, which this role helps lead. Equity: Co-Founder Equity Share (12% – 20%, vesting schedule, open to negotiation based on experience and capital match capability)

job_description: Who We Are Moniepoint Inc. is Africa’s all-in-one financial platform, helping 20 million businesses and individuals access seamless payments, banking, credit, cross-border, and business management tools each month. As Nigeria’s largest merchant acquirer, we power most of the country’s point-of-sale (POS) transactions. Through our subsidiaries, Moniepoint Inc. processes over $250 billion in digital payment transaction value annually. Why Kenya Powering that scale takes engineering talent well beyond our home markets - which is where Kenya comes in. Kenya is where our next chapter begins. Following our acquisition of Sumac Microfinance Bank, we're preparing to go live - which means the people we hire here help build a business from its first day, not inherit one. How we execute in Kenya will shape how we approach every market we enter after it, making this one of the most consequential engineering mandates in the business right now. This is the natural extension of our mission: to drive financial inclusion, and help millions of business owners and individuals across the African continent achieve financial happiness and success. We already have a small number of team members in engineering based out of Kenya, who have become central to how we build and run our platform globally. So, now we are now looking for our Head of Engineering, POS Apps to join us in India. About The Role More than 6 million businesses run their financial lives through Moniepoint - and the primary way they interact with us every single day is through a POS device. For most of our merchants, that device is their business. It is how they accept payments, how they access credit, and how they track their finances. Everything those devices are capable of, in terms of speed, reliability, and developer quality, flows from the engineering platform this role leads. We are building a dedicated POS Application Platform function: the foundational Kotlin-based engineering layer that sits beneath every POS product at Moniepoint. Think of it as the operating system for our POS engineering organisation - the standards, frameworks, tooling, and architectural backbone that every POS engineer across the business builds on top of. This is not a feature team. It is a platform team in the truest sense, and the Head of Engineering for POS Application Platform is the technical owner of that layer. We currently operate across five POS device types from multiple OEM manufacturers, all running on Android. The engineering challenges here span device governance, developer experience, platform reliability, foundational frameworks, and adoption across a distributed set of POS engineers working in separate product squads. And the scope is growing. We have a UK entity live, a cross-border payments product in market, and a microfinance bank acquisition which just finalized in Kenya. The platform you build will become the foundation for tens of millions of businesses across multiple markets to accept payments, access financial services, and grow. If you have spent your career going deep on POS systems and you want to build the platform that underpins one of Africa's most consequential fintech businesses during its expansion, this is the role. What You'll Get To Do Own the technical strategy and architecture for the POS Application Platform, acting as the domain CTO for everything that runs on our POS devices. Build and govern the four core platform pillars across the organisation: developer experience (tools, libraries, SDKs), platform reliability (observability, uptime, quality standards), foundational frameworks (architecture, coding standards, testing and release pipelines), and squad adoption (driving uptake of platform tooling across all embedded POS engineers). Define and enforce engineering standards across all POS device types and OEM manufacturers, ensuring architectural consistency and quality across a heterogeneous device fleet. Functionally lead POS engineers embedded across Payments, Onboarding, VAS, Savings, and Loans squads - setting the bar for engineering quality and providing the platform layer above all of them. Own POS observability end-to-end: monitoring, alerting, and incident response frameworks that ensure platform health across all devices and squads. Drive the architecture for how Moniepoint supports multiple POS device types, including defining how new devices are onboarded, governed, and integrated with the platform. Collaborate with OEM partners and the POS hardware team when new device types are introduced, ensuring the application layer is ready to support them from day one. Build and scale the POS platform team, including hiring, mentoring, and structuring for growth as the platform expands internationally. Translate platform decisions into business impact, working closely with Product, Payments, and Business leadership across markets. Establish and continuously improve engineering processes, tooling standards, CI/CD pipelines, and developer productivity metrics across the POS engineering community. To succeed in this role, we think you should have A minimum of 10 years of hands-on software engineering experience, with at least 6 years leading engineering teams through meaningful growth phases, ideally in multi-national or large VC-backed companies. Direct, hands-on experience building software that runs on Point-of-Sale terminal devices. This means engineering on the device itself — the application layer — not server-side integrations with POS systems. This is a non-negotiable requirement and candidates without it will not be considered. Strong working knowledge of EMV standards (Europay, Mastercard, Visa) and experience navigating payment certification processes such as PCI DSS and P2PE. Candidates without this will not be considered. Deep Android engineering expertise in Kotlin and Java. The POS application layer at Moniepoint is Android-based and there are no exceptions to this requirement. Proven experience building internal engineering platforms, shared libraries, developer tooling, or foundational frameworks used by other engineering teams — not just consumer-facing feature products. Experience governing or architecting across multiple POS device types from different hardware manufacturers, with an understanding of how OEM integrations and device management work at scale. Experience building or maturing platform engineering functions, including establishing engineering processes, tooling strategies, and cross-squad governance structures. Demonstrated ability to scale engineering teams and build the organisational layer beneath you — leaders who can grow into and around the role you are hiring into. Experience at a company processing high volumes of financial transactions in a regulated environment. Fintech background is strongly preferred. Familiarity with terminal management systems and device observability tooling is a strong advantage. Backend engineering experience in Java or Spring Boot is a strong plus given the breadth of the platform and the integration surface it sits on. Experience working directly with OEM vendors on hardware specification and integration is a bonus. Exposure to C or C++ is a plus — one of our device variants uses C. Experience at Series A or B stage startups alone is unlikely to reflect the scale and complexity required for this role. Cultural Alignment We assess every candidate across eight dimensions that define how great leaders operate at Moniepoint. We look for evidence of all eight throughout the process, not just in a single conversation. Customer Obsession: Deep empathy for the people depending on the platform — whether that is a merchant in Lagos trying to accept a payment, or a POS engineer blocked by missing tooling. You solve problems quickly and intuitively. You close loops by fixing root causes, not just tickets. Craft: You have mastered your domain at the fundamentals level. You make trade-offs explicit, reason from first principles, and consistently produce solutions that are better than typical. Systemisation: You convert recurring decisions into repeatable mechanisms. You reduce cognitive load for others. You strengthen institutional memory and improve engineering quality at scale. Urgency: You move with disciplined speed. You act without waiting for permission when you are within scope. You escalate early when risk exceeds your authority. You remove friction and close loops. Ownership: You treat the platform as yours to solve regardless of job description boundaries. You take responsibility without being asked. You follow through on commitments without being reminded. No Ego: You put the mission ahead of personal status. You credit others genuinely, welcome challenge, and never protect your position at the expense of collective outcomes. Candour: You surface reality early, clearly, and completely — especially when it is uncomfortable. You name risks before they become crises. Intelligent failure is acceptable; concealment is not. Integrity: Truthfulness and ethical consistency in everything. You adhere to rules and obligations. You never perform under intimidation or corrosive behaviour. Performance without integrity is unacceptable. Stage 4: Technical and Architectural Leadership - An interview with one Head of Engineering focused on leadership skills and attributes. Senior Manager, Communications — M-KOPA Your pitches land. Your crisis plans hold up. But can you make both work across five markets — while keeping a business, its leaders and its reputation moving in the same direction? There are communications roles where the brief is clear, the markets are familiar, and there is a team for every specialist need. This isn't one of them. At M-KOPA, communications sits much closer to the business. You'll shape the narrative, advise senior leaders, manage reputation, navigate complex stakeholders and know what to do when the story changes faster than the plan. You'll need to be equally comfortable building the story before it becomes news and protecting it when the stakes suddenly rise. We're building financial access at a scale few companies attempt. M-KOPA now serves 7 million customers across Sub-Saharan Africa, having unlocked over $2 billion in credit . Independent research tells us 86% of our customers report improved quality of life , 70% use our products to generate income , and 55% are accessing formal financial services for the first time . Behind that: 2,300+ employees, 35,000+ agents, $45 million contributed in taxes, 2 million smartphones assembled in Kenya, and a growing e-mobility business already saving riders $5.62 a day in fuel costs. Why this timing matters If you've noticed M-KOPA advertising several senior roles at once, that's not a coincidence — it's deliberate. We're scaling from 7 million customers toward 10 million, and that means building the infrastructure, leadership bench, and narrative capability to match. Communications sits right at the centre of that. As we grow, more markets, more media, more employees, more regulators and more public stakeholders need a coherent, credible story about who we are and the impact we're creating. And that story needs to work at two levels: locally, where context matters, and across the Group, where consistency matters just as much. This role exists because we're at the point where communications can't simply respond to what is happening. It needs to help shape what happens next. What makes this different Most Senior Manager, Communications roles at this level sit above the work — reviewing, approving, delegating. This one doesn't. You'll draft the media pitch yourself. You'll sit with a Country MD and work through group positioning. You'll counsel senior stakeholders on how to navigate a sensitive issue. You'll work alongside marketing to make sure campaigns, brand and corporate reputation are telling the same story. You'll partner directly with People/HR on a sensitive change narrative. You'll also build relationships with the people who matter beyond the organisation — from media and partners to government stakeholders and regulators across the markets in which we operate. And when something goes wrong, you'll be one of the people in the room figuring out what happens next. Because reputation doesn't stop at the press release. It lives in the decisions a business makes, the way leaders communicate, the relationships it builds and how it responds when circumstances get complicated. And in the same week, you might chase a purchase order and reconcile a budget line, because there's no one else to hand that to. It's a rare mix of strategic counsel, integrated communications, reputation management and genuine hands-on ownership — and because M-KOPA doesn't have dedicated in-market communications teams, you'll be the connective tissue holding Group positioning and market execution together across the region. What you'll need to bring A communications career, not just communications exposure. You've built your expertise in corporate communications, integrated communications or a similarly broad communications environment, and understand how media, reputation, brand, internal communications and stakeholder engagement connect. Strong strategic instincts. You can take a business objective, understand what matters to different audiences and turn it into a communications strategy that leaders can actually use. You're as comfortable giving counsel as you are executing the work yourself. Deep experience in reputation and issues management. You've operated in situations where the stakes are high and judgement matters. You understand that protecting reputation isn't simply about controlling a message — it's about understanding the business, anticipating risk and knowing how to communicate when there isn't an obvious answer. Crisis communications experience that goes beyond a playbook. You've had to think clearly under pressure, advise leaders, coordinate stakeholders and communicate externally when the circumstances weren't neatly packaged. You know that a crisis rarely arrives in the format you prepared for. Multi-market experience, ideally across Africa. You've managed reputation and communications across different geographies, cultures, regulatory environments and stakeholder landscapes. You understand that what works in one market may not work in another — and can balance local relevance with a consistent Group narrative. Stakeholder confidence. You'll work with Country MDs, senior executives, government stakeholders, regulators, media and other external partners. You need to be able to build trust quickly, navigate different agendas and provide clear counsel — particularly when the answer isn't straightforward. Strength across external and internal communications. External communications will be a significant part of the role, but you'll also need to understand employee communications, leadership messaging, organisational change and culture — and how the two worlds influence each other. Excellent writing. You can turn complexity into clarity. You know when a message needs precision, when it needs personality and when it needs both. Whether you're writing a press statement, executive briefing, leadership speech, crisis response or employee communication, the quality of your thinking should come through in the quality of your writing. Experience in complex, fast-moving environments. You may have worked in a fintech, technology business, high-growth company, agency or another matrixed organisation. What matters is that you've learned to operate across functions, influence without always having direct authority and get up to speed quickly when the context changes. Comfort operating lean. You don't need a large team around you to get things done. You know when to bring in an agency or specialist, when to solve the problem yourself and how to keep momentum without unnecessary layers. Operational ownership. Agencies, suppliers and budgets aren't someone else's problem. You're comfortable taking work from strategy through to execution — including procurement, POs, spend tracking and the finance administration that keeps the function moving. What the work actually looks like One day you're drafting a press statement under time pressure. The next, you're on a call with a Country MD, working through why local execution has drifted from Group messaging — and helping them fix it, not just flagging it. You're preparing a senior leader for a difficult conversation with an external stakeholder. You're working with marketing on an integrated campaign and asking the questions that make sure the communications strategy supports the wider business objective. A regulatory issue emerges in one market. You need to understand it quickly, bring the right people together, assess the reputational implications and help determine what M-KOPA should say — and what it should do. You're building the weekly media report that actually tells the Director something useful about sentiment and share of voice, not just a list of clippings. You're in a planning session with People/HR, shaping how a sensitive organisational change gets communicated to employees across several countries. And somewhere in the same week, you're raising a PO, chasing an invoice, or reconciling the department's budget — because keeping the function's engine running is as much your job as the storytelling is. The honest version This role is genuinely demanding. You're doing strategic, high-visibility work and operational detail in the same breath, often across multiple markets and without the buffer of a dedicated in-market communications team. It asks for someone who can move between the boardroom and the detail. Someone who can challenge a senior leader with confidence, build trust with a regulator, navigate a developing issue, write a statement at speed and still care about whether the budget reconciles at the end of the month. You'll need to be curious about Africa. Comfortable with ambiguity. Commercial enough to understand the business behind the story. Calm when things move quickly. And experienced enough to know when communications needs to lead, when it needs to listen and when it needs to get out of the way. If you're looking for a role where communications is neatly separated into internal, external, brand and PR lanes, this probably isn't it. If you're looking for the opportunity to shape reputation, influence leaders, work across markets and be close enough to the business to actually change the outcome , it might be. Let's talk If you're the kind of communications professional who wants to do more than manage the message — someone who wants to understand the business, shape the narrative, counsel the people making the decisions and know what to do when the unexpected happens — we'd like to hear from you. Maybe you've built that experience inside a high-growth fintech. Maybe you've done it in a global agency. Maybe you've worked across multiple markets in a complex, matrixed organisation and know how to make things happen without waiting for perfect conditions. Wherever you've built it, if Africa, reputation, complexity and meaningful scale sound like the kind of communications challenge you'd want to get your hands on, let's talk. Why M-KOPA? We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility. Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com . This is an unpaid, volunteer opportunity About The Affiliated Organization Conserv Congo is building a locally led conservation model in which communities, government institutions, and Congolese professionals become the principal actors protecting biodiversity- shifting conservation from externally driven protection toward a system rooted in local leadership, justice, opportunity, and long-term ownership. Your contribution is important because conservation organizations working on the frontlines often have strong field knowledge and local networks but limited access to specialized technical expertise. By contributing professional skills, you can help Conserv Congo build stronger systems, communicate its impact more effectively, improve decision-making, and develop solutions that can continue serving communities and conservation practitioners long after the volunteer assignment ends. Most importantly, you will be contributing to a broader vision: strengthening African-led conservation by helping Congolese professionals and communities develop the tools, institutions, and capacity to protect their own natural heritage. job_title: ENDLINE EVALUATION CONSULTANCY- MPROTECT(Learning to Earning)
job_description: Applicants are welcome to review the Consultancy TOR Here Specific Objectives To examine the extent to which the project objectives have been achieved. Assess how the project contributed to the impact including key enabling and/or constraining factors that led to project achievements. Also assess the unintended/unplanned effects of the project among the project participants, local communities, and wider context. To determine how the project benefited the project participants . (include the two most significant change stories/case studies) Assess how it (project) addressed barriers in the prevention of sexual exploitation of children and youth and integration into the world of work To assess the inclusiveness of the project; where any participants or groups left behind and why (gender, socio-economic background, religion, etc ) To examine the quality and efficacy of the technical skills training with regard to expanding economic opportunities for youth and making them employable. What is working and what needs improvement to enhance youth employability (formal employment and business) To document what worked, what did not work, key lessons learned, and recommendations for future implementation on youths skills development and employment, as well as sexual exploitation of children and youth prevention programming in Kenya and in other projects designed under similar contexts To Assess the Project's Accountability towards participants and communities (in reference to the PAF) and the quality of Participation and Trauma-informed care approaches. Evaluate relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and sustainability of the project. Evaluation Scope and Duration The scope of the evaluation includes a review and assessment of all activities carried out under the TdH NL and its partner’s agreement from inception until the end of the project period. The evaluation should assess the project’s achievements in reaching its targets and objectives outlined in the relevant project documents as will be provided by TdH NL. It should assess project design, implementation, effectiveness, lessons learned, replicability, and provide recommendations for future projects. The proposed evaluation timeframe is 30 working days between 13/10/2026 and 24/11/2026. This will be done per the OECD Development Assistance Committee (OECD - DAC) evaluation criteria with an intersectionality approach including but not limited to child participation and gender Deliverables and Key Responsibilities In accordance with the timetable, the evaluator (s) will produce: A draft inception report which responds to the scope of work with a methodology, safeguarding and privacy plans, data collection instruments, detailed work plan, and budget. A field work implementation plan ( to be submitted before field work begins). This field work plan should be presented to TdH NL for comments and revised as necessary prior to commencing field work. A final End-Term Evaluation report incorporating feedback from TdH NL,KNOTE and JCP. The Revised Report will synthesise all data, MsC stories, identify conclusions, and make recommendations (Taking into account ALL comments and additions from TdH NL and JCP following submission of the Draft Report). Oral Presentation/Meeting and debrief with project staff: The consultant will make a presentation to TdH NL, KNOTE and JCPs of the findings of the evaluation, including lessons for project improvement. The debriefing meeting will be an opportunity to clarify outstanding aspects of the evaluation before the finalisation of the end line report. The Final Report: The consultant will be expected to produce a final report, with comments from the debriefing taken into account. While the substantive content of the findings, conclusions, and recommendations of the report shall be determined by the evaluator, the report is subject to final approval by TdH NL in terms of whether or not the report meets the conditions of the ToR and expected standards. The consultant will be required to submit all data sets used for the evaluation, any scripts or instructions on data management as well as transcripts of all qualitative information gathered during data collection, key informant interviews, focus group discussions, and a list of people interviewed /met as appendices to the final report. Validation Workshop: After the evaluation report is finalised, TdH NL, KNOTE and JCP will organise a validation workshop with its key stakeholders(both internal and external). The consultant is expected to co-facilitate the workshop and present the results of the evaluation. The consultant is expected to incorporate feedback from the workshops into the final report. job_description: About CHANCEN International Submission Deadline: 21st September 2026 Chancen International is a non-profit financial institution providing ethical, fair, and responsible financing to help young Africans access quality tertiary education. Using an innovative Income Share Agreement (ISA) model, we cover students' tuition fees, allowing them to study without financial barriers. Graduates repay a portion of their income once employed, creating a sustainable funding cycle that supports future generations. By empowering young people with education, we enable their transition to meaningful employment, fostering economic mobility and strengthening communities. Headquartered in Kigali, Rwanda, and operating in Rwanda, Kenya, South Africa, and Ghana, Chancen International has helped over 11,000 young people access education leading to dignified work. Our focus on marginalized populations ensures these youth gain the skills needed to thrive and contribute to building strong economies and peaceful nations. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive working environment where each individual can flourish and achieve their full potential. Our actions are guided by our company values: Authenticity, Curiosity, Courage, Stewardship and Fairness. Background and Objective Chancen's means testing methodology, developed and validated in Rwanda, is used to assess applicants' socioeconomic status and determine eligibility for our Income Share Agreement financing. As we expand our reach in South Africa and Kenya, we need this methodology Chancen invites qualified organizations and individual consultants with relevant expertise to apply to support this adaptation, ensuring the methodology remains rigorous, locally grounded, and fit for purpose in both countries. Applicants may apply to work on one country or both , please indicate clearly in your proposal which country/countries you are applying for. Scope of Work The selected organization(s) or consultant(s) will adapt Chancen's existing methodology and scoring tool for South Africa and/or Kenya, preserving its overall structure and logic while ensuring indicators, thresholds, and data sources fit local realities. The assignment includes: Reviewing the existing methodology and tool, and assessing fit and gaps for the country/countries applied for. Identifying appropriate national data sources to inform country-specific thresholds. Recommending and justifying adapted indicators and thresholds for each country applied for. Updating the scoring tool and methodology note for each country applied for. Supporting Chancen's MEL team to test and validate the adapted tool(s) ahead of roll-out. Expected Deliverables Per country applied for: Inception note confirming approach, data sources, and timeline Country methodology note documenting adapted thresholds and rationale Adapted scoring tool, mirroring the structure of the existing tool Validation summary and final handover, including a short presentation to Chancen's leadership and MEL team. Requirements Required Qualifications and Experience: Chancen welcomes applications from both organizations (research firms, consultancies, academic/policy research centers) and individual consultants able to demonstrate: Experience designing or adapting means testing, targeting, or proxy means test methodologies — ideally in education, social protection, or development finance. Familiarity with household living standards, income/expenditure, or multidimensional poverty measurement, and with South Africa's and/or Kenya's household survey landscape. How to apply: Submit the following by 21st September 2026 combined into a single file : A cover note stating whether you are applying for South Africa, Kenya, or both. A brief technical proposal (max. 3 pages) outlining your proposed approach to means testing/proxy mean test methodology design, relevant data sources you would use, and how you would validate the tool for the country context. A CV (individuals) or company profile with team CVs (organizations). At least two references or examples of similar past work, ideally relevant to the country/countries applied for. A financial proposal / cost estimate (separate line items per country if applying for both).

Role Overview The Repossession Associate is responsible for executing motorcycle repossession, recovery, and field response activities across Nairobi and its environs. The role involves locating and recovering company assets from customers in default, coordinating voluntary returns, responding to operational incidents, and ensuring that all recovered motorcycles are safely and properly handed over to designated company facilities. The role requires a high level of professionalism, integrity, accountability, and discretion, while ensuring that all recovery activities are conducted in accordance with company policies, applicable laws, and established operational procedures. Key Responsibilities Motorcycle Repossession & Recovery Execute assigned motorcycle repossession and recovery cases within required service-level timelines. Locate motorcycles and riders using company systems, GPS/tracking tools, field intelligence, and other authorized resources. Conduct field visits to assigned locations to facilitate recovery of company assets. Engage customers professionally to encourage payment resolutions and voluntary motorcycle surrender where appropriate. Carry out repossessions in a lawful, professional, safe, and non-confrontational manner. Prioritize cases based on risk level, recovery urgency, location, and instructions from the Repossession Lead. Recover motorcycles from authorized locations, including police stations, impound yards, workshops, and other designated holding facilities. Coordinate with authorized recovery agents where external support is required. Ensure recovered motorcycles are safely transported to the designated company yard, workshop, or authorized location. Field Support Respond promptly to incidents assigned through the Control Room or Repossession Lead. Provide field support for road traffic accidents, abandoned motorcycles, theft or suspected theft, security-related incidents, impounded motorcycles, and other fleet-related emergencies. Assess incident locations and provide accurate updates to the Control Room and relevant supervisors. Assist in securing company motorcycles and other assets involved in incidents. Escalate serious incidents, safety concerns, disputes, suspected fraud, and security threats through the appropriate channels. Maintain clear communication with the Control Room until incidents are resolved or formally handed over. Asset Recovery & Handover Verify recovered motorcycles against company records. Inspect and document the condition of motorcycles at the point of recovery. Verify company-issued accessories, including helmets, spare keys, trackers, and other assigned equipment. Take photographs and collect supporting evidence where required. Complete recovery and handover documentation accurately and promptly. Ensure all recovered motorcycles are handed over to designated yards, workshops, or authorized company representatives. Immediately report missing, damaged, vandalized, or altered assets. Follow up on motorcycles held at police stations, impound yards, or other authorized facilities to support timely release and minimize downtime and storage costs. Customer & Stakeholder Engagement Interact professionally and respectfully with customers and riders during recovery activities. Clearly explain the recovery process and relevant company requirements. Handle customer resistance, complaints, and disputes calmly and escalate unresolved matters appropriately. Liaise with police officers, county enforcement officers, NTSA representatives, insurance personnel, workshop teams, and other relevant stakeholders. Maintain professional relationships with external recovery agents and service providers. Represent the company positively and professionally in all field engagements . Compliance, Safety & Risk Management Conduct all repossession and recovery activities in compliance with company policies, procedures, and applicable laws and regulations. Avoid confrontational or unsafe situations and escalate matters where there is a risk to personal safety, company personnel, customers, or company assets. Follow approved procedures when dealing with police stations, impound facilities, government agencies, and other third parties. Maintain confidentiality of customer, company, and operational information. Report suspected fraud, misconduct, theft, asset tampering, and other irregularities immediately. Comply with all health, safety, security, and field-operational requirements. Maintain proper conduct and professionalism while representing the organization. Documentation & Reporting Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of assigned repossession and recovery cases. Update recovery status through designated fleet management, tracking, or operational systems. Submit daily field activity and recovery reports within required timelines. Prepare incident reports for accidents, arrests, thefts, impoundments, breakdowns, disputes, and other significant occurrences. Maintain supporting documentation, including photographs, recovery forms, police documentation, release letters, rider statements, and handover records. Ensure assigned cases are properly updated, closed, or escalated in accordance with established procedures. Provide accurate information for daily, weekly, and monthly operational reporting. Performance & Operational Support Achieve individual recovery targets and agreed performance standards. Maintain a high recovery success rate while controlling unnecessary operational costs. Support the Repossession Lead in reducing the outstanding repossession backlog. Identify recurring recovery challenges and report them to the supervisor. Provide field intelligence on customer locations, operational risks, recovery challenges, and emerging trends. Support initiatives aimed at improving recovery turnaround time, asset utilization, and operational efficiency. Perform any other duties reasonably assigned by the Repossession Lead or Incident Response Manager. Key Performance Indicators Performance will be evaluated based on: The number and success rate of motorcycles recovered. Recovery turnaround time. Number and value of outstanding assigned cases. Percentage of successful voluntary motorcycle returns. Response and resolution time for assigned field incidents. Number of motorcycles recovered from police stations, impound yards, NTSA facilities, and other authorized locations. Accuracy and completeness of recovery and incident documentation. Condition of recovered motorcycles and accessories. Reduction in motorcycle downtime following accidents, impoundment, or recovery. Compliance with repossession, safety, and reporting procedures. Customer and stakeholder handling. Individual productivity and achievement of assigned targets. Requirements Qualifications & Experience A Diploma or Certificate in Business Administration, Logistics, Fleet Management, Security Management, Operations Management, or a related field is an added advantage. Previous experience in repossession, debt collection, field operations, fleet operations, asset recovery, security, logistics, or a related environment. Experience working in a field-based operational role within Nairobi and its environs. Good knowledge of Nairobi roads, estates, and surrounding areas. Experience dealing with customers, police officers, government agencies, or other external stakeholders is an advantage. A Valid motorcycle riding license is an advantage where motorcycle-based field operations are required. Basic computer literacy and ability to use mobile applications, GPS/tracking systems, and operational management platforms. Ability to prepare basic reports and maintain accurate records. Skills & Competencies Strong communication and interpersonal skills. Excellent negotiation and conflict-resolution skills. High level of integrity, honesty, and professionalism. Strong customer-handling skills. Good decision-making and problem-solving ability. Strong attention to detail. Ability to work independently and as part of a team. Good organizational and time-management skills. Ability to work under pressure and meet strict deadlines. Strong situational awareness and risk-management skills. Ability to remain calm and professional in difficult or sensitive situations. Good knowledge of Nairobi and surrounding operational areas. Ability to use GPS, mobile applications, tracking systems, and other operational technology. Working Conditions Predominantly field-based role requiring frequent movement across Nairobi and its environs. Regular visits to customer locations, police stations, county/impound facilities, workshops, company yards, and other recovery locations. May require working outside normal business hours, including early mornings, evenings, weekends, and public holidays, depending on operational requirements. Regular interaction with customers, riders, Control Room personnel, police officers, county enforcement officers, recovery agents, insurance representatives, and other stakeholders. Requires the ability to respond promptly to urgent repossession and fleet-related incidents. Must maintain a professional appearance, conduct, and attitude while representing the organization in the field. Role Requirements The successful candidate must demonstrate: Strong commitment to achieving recovery targets. Willingness to work predominantly in the field. Ability to travel extensively within Nairobi and surrounding areas. Ability to work flexible hours based on operational requirements. High ethical standards and respect for company policies and applicable laws. Ability to handle sensitive customer and asset-recovery matters professionally. Commitment to the safety and security of company assets, customers, colleagues, and other stakeholders. Overall Accountability The Repossession Associate is accountable for the effective, safe, timely, and compliant execution of assigned repossession, recovery, and incident-response activities, while maintaining accurate documentation and protecting the organisation's assets and reputation. The position plays a critical role in supporting the Fleet Operations function by maximizing asset recovery, reducing motorcycle downtime and operational losses, and ensuring recovered assets are returned to the organization in a controlled and properly documented manner. Benefits Comprehensive Medical Cover Electric Bike Provided to support field mobility and work-related operations Growth & Career Development Opportunities as the company and function continue to grow Dynamic, Collaborative & Friendly Start-up Culture Regular Team-Building & Engagement Activities Monthly Birthday Celebrations
