job_description: Kenya Technical monitoring and implementation support for WRA water infrastructure under TWENDE Project Organization International Union for Conservation of Nature Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 15 Sep 2026 Terms of reference for IUCN Consultancy Title: Technical monitoring and implementation support for WRA water infrastructure under TWENDE Project. Objective of the Consultancy This Consultancy Has The Following Objective(s) Specific Objectives The Consultancy Shall Pursue The Following Specific Objectives Undertake an independent technical assessment of all completed and ongoing water infrastructure to determine compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), and applicable engineering standards. Assess the quality, functionality and sustainability of the water infrastructure by evaluating workmanship, structural integrity, operational performance, safety, operation and maintenance arrangements, and compliance with applicable environmental and social safeguard requirements. Identify technical deficiencies, implementation gaps and risks affecting the functionality, safety, durability and sustainability of the infrastructure, and assess whether project resources have been utilised efficiently and delivered value for money. Develop prioritised corrective action plans for each infrastructure, detailing the engineering, operational and management measures required to rectify identified defects, improve performance and ensure long-term functionality and sustainability. Provide independent technical supervision and quality assurance for the implementation of agreed corrective works on existing water infrastructure, ensuring that all remedial works comply with approved engineering standards, technical specifications and contractual requirements. Provide technical oversight and quality assurance during the construction of any new water infrastructure implemented under the TWENDE Project, including review of designs where required, verification of construction quality, materials, workmanship and compliance with approved standards and safeguards. Provide practical recommendations and build capacity of the implementing teams through on-site technical guidance, periodic inspections and final certification of completed corrective and new infrastructure works to ensure they are fit for purpose and capable of delivering sustainable water services. Background And About The Project Project Reference: P02886 Donor Reference: N/A About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples’ organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN/ About The Project The IUCN Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO) implements a diverse portfolio of programmes across twenty-four countries in the Horn of Africa, Eastern Africa, Southern Africa and the Western Indian Ocean. Among these is the Towards Ending Drought Emergencies (TWENDE): Ecosystem-based Adaptation in Kenya's Arid and Semi-Arid Rangelands Project, a five-year initiative financed by the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The project contributes to Kenya's Vision 2030 and the national Ending Drought Emergencies (EDE) strategy by strengthening the resilience of communities, ecosystems and livelihoods to climate change in Kenya's Arid and Semi-Arid Lands (ASALs). The project seeks to reduce the economic impacts of recurrent drought by restoring degraded rangelands, strengthening climate-resilient natural resource management and promoting sustainable investments that enhance ecosystem services and livelihoods. The TWENDE Project is implemented across the Sabarwawa, Mid Tana and Chyulu Hills landscapes, covering eleven counties. These landscapes are characterized by increasing climate variability, land degradation, weak landscape governance, inadequate access to climate information, and limited investment in sustainable natural resource management. To address these challenges, the project is implemented through three complementary components. Component 1 strengthens climate-informed planning and governance for drought resilience through improved climate information, participatory planning and coordinated landscape management. Component 2 supports the restoration and sustainable management of priority rangeland ecosystems and water resources to enhance ecosystem-based adaptation and climate resilience. Component 3 promotes climate-resilient public, private and community investments that improve sustainable natural resource management, livelihoods, market access and financial inclusion. The project is implemented by IUCN as the Green Climate Fund Accredited Entity in partnership with the Government of Kenya and Conservation International (CI). The National Drought Management Authority (NDMA), the State Department for Livestock Development (SDLD) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development, and Conservation International serve as the Executing Entities for Components 1, 2 and 3 respectively. To deliver project interventions, the Executing Entities engage specialized government agencies, service providers, contractors and other technical partners through subsidiary and procurement agreements. Under Component 2, the Water Resources Authority (WRA) as service provider to the State Department for Livestock Development (SDLD) under the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development has implemented a portfolio of climate-resilient water infrastructure interventions, including water pans, sand dams, spring protection systems, rainwater harvesting facilities and groundwater monitoring boreholes. These investments are designed to improve access to water for domestic, livestock and ecosystem needs while supporting landscape restoration, groundwater recharge, climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods in the target landscapes. Following the substantial completion of these infrastructure investments, IUCN intends to engage an independent engineering consultancy to undertake a comprehensive technical assessment, quality assurance and compliance audit of the completed and ongoing works. The assignment will independently verify compliance with approved engineering designs, technical specifications, contractual obligations and applicable engineering standards, while assessing construction quality, structural integrity, operational functionality, sustainability and value for money. The findings will provide assurance on the quality and performance of the completed infrastructure, identify any technical deficiencies requiring corrective action, strengthen accountability for project investments, and generate lessons to inform the design and implementation of future climate-resilient water infrastructure programmes. Description Of The Assignment The purpose of this consultancy is to undertake an independent technical assessment of all water infrastructure constructed by WRA under the TWENDE Project to determine whether the completed/ongoing works comply with approved engineering designs, contractual requirements and applicable quality standards. The assignment will evaluate the structural integrity, operational functionality, sustainability and value for money of the investments while identifying defects, risks and corrective measures required to ensure long-term performance and service delivery. Rationale The TWENDE Project has invested substantial financial resources in the development of climate-resilient water infrastructure across the three target landscapes. As the Accredited Entity responsible for fiduciary oversight and quality assurance, IUCN, in its role as accredited entity to GCF, has an obligation to verify that these investments have been implemented in accordance with approved engineering standards, contractual obligations and applicable environmental and social safeguard requirements. This independent assessment will establish whether the completed/ongoing infrastructure meets the required technical standards, is structurally sound, safe and fully operational, and is capable of delivering the intended services throughout its expected design life. The assignment will further evaluate the adequacy of operation and maintenance arrangements, identify technical deficiencies and implementation gaps, assess risks that may compromise sustainability, and determine whether project resources were utilised efficiently and effectively. The findings will provide an evidence base for improving infrastructure quality, strengthening accountability and informing future investments in climate-resilient water infrastructure. The Consultant will also provide practical, prioritized recommendations for addressing identified deficiencies, including corrective and remedial measures required to restore or enhance the functionality of any affected water infrastructure so that it can effectively serve its intended purpose. Scope of the assignment The consultancy shall cover all water infrastructure developed by the Water Resources Authority (WRA) under the TWENDE Project, including 12 water pans, 19 sand dams, 4 spring protection systems and 2 groundwater monitoring/exploratory boreholes across the three landscapes The consultant shall undertake a comprehensive assessment to establish whether the completed infrastructure complies with approved engineering designs, contractual obligations and applicable regulatory and quality standards, and whether the investments are functioning effectively and are sustainable over their intended design life. The assignment shall commence with a detailed review of all relevant project documentation, including engineering designs, technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), contract documents, supervision reports, quality assurance records, laboratory test reports, completion certificates, payment records, environmental approvals, Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs), operation and maintenance manuals, and any approved design variations. Following the document review, the consultant shall undertake field inspections of all completed infrastructure to verify construction quality, structural integrity, workmanship, material quality and compliance with approved designs and specifications. The consultant shall confirm completed quantities through physical measurements and compare the completed works with approved drawings, contract requirements and as-built records. Where necessary, the consultant may apply appropriate engineering tests and assessment techniques to validate the quality and structural performance of the infrastructure. The consultancy shall further assess the operational functionality of each facility by determining whether it is performing as intended, delivering reliable water services and meeting the needs of the targeted beneficiaries. The assessment shall also evaluate infrastructure safety, accessibility, operational efficiency and any defects or operational constraints that may affect long-term performance. The consultant shall evaluate the sustainability of the investments by assessing the adequacy of operation and maintenance arrangements, institutional and community management structures, financing mechanisms for maintenance, environmental sustainability measures and the capacity of responsible institutions to manage the infrastructure throughout its expected service life. As part of the assignment, the consultant shall engage key stakeholders, including IUCN, WRA, respective County Government department of Water, Water Resource Users Associations (WRUAs), supervising engineers and beneficiary communities, to validate technical findings, gather operational information and document lessons learned. The assignment shall conclude with a comprehensive analysis of findings, identification of technical defects and implementation gaps, assessment of value for money, and preparation of practical recommendations to improve the quality, sustainability and long-term performance of climate-resilient water infrastructure investments. Methodology The consultant shall propose a robust methodology demonstrating how the assignment will be undertaken. At a minimum, the methodology shall combine document review, field inspections, engineering measurements, technical compliance verification, stakeholder consultations and comparative analysis of approved designs against completed works. The consultant shall employ appropriate engineering assessment techniques, including non-destructive testing where necessary, supported by geo-referenced photographs, GPS data and drone surveys where applicable. The methodology shall include a clear quality assurance framework outlining procedures for data collection, verification, analysis and reporting to ensure that the assessment findings are technically sound, objective and evidence based. Proposal Format: To ensure a focused evaluation, the Technical Proposal must not exceed 15 pages (excluding annexes such as CVs, company profiles, and the financial proposal). The technical proposal must include: Understanding of the ToR. Detailed Methodology and technical approach. Work plan and delivery schedule. Team composition and task allocation. Duration of the Assignment The assignment is expected to be completed within thirty (30) calendar days from the date of contract signing, including submission of all reports and incorporation of comments from IUCN. Deliverables The consultant will provide the following deliverables and carry out the following activities: Deliverable/Activity 6/10/2026 Inception report Outlining the assignment methodology, work plan, inspection framework, quality assurance approach, and data collection tools. 22/10/2026 Draft technical assessment report Presenting findings from the document review, field inspections, compliance assessment, functionality assessment, sustainability analysis, value-for-money assessment, and identified technical risks. 22/10/2026 Infrastructure defects and corrective action register Detailing identified defects, non-compliance issues, risk ratings, recommended corrective measures, estimated level of effort, and proposed implementation priorities for each water infrastructure facility. 22/10/2026 Technical supervision and quality assurance reports Documenting the consultant's oversight of corrective works on existing infrastructure and the construction of any new water infrastructure, including verification of compliance with approved designs, technical specifications, engineering standards, and quality requirements. These reports may be submitted periodically or upon completion of each supervision assignment, as agreed with IUCN. 22/10/2026 Geo-referenced water infrastructure database Containing GPS coordinates, geo-tagged photographs, inspection records, and other relevant spatial information collected during the field assessments and supervision visits. 26/10/2026 Final technical assessment and supervision report Incorporating comments from IUCN and other stakeholders, summarising the assessment findings, corrective actions undertaken, quality assurance results, lessons learned, and recommendations for improving the planning, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of climate-resilient water infrastructure. Payment Schedule The Timetable below summarises the chronological order of deliverables and indicates milestones at which IUCN will pay the Consultant. Deliverable and Milestone payment Inception report- 20% Draft technical assessment report- 60% 20% Infrastructure defects and corrective action register Technical supervision and quality assurance reports Geo-referenced water infrastructure database Final technical assessment and supervision report Skills And Experience Team Composition and Qualifications Position, Minimum Qualification And Minimum Experience The assignment shall be undertaken by a competent consultant with demonstrated experience in engineering assessment, construction quality assurance and water infrastructure development. At a minimum, the proposed team shall comprise the following key experts: Team Leader / Senior Civil or Water Engineer Master’s degree in civil or water engineering and registered Professional Engineer 10 years Water Resources Engineer Bachelor’s degree in civil or water engineering 7 years Qualifications Of The Consulting Firm The consulting firm shall demonstrate substantial experience in engineering consultancy, construction supervision and technical assessment of water infrastructure projects. The firm shall have proven expertise in engineering quality assurance, compliance audits and technical inspections of donor-funded infrastructure projects, preferably within the water, natural resources or climate resilience sectors. The firm shall demonstrate successful completion of at least five comparable assignments within the last ten years involving technical assessment, quality assurance or supervision of water infrastructure projects. Experience working with government institutions, development partners and international organizations will be an added advantage. Supervision and Coordination The consultant shall report directly to the TWENDE Chief of Party and work closely with the IUCN technical team throughout the assignment. Coordination with SDLD, WRA, County Governments and other relevant stakeholders shall be undertaken as necessary to facilitate access to project sites and technical documentation. All reports shall be submitted in both editable (Word, Excel) and PDF formats. Spatial data, maps and other geo-referenced information shall be provided in GIS-compatible formats, while all photographs shall be submitted in high-resolution digital format. job_title: Senior Research Officer for Sudan, based in Nairobi
job_description: Kenya Senior Research Officer for Sudan, based in Nairobi Organization IMPACT Initiatives Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 30 Sep 2026 BACKGROUND ON IMPACT Created in 2010, IMPACT is a Geneva-based NGO and the largest independent data provider in contexts of crisis. IMPACT aims to support a range of stakeholders in making better, more informed decisions in humanitarian, stabilization, and development settings. Through our team of assessment, data, geospatial, and thematic specialists, IMPACT promotes the design of people-centred research and set standards for collecting and analysing rigorous, high quality data in complex environments. Over the past 15 years, IMPACT has been growing in size and geographic reach to become one of the largest humanitarian research agencies in the humanitarian sector. IMPACT's teams implement assessment, monitoring, evaluation, and organisational capacity-building programmes in direct partnership with aid actors. IMPACT's team is composed of over 200 full-time international experts as well as a roster of consultants, who are currently implementing over 50 programmes in over 30 countries across Africa, Middle East and North Africa, Central and South-east Asia, and Eastern Europe. We are currently looking for a Senior Research Officer to support our Sudan country team, currently based in Nairobi, Kenya Position: Senior Research Officer Cash and Markets Contract duration : 6 months Starting Date : ASAP Location : Nairobi, Kenya. COUNTRY PROFILE Clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) erupted in Khartoum on 15 April 2023 and spread quickly across the country. Civilians have fled areas affected by fighting in large numbers, including to Chad, Egypt and South Sudan. Prices of food, fuel and other basic goods have skyrocketed skyrocketing, making critical goods unaffordable for many people. Half of Sudan’s population are in need of humanitarian assistance, and the country is on the verge of a catastrophic hunger crisis. Humanitarian organizations are racing to respond to the most pressing needs wherever and whenever feasible, with access issues complicating the ability of actors to respond. In this fast-evolving context, IMPACT Initiatives is working to inform the emergency response to enable effective prioritization with scarce resources. POSITION PROFILE Under the line management of the Research Manager for the Inter-Cluster Unit, the Senior Research Officer will take responsibility for all Cash workstreams, including overall responsibility for the Joint Market Monitoring Initiative (JMMI) research cycle which records prices and stock levels across Sudan on a monthly basis, as well as associated analytical pieces based on JMMI data. This involves overseeing two Research Officers responsible for managing the JMMI, representing IMPACT in critical cash coordination fora like the Cash Working Group and Transfer Value Task Force, and independently developing and implementing new analysis based on JMMI data. This position requires strong research skills, a willingness to work in a team, an analytical mind, creativity, and strong independence. Knowledge of the national or regional context in Sudan, as well as fluency in Arabic are considered a strong asset. Candidates should have strong writing and presentation skills and be able to clearly think through and articulate implications of research findings. The position will regularly require looking at data, pulling out relevant findings, writing engaging briefs and factsheets, presenting findings to external audiences with varying amounts of data literacy, and guiding colleagues in how to think more analytically about their own research. BACKGROUND ON CASH AND MARKET ASSESSMENTS In recent decades, humanitarian action has moved towards giving aid in the form of cash or voucher assistance (CVA) issued directly to beneficiaries. This gives beneficiaries a choice in how to spend aid money, and it also supports livelihoods, markets, and supply chains within impacted localities. Effective CVA must be backed by informed research on price levels, the availability of goods, and the resilience of supply chains across different localities. Responsibilities The Senior Research Officer’s responsibilities include: RESEARCH CYCLE MANAGEMENT Take overall accountability for the robust and timely implementation of the JMMI research cycle Manage additional research cycles based on JMMI data end-to-end, including development of objectives, research design and analysis. Manage timelines and deliverables aligning outputs with partners programmatic objectives Research And Technical Skills Independently develop analysis based on JMMI and additional secondary data sources relevant to the context and supporting humanitarian programming Oversee the development of the JMMI and provide technical guidance on needed adjustments Produce high quality research outputs in English. EXTERNAL ENGAGEMENT Represent IMPACT on all cash-related platforms, including the Cash Working Group, Collective Sudan (CCS), Markets in Crisis Group and others, as well as regular engagement with senior stakeholders involved in cash programming, including WFP, IFPRI, CHC, Rift Valley Institute and others Provide technical advice to external partners such as the Transfer Value Working Group based on JMMI data Develop an understanding of key information gaps based on feedback from partners to develop new analysis products accordingly CONTEXTUAL UNDERSTANDING Develop an understanding of price and market dynamics across different regions in Sudan Keep up to date with conflict dynamics STAFF MANAGEMENT AND TRAINING Manage two Research Officers who are responsible for liaising with partner organisations who carry out data collection, supporting data cleaning, analysing findings, and crafting outputs such as factsheets and written reports Promote capacity building across the IMPACT Sudan mission related to deepening analytical capacities using existing research (capacity building portfolio will depend on level of experience). INTERNAL COORDINATION Interact autonomously with HQ departments and possibly serving as a mission focal point for particular themes or technical areas; Coordinate with research units and teams to move forward or improve aspects of the research cycle; Supporting senior management with designing, planning, and implementing strategies, and objectives. The Senior Research Officer will maintain the strictest confidentiality on all data collected and related processes. They will actively take measures to prevent the unauthorized sharing of any information and data belonging to IMPACT and its partners, or collected during their assignment with IMPACT. Requirements Academic qualifications Excellent academic qualifications are required. A master’s degree or equivalent in a relevant discipline (e.g. international studies, development, humanitarian response, data science, political science, etc.) is an asset. Years of work experience At least 3-5 years of relevant working experience in a humanitarian setting or equivalent, which could include assessments, monitoring and evaluation, research design and analysis. Research skills Excellent quantitative and qualitative research data analysis experience is required. Thematic experience in cash and markets in emergencies Proven track record of engaging in cash and markets work in contexts of crises with a deep understanding of concepts such as the MEB, Transfer Values, regional price fluctuations and impacts on the response Communication/reporting skills Excellent verbal and written communication and drafting skills in English for effective reporting are required. Software skills Proven knowledge of the Microsoft Office Suite, to include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. Familiarity with R, SPSS and/or STATA or other statistical analysis software is an asset Familiarity with aid system Good understanding of the aid system and the research community. Prior experience with humanitarian coordination forums is an asset. Thematic experience Prior experience with Cash and Markets, particularly with the JMMI is an asset. Experience in geographical region Past experience in the region is desirable; knowledge of the national context in Sudan would be a significant asset. Language skills Fluency in English required, competency in Arabic is a significant asset. Compensation & Benefits For this position, salary between 2’580 CHF and 2’640 CHF monthly (before income tax), etc as well as a monthly living allowance of 300 USD NB - IMPACT salaries are strictly determined by our salary grid depending on the grade of the position and the level of education of staff. A location-dependent security and/or isolation adjustment is then applied as a recognition that some staff are required to work in difficult places where living and working conditions are much more difficult than elsewhere. Accommodation and food provided in the guesthouse. Enrolment in Swiss private pension fund (Swisslife – approx. 9.975% of staff gross salary), health insurance, life insurance and repatriation assistance. Flight tickets every 6 months & visa fees covered (in-country travel costs and professional expenses are fully covered). Contribution to the luggage transportation: between 20 and 100 kgs, depending on the length of the contract (+ luggage and personal property insurance) Annual leave of 36 days per year. Public holidays of the country of assignment. Family/compassionate leave when applicable. Predeparture induction - 3 days at IMPACT Initiatives’s HQ in Geneva + one week pre-departure training in ACTED HQ in Paris, including a 4-days in situ security training; IMPACT prioritizes the psychological safety of its staff and the health insurance provided covers, among others, up to 1000 € per year of psychosocial counselling fees. job_description: Kenya Request for Proposal- conduct an Economic Benefits Analysis of Regenerative Farming transition among Smallholder Farmers in Kirinyaga County, Kenya Organization Aga Khan Foundation Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 23 Sep 2026 About Aga Khan Foundation (akf) The Aga Khan Foundation (AKF), established by His Highness the Aga Khan in Switzerland in 1967, is an agency of the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). In Kenya, since 1974, AKF works with partners to improve the quality of life by promoting and developing innovative solutions to development challenges. AKF responds to local priorities by developing and implementing effective programming, measuring, and documenting results, and sharing its lessons with governments, donors, and development actors to influence policy and practice. Programme Overview The Aga Khan Foundation is implementing MAENDELEO, a Regenerative Farming Initiative in Kirinyaga County. aimed at improving smallholder farmers livelihoods. The initiative focuses on capacity strengthening of farmers in regenerative farming practices through farmer field schools and on-farm support. The overall principle is to co-develop with smallholder farmers simple solutions (aka SIIIMs: Small Integrated Innovative & Impactful Modules), that are accessible to farmers easy to adopt regenerative practices. The overall goal is to strengthen climate-resilient livelihoods, sustainable food systems, and improved nutrition among smallholder farming households through regenerative agriculture in target counties in Kenya. The specific objectives of the programme includes: Objective 1: Increase smallholder farmers productivity, income, and autonomy Objective 2: Reduce smallholder farmers operating costs and labour Objective 3: Strengthen smallholder farmers socioeconomic and climate resilience Objective 4: Improve smallholder farmer household food security and nutrition Objective 5: Restore farm natural capital (soil, water, air, biodiversity) PURPOSE OF THE CONSULTANCY The purpose of this consultancy is to assess and quantify the economic benefits, costs, returns, and livelihood impacts associated with the adoption of regenerative farming practices promoted under the initiative in Kirinyaga County. The study will generate robust evidence on the economic viability and sustainability of regenerative agriculture interventions and provide actionable recommendations for programme improvement, scaling, investment prioritization, influence policy and practice. Specifically, the Foundation intends to assess whether adoption of regenerative farming practices contributes to improved farm productivity, reduced production costs, increased profitability, improved household incomes, enhanced resilience to climate variability, and broader socio-economic benefits for farming households and communities. To support evidence-based programming and scaling of regenerative agriculture approaches, the Foundation seeks to engage a qualified consultant or consulting firm to undertake a comprehensive Economic Benefits Analysis of the initiative among target farmers in Kirinyaga County. OBJECTIVES OF THE CONSULTANCY Overall objective of the consultancy To conduct a comprehensive economic benefits analysis of the regenerative farming initiative among target farmers in Kirinyaga County. The evaluation will adopt the before and after evaluation design where the adopting farmers will be required to recall the pre-adoption status and compared with non-participating farmers. Specific objectives of the consultancy. The Consultant Shall Assess the extent and level of adoption of regenerative farming practices among participating farmers. Analyze changes in: Agricultural productivity and yields of the main crops and horticulture produce being grown; Farm input costs with breakup in fertilizer, pesticide, seed and labor costs Household agricultural net income; Farm profitability and gross margins; Household food security and dietary diversity; Climate resilience and risk reduction. Assess farmers’ perceptions of economic gains, risks, barriers, and incentives associated with regenerative farming. Identify gender, youth, and socio-economic dimensions influencing economic outcomes and adoption patterns. Generate lessons, recommendations, and strategic insights for scaling regenerative agriculture programming in Kenya. SCOPE OF WORK The consultancy shall cover target farmers participating and non-target farmers in the regenerative farming initiative within selected wards/communities in Kirinyaga County. The consultant will be expected to: Review programme documents, data, training materials, monitoring reports, and existing assessments; Design an appropriate analytical framework and methodology; Undertake quantitative and qualitative data collection; Conduct household economic analysis; Analyse production, profitability, labour, and market linkages Assess environmental-economic linkages where relevant; Produce high-quality analytical report KEY EVALUATION QUESTIONS The Analysis Should Respond To The Following Indicative Questions Farm location: Total farm size and whether owned or rented Household size / number of people live and depend on the farm. Five main crops of the farm and current hectarage Type and number of livestock (cattle, goats, sheep, poultry, bees, fish, etc) When the farmer started the regenerative transition in their farm (month, year). Which factors have convinced the farmer to adopt regenerative farming. What regenerative farming practices the farmer has adopted. Whether the farmer was using synthetic chemical fertilizers before the MAENDELEO Initiative. Whether the farmer was using synthetic chemical pesticides before the MAENDELEO Initiative. Whether farmer is still using synthetic chemical fertilizers. Whether farmer is still using synthetic chemical pesticides. Whether the farmer is considering going back to synthetic chemical inputs. Ranking in order of importance at least any five main benefits experienced from the transition to regenerative farming. Key challenges faced in adopting regenerative farming. METHODOLOGY The consultant is expected to propose a rigorous mixed-methods approach, including but not limited to: Desk review, Household surveys, Key informant interviews, Focus group discussions, cost-benefit analysis, gross margin analysis, enterprise budgeting, comparative analysis, case studies, and farmer success stories. The Methodology Should Incorporate Gender-sensitive and inclusive approaches; Participatory methods; Appropriate sampling strategies; Ethical data collection standards; Data quality assurance mechanisms. The Consultant Should Clearly Indicate Sample size determination Sampling procedures; Analytical tools and software; Limitations and mitigation measures. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES The consultant shall provide the following deliverables within the specified timelines: No Deliverable Description Timeline 1 Inception Report Detailed methodology, work plan, sampling framework, tools, and 1 week analytical approach 2 Data Collection Tools Survey questionnaires, interview guides, and data collection protocols 2 weeks 3 Draft Report Preliminary findings, analysis, and recommendations 6 weeks 4 Validation Workshop Presentation of findings to stakeholders 7 weeks 5 Final Report with power Revised final report incorporating stakeholder feedback 8 weeks point presentation Clean Dataset and Raw and cleaned data, codebooks, analytical models Upon completion Analysis Files EXPECTED CONTENTS OF THE FINAL REPORT The Structure Of The Final Report Should Include Executive summary Introduction and background Design and Methodology Study objectives Study sample and sample determination. Data collection procedures Data Analysis procedures Findings Socio-economic profile of farmers Adoption of regenerative farming practices Economic and livelihood analysis Gender and inclusion analysis Resilience and sustainability outcomes Summary of key findings and lessons learned Conclusions Recommendations Annexes DURATION OF THE ASSIGNMENT The assignment is expected to be completed within a period of eight (8) weeks from the date of contract signing. Consultant Qualifications And Experience The consultant or consulting firm should possess the following qualifications: Lead Consultant Advanced degree in Agricultural Economics, Development Economics, Agribusiness, Rural Development, Environmental Economics, or related field; At least 7 years of demonstrated experience conducting agricultural economic analyses, impact evaluations, or cost-benefit studies; Strong expertise in regenerative agriculture, climate-smart agriculture, agroecology, or rural livelihoods; Proven experience in quantitative and qualitative research methodologies; Experience working with donor-funded agricultural programmes; Strong analytical, report writing, and presentation skills; Experience working in Kenya, preferably in smallholder agricultural systems. Additional Desirable Attributes Knowledge of Kirinyaga County agricultural systems; Gender-responsive research expertise; Data analysis proficiency using software such as STATA, SPSS, R, or similar; Excellent stakeholder engagement and facilitation skills. REPORTING AND MANAGEMENT The consultant will report to the Programme Director at the Aga Khan Foundation, Kenya. The Foundation Will Provide relevant programme documentation; Facilitate introductions to stakeholders and communities; Recruitment and management of enumerators; Support logistical coordination where necessary. The Consultant Will Be Responsible For Training of enumerators Field data collection logistics; Data quality assurance; Ethical compliance; Timely delivery of outputs. job_title: Consultancy for Monitoring and Implementation Support for Institutional Strengthening of Community Rangeland Governance Structures Under the TWENDE
job_description: Kenya Consultancy for Monitoring and Implementation Support for Institutional Strengthening of Community Rangeland Governance Structures Under the TWENDE Organization International Union for Conservation of Nature Posted 8 Sep 2026 Closing date 17 Sep 2026 Terms of reference for IUCN Consultancy Title: Consultancy for Monitoring and Implementation Support for Institutional Strengthening of Community Rangeland Governance Structures Under the TWENDE Objective of the Consultancy This Consultancy Has The Following Objective(s) Specific Objectives The Consultancy Shall Pursue The Following Specific Objectives Assess the functionality and effectiveness of community rangeland governance institutions established under TWENDE and their contribution to improved resource management, sustainable grazing management, reduced livestock pressure on rangelands, restoration of degraded landscapes and reduced natural resource conflicts. Identify opportunities for integrating existing community rangeland governance structures into relevant county governance structures and systems, with a view to strengthening their institutional recognition, continuity and sustainability beyond the project period. Identify opportunities for ensuring that priorities emerging from community rangeland and restoration plans are reflected in county planning and budgeting processes, including relevant Annual Development Plans (ADPs), pre-County Integrated Development Plans (pre-CIDPs) and other appropriate county planning instruments and processes. Assess the key barriers to pastoralists' access to and use of climate information and identify innovative opportunities for improving accessibility and uptake, including through digital delivery mechanisms. Identify strategic opportunities for policy influencing within the next 12 months, with particular emphasis on integrating TWENDE-generated community plans, evidence and lessons into relevant county and national policies, strategies and planning processes related to rangeland governance, restoration and drought resilience. Document the actual and/or expected impact of governance interventions on resource management and conflict reduction, capturing evidence of change as well as plausible expected impacts where measurable outcomes are not yet fully realised. Provide prioritised recommendations and strategic actions that can be pursued during the remaining project period to strengthen the impact, institutionalisation and sustainability of TWENDE investments. Background And About The Project Project Reference: P02886 Donor Reference:N/A About IUCN IUCN is a membership Union uniquely composed of both government and civil society organisations. It provides public, private and non-governmental organisations with the knowledge and tools that enable human progress, economic development and nature conservation to take place together. Created in 1948, IUCN is now the world’s largest and most diverse environmental network, harnessing the knowledge, resources and reach of more than 1,400 Member organisations and around 15,000 experts. It is a leading provider of conservation data, assessments and analysis. Its broad membership enables IUCN to fill the role of incubator and trusted repository of best practices, tools and international standards. IUCN provides a neutral space in which diverse stakeholders including governments, NGOs, scientists, businesses, local communities, indigenous peoples’ organisations and others can work together to forge and implement solutions to environmental challenges and achieve sustainable development. Working with many partners and supporters, IUCN implements a large and diverse portfolio of conservation projects worldwide. Combining the latest science with the traditional knowledge of local communities, these projects work to reverse habitat loss, restore ecosystems and improve people’s well-being. www.iucn.org https://twitter.com/IUCN/ About The Project The IUCN Eastern and Southern Africa Regional Office (ESARO) implements the Towards Ending Drought Emergencies (TWENDE): Ecosystem-based Adaptation in Kenya's Arid and Semi-Arid Rangelands Project, a five-year initiative supported by the Green Climate Fund (GCF). The project contributes to Kenya's Vision 2030 and the Ending Drought Emergencies (EDE) strategy by strengthening the resilience of ecosystems, livelihoods and communities to climate change across Kenya's arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs). The Project Is Implemented Across The Sabarwawa, Mid Tana And Chyulu Hills Landscapes, Covering Eleven (11) Counties. These Landscapes Face Increasing Climate Variability, Recurrent Drought, Land Degradation, Weak Natural Resource Governance, Resource-use Conflicts And Limited Investment In Sustainable Rangeland Management. To Address These Challenges, TWENDE Is Implemented Through Three Complementary Components Component 1: Climate Change Adapted Planning for Drought Resilience. Component 2: Restoration of Rangeland Landscapes for Ecosystem-based Adaptation. Component 3: Climate-resilient Ecosystem Management Investments. IUCN serves as the GCF Accredited Entity, working in partnership with the Government of Kenya and Conservation International (CI). The National Drought Management Authority (NDMA), the State Department for Livestock Development (SDLD) and Conservation International are the Executing Entities for Components 1, 2 and 3, respectively. Through TWENDE project, significant investments have been made in community-based rangeland governance, participatory rangeland and restoration planning, ecosystem restoration and climate-resilient natural resource management across the target landscapes. These investments have included strengthening community governance structures, supporting rangeland and restoration planning, and strengthening linkages between community institutions and relevant government structures. Description Of The Assignment The purpose of this consultancy is to provide strategic technical and analytical support to NDMA to strengthen the effectiveness, institutional sustainability and policy uptake of TWENDE investments in community rangeland governance and drought resilience. Rationale TWENDE has made significant investments in strengthening community-based rangeland governance through the establishment and strengthening of grazing committees, peace committees and other community governance mechanisms, alongside the development of community rangeland and restoration plans. As the project progresses towards completion, there is a need to assess the extent to which these investments are contributing to improved rangeland governance, sustainable resource management, restoration, drought resilience and conflict reduction. The assignment will generate evidence on the functionality, effectiveness and outcomes of community rangeland governance structures and examine the institutional conditions influencing their continuity, integration and sustainability within relevant county governance systems. CREATES is implemented jointly by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) and UNEP-DHI Centre for Water and Environment through two complementary projects that collectively contribute to a common programme objective. The programme focuses on two transboundary river basins: the Mara Basin, shared between Kenya and Tanzania, and the Sio-Malaba-Malakisi (SMM) Basin, shared between Kenya and Uganda. These basins were selected due to their ecological significance, socio-economic importance, existing transboundary cooperation mechanisms, and the urgent need to strengthen climate-resilient and sustainable water resources management. The programme responds to persistent challenges affecting transboundary water management in Eastern Africa, including inadequate hydrological and environmental data, limited decision-support systems, weak institutional and governance capacities, insufficient cross-border coordination, inadequate financing for transboundary water investments, and low adoption of climate-resilient Nature-based Solutions (NbS). Through strengthening institutional capacity, improving access to decision-support tools and knowledge, enhancing governance arrangements, promoting collaborative water resources management, and supporting investments in climate-resilient water infrastructure and NbS, CREATES aims to contribute to improved water security and resilience across the target basins. The Programme seeks to achieve the following four immediate outcomes: Outcome A1: Water agencies, River Basin Organisations (RBOs), and regional bodies conduct effective climate-resilient transboundary water resources management through improved technical capacity and decision-support tools. Outcome A2: Water agencies, RBOs and regional bodies implement and share improved climate-resilient Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) practices. Outcome B1: Governance arrangements for transboundary water management are strengthened, enabling institutions to effectively deliver on their mandates, operationalise policy and regulatory frameworks, mobilise resources, and support policy dialogue and conflict prevention. Outcome B2: Climate-resilient water infrastructure combined with Nature-based Solutions contributes to inclusive and sustainable water management and economic development within targeted river basins and communities. Description Of The Assignment Purpose The purpose of the baseline assessment is to establish a comprehensive and credible evidence base to inform the implementation, monitoring, adaptive management, learning, and evaluation of the Climate Resilient Eastern African Transboundary Water Management for Environmental Sustainability (CREATES) Programme over its implementation period. The Assessment Will Also Establish Basin-level Baseline Values For The Programme's Impact Indicator On Achievement Of SDG Target 6.5 On Transboundary Water Management Using The Programme-specific SDG 6.5 Transboundary Assessment Methodology. The Assessment Will Calculate The Impact Indicator As The Average Of The Transboundary-related Scores Under SDG 6.5.1 And The SDG 6.5.2 Scores. In addition, the consultancy will assess the feasibility of achieving the programme's targeted 10% improvement in the impact indicator by analysing the performance of each scoring dimension, identifying key drivers, gaps, and constraints, and recommending strategic areas of focus to maximise programme impact and contribute to improved transboundary water management. Results Framework and Indicator Validation Informed by evidence from the data collected during baseline assessment, the consultancy in consultation with CREATES programme team and MEL team shall review and validate the programme Results Framework to ensure that indicators are clearly defined, measurable, practical, and aligned with the programme's intended results. This shall include verification of indicator definitions, measurement methodologies, means of verification, data sources, assumptions, disaggregation requirements, frequency of data collection, and calculation methods. The consultant shall also develop or refine Performance Indicator Reference Sheets (PIRS) for all programme indicators to ensure standardised indicator definitions and measurement. Where necessary, the consultant shall recommend revisions to strengthen the Results Framework while maintaining alignment with the approved programme design. SDG 6.5 Impact Indicator Assessment The consultancy shall establish basin-level baseline values for the programme's impact indicator, Achievement of SDG Target 6.5 on Transboundary Water Management, using the programme-specific methodology derived from the SDG 6.5 monitoring framework. The assessment shall establish baseline scores for each target basin by analysing the transboundary-related dimensions of SDG Indicator 6.5.1 together with the SDG Indicator 6.5.2 scores to generate the overall programme impact baseline. The consultancy shall also assess the feasibility of achieving the programme's targeted 10% improvement by analysing the contributing scoring dimensions, identifying opportunities and constraints, and providing evidence-based recommendations to inform programme implementation, learning, adaptive management, and progress towards the intended impact. Validation of Existing Data and Evidence The consultancy shall review, verify, and validate existing programme data and information generated during programme design and inception. Stakeholder Consultations The consultancy shall undertake inclusive stakeholder consultations involving relevant regional organisations, government institutions, river basin organisations, implementing partners, civil society organisations, local communities, development partners, and other key stakeholders to validate findings, strengthen evidence generation, and ensure ownership of the baseline results. The consultant shall compile, review, validate, and analyse available spatial datasets and generate GIS products that support evidence-based planning, monitoring, and decision-making. Recommendations for Programme Implementation, learning and adaptive management Based on the findings of the assessment, the consultancy shall provide practical, evidence-based recommendations to strengthen programme implementation, indicator measurement, monitoring systems, data quality, target achievement, learning, and adaptive management. The recommendations shall identify priority actions to improve programme performance, enhance data-driven decision-making, strengthen results-based management, and support continuous learning and adaptation throughout programme implementation. The consultant shall also recommend measures to address identified gaps, mitigate potential risks, and enhance the likelihood of achieving the intended programme outcomes and impact. The consultant shall ensure that all personal data are collected, processed, stored, shared, and retained in accordance with the applicable legal requirements and recognised international standards for data protection and confidentiality. The methodology should employ a mixed-methods approach, integrating both quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis techniques to ensure comprehensive, reliable, and triangulated findings. The methodology shall clearly describe the sampling approach, data collection methods and tools, quality assurance and quality control measures, data analysis procedures, and ethical considerations. It should also demonstrate how the consultant will validate the Results Framework and indicator definitions, establish credible baseline values for all programme indicators, assess the SDG 6.5 impact indicator, and ensure that findings are evidence-based, representative, and suitable for informing programme implementation, monitoring, learning, and evaluation. You spend real time where the work happens: the receiving bay, the pick aisle, the rider hub, the customer service desk. Every process here is judged on the floor, and the best specs come from having watched the thing go wrong. You write. Short, clear problem statements and specs that an engineer can build from and an operations lead can challenge. If it cannot be explained on one page, it is not understood yet. You prioritise a backlog and you can say why the thing at the top is at the top. You use AI tools to prototype small internal tools and analyze yourself. Turn data into insight into action quickly, without waiting for a full engineering cycle every time. You make sure the team actually uses what you build. If they do not, it is on you to figure out why. What we are looking for 2 to 4 years of experience in a demanding role. Many of the people who fit this description are developers who have found they care more about whether the right thing gets built than about building it themselves. Others come from operations, data or analytics, consulting, or a start-up where you wore several hats. Technically literate. You can read SQL, sketch a data model, follow an engineering discussion and have an opinion on the trade-offs. You have already been the person who fixed something nobody asked you to fix. A report people came to rely on, a script that removed a manual step, a process you rewrote because the old one kept breaking. We want to hear about it. You know how a product team is meant to work. Problem discovery, solution discovery, then delivery, in that order (Marty Cagan, Inspired). You do not need to have run it end to end yet, but you should recognise the difference between a team that ships features it was handed and a team that finds the problem, tests a few ways to solve it, and only then builds. If you have not read the book, read it before the interview. Curious about why. When a number looks wrong, your instinct is to go and find out, rather than correct it and move on. Comfortable with people who are not like you. A warehouse supervisor, a rider and a backend engineer will all need to trust you, and none of them are impressed by the same things. Commercially aware. You do not need to have owned a P&L, but you should be able to connect a feature to margin, availability, working capital or customer retention, and be curious when you cannot. Decisive with incomplete information. You would rather ship a decent fix this month and correct it than wait for certainty. Low ego. You listen, you ask good questions, and you are willing to be on the floor at 6am when that is where the answer is. What makes people succeed in this job They accept being judged on outcomes. A developer is judged on what they built. A product manager is judged on whether it was the right thing and whether anyone uses it. Some people find that shift liberating and some find it uncomfortable. The first group does well here. They distrust stated requirements. What a user asks for is a clue. The good ones watch the work, ask the second and third question, and often end up building something smaller and more useful than what was requested. They write clearly because they think clearly. Short documents with the problem, the evidence, the proposed change and the number it should move. They say no, and explain it. A backlog with no noes in it is a wish list. Prioritisation is the actual job. They close the loop. They go back after shipping to see whether it worked, and they say so plainly when it did not. They stay close to the floor after they have stopped needing to. The ones who drift into meetings and dashboards lose the feel for the work within a quarter. If you are a developer thinking about this This is a real option for the right engineer, and we want to be straight about what changes. You will write far more than you code. You will spend hours with people who do not care how elegant a solution is, only whether it works on a wet floor at 6am. You will hand your best ideas to other engineers to build, and you will be measured on what they ship. In return you get to decide what gets built, which is the part most engineers wanted all along. What success looks like after a year You own a product area, or a substantial part of one, end to end, and the operations team treats you as the person to call when something in it is not working. You have shipped several things that are used by choice, because they are faster than the workaround. You can point to at least one number you were accountable for and show what you did to move it. Do not apply if You want the plan handed to you. You will get support and a senior product owner to learn from, but nobody is going to write your backlog for you. You want to keep being a developer with a different title. You will prototype, but the production code will be written by your squad. You think product management is about managing people. You will have no direct reports and a great deal of influence, and you will need to earn all of it. You would rather be thorough than moving. We will take a decent fix shipped this month over a perfect one next quarter. You will often decide with about 70% of the information and correct the course later.

job_title: Technical Specialist- Gender and Social Inclusion (GESI) and Advocacy, AIM (Kisii and Kakamega)
job_description: About BRAC International BRAC is an award-winning international non-governmental development organisation, with the vision of a world free from all forms of exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realise their potential. BRAC is a leader in developing and implementing cost-effective, evidence-based programs to assist poor and disadvantaged communities in low-income countries, including in conflict-prone and post-disaster settings. It is an organisation of and for the people of the Global South, pioneering new development and social enterprise approaches to equip communities to achieve prosperity. As well as being the world’s biggest NGO by number of staff and people directly reached, BRAC has regularly been ranked the number one NGO in the world by the Geneva-based NGO Advisor, an independent organisation committed to highlighting innovation, impact and governance in the non-profit sector. BRAC retained the top spot in 2020 among the top 500 NGOs for the fifth consecutive year. BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 by Sir Fazle Hasan Abed. It started its first program outside of Bangladesh in Afghanistan in 2002, and has since reached millions of people in 11 countries in Asia and Africa. BRAC has a holistic approach to development that uses a wide array of programs and social enterprises, including in microfinance, education, health, agriculture, gender and human rights. BRAC believes that every person has inherent potential, and when an enabling environment is created and that potential is unleashed, even the poorest can become agents of positive change in their own lives, for their families and their communities. About The AIM Program The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway. About The AIM Education Pathway The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students. This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems. Job Summary The GESI and Advocacy Coordinator will lead the implementation of advocacy, policy, social empowerment, and community engagement activities, with a strong focus on gender and social inclusion, disability inclusion, SRHR, SGBV, and community engagement which includes mobilization, dialogues, and evidence-based advocacy. The role will strengthen staff capacity through targeted training, technical assistance, and quality control in advocacy, SGBV, and SRHR case management and referral systems. Working directly with AIM programme participants and country-level teams, the coordinator will advance the programme’s advocacy agenda, build the capacity of adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) to advocate for their rights, and support them in identifying and leveraging key advocacy spaces. This work aims to sustain the programme’s long-term impact and foster continued self-advocacy among programme alumni in their communities. Additionally, the role will serve as the in-country knowledge management focal point, ensuring effective documentation, knowledge sharing, and dissemination of best practices to enhance the overall impact and effectiveness of the programme. Key Duties/Responsibilities: The GESI and Advocacy Coordinator will be responsible for the development and delivery of the advocacy and GESI component within the Enabling Environment Strategy of the Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in partnership with BRAC programme. Working closely with the Programme Manager - AIM, the position will do the following: Advocacy engagement Support the Programme Manager in the development, annual work planning, and comprehensive rollout of the AIM programme Enabling Environment / Youth Voices and action modality. Coordinate tailored support and capacity strengthening for programme participants and youth advocates on essential skills, including evidence-based advocacy, negotiation, and effective communications/media engagement. Coordinate the planning and execution of technical assistance for youth advocates in developing and implementing effective advocacy plans and strategies at the grassroots level in collaboration with the Technical Sector Officers (TSO-CMs). Coordinate and provide direct support to national and subnational-level advocacy initiatives, including supporting field teams to organize local workshops and meetings to secure buy-in from government authorities. Support country-level research to facilitate evidence-based advocacy, including contributing to the development and dissemination of policy briefs and IEC fact sheets targeting decision-makers at all levels. Support Programme team to develop policy papers and briefs, advocacy messages, talking points , factsheets, presentations, stakeholder reports, consultation summaries, and knowledge products that effectively communicate evidence and policy recommendations. Monitor emerging policy developments and strategically position BRAC in key national and subnational policy fora by representing the organization where appropriate, facilitating technical leadership engagement, and providing technical direction in the design and delivery of policy and advocacy initiatives across country programmes. Support programme staff in forging and strengthening strategic networks and linkages with key actors including decision makers, existing advocacy networks within the programme areas and link advocacy efforts with national and subnational policy agendas. Ensure programme quality by undertaking periodic visits to programme areas to backstop challenges, participate in periodic reviews and reflections and ensure implementation is on course. Work closely with the program team to institutionalize the Youth Development Committee (YDCs) as platforms for grassroots advocacy and undertake activities to deepen their impact at the community level. Provide support to the Monitoring & Evaluation Manager to assess advocacy outcomes , capture and report on advocacy outcomes, and produce comprehensive progress reports. Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI and SRHR) Lead in enhancing the capacity of regional staff, Technical Sector Officers (TSOs-CM), Programme Assistants, and Mentors in GESI, SGBV, SRHR, disability inclusion, SGBV reporting, and women’s rights advocacy, as well as community mobilization facilitation. Also, ensure YDC member capacity on SGBV and SRH referral systems is built. Leas in service providers mapping and engagement for holistic SGBV response. Lead, champion and take custody of the AIM AGYW social empowerment (life skills) curriculum. Lead the GESI-responsive community engagement technical support planning, coordination, and execution for the country program. This includes collaborating with TSO-CM to analyze implementation issues, assess needs, and develop the overall community program action plan. Coordinate the identification of participants with disabilities during household surveys to ensure disability inclusion and support across programme components. Lead the implementation of SBCC dialogue sessions at the community level, engaging local leaders, religious leaders, cultural leaders, and other duty bearers. Guide community leaders in developing accountability action plans based on commitments made during SBCC dialogues, and take the lead in tracking and following up on these action plans to ensure progress and sustainability. Support the review and dissemination of community mobilization materials promoting positive behavior change towards GE, DI, SGBV and SRHR services. Identify and adapt safe, accessible, and inclusive club spaces, ensuring reasonable accommodations such as disability-friendly modifications, gender-segregated restrooms, dignity kits, and baby-changing stations. Prioritize the needs of marginalized groups, including persons with disabilities, adolescent mothers, and out-of-school girls. Knowledge Management & Reporting Work closely with the Senior Manager - Knowledge Management & Learning (AIM) at the central team to support the knowledge management component at the country level. Coordinate and facilitate regular learning sessions (e.g., reflection meetings, peer-learning forums, workshops) to share insights, surface challenges, and embed a culture of continuous learning across the country team. Work as a knowledge champion and help support process documentation, good practices and success story compilation. Stay up-to-date on the latest research and remain informed on issues such as women’s social and economic development, youth-led advocacy, alumni engagement, group self-governance, and gender equality. Support and coordinate with country-level grants managers, M&E, and Finance teams to ensure timely submission of quality narrative and financial reports quarterly. Support the AIM program manager in the AIM program database management, including updates for pipeline reports, grant stewardship, and prospect research relevant to the AIM programme. Outreach, external engagement, and communications Map and engage key stakeholders to operationalize the Enabling Environment strategy. Lead young women's participation in major events (e.g., International Women’s Day, 16 Days of Activism) to drive advocacy. Identify opportunities and forge strategic partnerships and advocacy networks to advance objectives. Strengthen and manage partnerships with policymakers and government officials to promote priority policy changes and investments. Research and identify high-level national/regional events to share the AIM programme's evidence, lessons, and priorities with key decision-makers and practitioners. Perform other responsibilities, as requested by the Programme Manager. Monitoring and Learning Ensure appropriate, timely, and accurate data collection against agreed GESI disaggregated indicators to enable both internal and external reporting. Work closely with the M&E and knowledge management teams to collate lessons learned and best practices among internal and external stakeholders. Work with the MEL team to identify and incorporate project-suitable accountability mechanisms that are accessible to marginalized groups. Manage and strengthen MIS, program/management data collection, and reporting on implemented activities Safeguarding Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment, and exploitation to achieve the program’s goals on safeguarding implementation. Act as a key source of support, guidance, and expertise on safeguarding to establish a safe working environment. Practice, promote, and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action. Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident occurs, and encourage others to do so. Experience (required): 4 - 6 years’ experience in leading any of the following engagements - advocacy portfolios, GESI portfolios, community mobilization, campaign management, stakeholder management, and/or supporting self-governance transition of youth groups, preferably in social and economic development. A robust understanding of the policy landscape around AGYW’s social and economic development, preferably in the African context. Prior experience in program-related knowledge management processes. Prior experience working with women's and persons with disability groups in advocacy and GESI. Experience in strategic relationship and partnership management. Knowledge, Skills & Competencies: (required) Prior experience in local-level advocacy, including experience with community mobilization and GESI Ability to set up groups, with community support, for self-governance Knowledge of training content and methodologies for youth on advocacy and/or rights and GESI Knowledge of the systemic barriers to girls' and women's social and economic development, particularly in the African context. Good understanding of knowledge management systems Excellent written and communication skills, including the ability to foster productive working relationships with strategic partners and diverse stakeholders, and good facilitation skills Computer-literate and Proficient in MS Office packages Ability to coach and motivate colleagues with key advocacy messaging and skills.
